And the hadiths about the ascension and his ascension to what is above the heavens, and the Lord’s enjoining upon him the five daily prayers at that time, and his vision of the signs that he saw, And Paradise and Hell, and the angels and prophets, in the heavens and the Inhabited House, and the Sidrat al-Muntaha, and other than that, is known.

It is frequently mentioned in hadiths, and this type was not found in other prophets like it. It shows that the fulfillment of the Almighty’s saying: {Those are the messengers We preferred some of them over others - those who spoke to God, and raised some of them in degrees, and We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs, and supported him with the Holy Spirit.} [Al-Baqarah: 253]

The levels that Muhammad raised on the night of the Ascension, and will be raised in the Hereafter in the Praiseworthy Station in which the ancients and the lasts will enjoy him, There is no one else like it. It is in the two Sahih books from the hadith of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of Malik bin Sa’sa’a, and Abu Dhar, and from the narration of Ibn Abbas, And Abu Hibbah Al-Ansari, and others.

Anas narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was brought with Al-Buraq, which is a tall white animal, taller than a donkey and shorter than a mule. He placed his hoof as far as he could see. He said: So I rode him until I came to the Holy House. He said: So I tied it with the ring with which the prophets are tied. He said: Then I entered the mosque and prayed two rak’ahs in it, then I went out, and he came to me. Gabriel had a vessel of wine and a vessel of milk, so I chose milk. Gabriel, peace be upon him, said: You chose the fitrah, then he took us up to heaven. Then Gabriel asked the question: Who are you? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you?

He said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: He was sent to him? He said: He was sent to him. He said: So it was opened for us, and I saw Adam. He welcomed me and prayed well for me. Then he took us up to the second heaven, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, opened the door. It was said: Who are you? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: And he was sent to him? He said: He was sent to him. He said: Then it was opened for us, and I saw my cousin Isa and Yahya bin Zakaria, peace be upon them. They welcomed me and prayed well for me, then he came back with me. To the third heaven, then Gabriel asked for the prayer to be opened, and it was said:
Who are you? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad, may God bless him

He said hello. It was said: He was sent to him? He said: He was sent to him. Then it was opened for us, and behold, I was with Joseph, peace be upon him, and behold, he had been given half of the good deeds. He said: He welcomed me and prayed well for me. Then he took us to The fourth heaven. Then Gabriel asked: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: He was sent to him? He said: He was sent to him. So it was opened for us, and I saw Idris, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and he welcomed me and prayed well for me. God Almighty said: {And We raised him to a high place} [Maryam:

57], Then he ascended us to the fifth heaven, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, asked for the prayer to be opened, and it was said, “Who is this?” He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad

May God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: He was sent to him? He said: He was sent to him. Then it was opened for us, and I saw Aaron, may God bless him and grant him peace. He welcomed me and prayed well for me. Then he took us up to the sixth heaven, so Gabriel opened the door. Peace be upon him, it was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: Was he sent to him? He said: He was sent to him. So it was opened for us, and I found Musa, peace be upon him, and he welcomed me and prayed well for me. Then he ascended with us to the seventh heaven, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, asked for the prayer to be opened, and it was said: Who is this? He said:

Gabriel, it was said: And who is with you? He said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: He was sent to him? He said: He was sent to him. Then it was opened for us, and I saw Abraham, may God bless him and grant him peace, with his back to the Holy House, and he entered it every day. Seventy thousand angels will not return to him. Then he took me to Sidrat al-Muntaha, and behold, its leaves were like the ears of elephants, and behold, its fruit was like a handful. He said: When God’s command overtook her, she did not change, and no one among God’s creation could describe her for her beauty. So God revealed to me

What he inspired, then he made obligatory upon me fifty prayers every day and night, so I went down to Moses, peace be upon him, and he said: What has your Lord made obligatory upon your nation? I said: Fifty prayers. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him for relief. Your nation cannot tolerate that, for I have tested the children of Israel and put them to shame. He said: So I returned to my Lord and said: Lord, lighten the burden for my nation, and He reduced for me five. So I returned to Moses, peace be upon him, and said: Five things were reduced from me. He said: Your nation cannot bear that, so go back to your Lord and ask Him for relief. He said:

I kept going back and forth between my Lord, Blessed and Most High, and Moses, peace be upon him, until he said to me: O Muhammad, they are five prayers every day and night, for each Ten prayers. These are fifty prayers. And whoever intends to do a good deed and does not do it, it will be recorded for him as a good deed. If he does it, ten good deeds will be recorded for him. And whoever intends to do it, it will be recorded for him as a good deed. If he did a bad deed and did not do it, nothing is recorded. If he did it, it is written as one bad deed. He said: So I went down until I reached Musa, peace be upon him, and told him. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him for relief. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Peace and blessings of God be upon him: So I said:
I have returned to my Lord until I am ashamed of Him.” And in a narration, he said: “So I came and he took me to Zamzam, and he explained about

My chest, then it was washed with Zamzam water, then a golden basin filled with wisdom and faith was sent down, and my chest was stuffed with it. And in a narration: an incision from the throat to the lower part of the abdomen. He said about Al-Bayt Al-Ma’mur: “So I said: What is this? He said: A building that God built for His angels, into which seventy thousand angels enter every day, sanctifying God and praising Him, and never returning to Him. In the hadith of Abu Dharr:

“So Gabriel came down and relieved my chest, then washed it with Zamzam water, then brought a golden basin full of wisdom and faith, and emptied it into my chest. Then he closed it, then took me by the hand and took me up to the lowest heaven. When we reached the lowest heaven, Gabriel said to the keeper of the lowest heaven: Open. He said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. He said: Is anyone with you? He said: Yes, with me is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. When we ascended to the sky, behold, there was a man with lions on his right, and lions on his left. He said: Then when he looked to his right, he laughed, and behold, He looked to his left and cried and said:

Welcome to the righteous son and righteous prophet. He said: I said: O Gabriel, who is this? He said: This is Adam, and these lions are on his right, and on his left are the names of his sons, so the people of the right are the people of Paradise.

And the lions to his left are the people of Hell. Al-Zuhri said: Ibn Hazm told me that Ibn Abbas and Abu Hibbah Al-Ansari said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Then he crept up on me until I appeared at a level from which I could hear the squeaking of pens.” And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, he said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the journey, he ended up at Sidra. The end, and it is in the seventh heaven, to it ends what ascends from the earth, and it is caught from it, and to it ends what comes down from it. Above it, then some of it will be seized. He said:
{When He covered the Sidr tree with that which it covered} [An-Najm: 16]

He said: A bed of gold. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was given three things: He was given the five daily prayers, and he was given the endings of Surah THE HEIFER (al-Baqarah), and He will be forgiven whoever does not associate anything with Allah from his immoral nation. And on his authority “in His saying, the Almighty, the Majestic: {And it was near by two bows or nearer” [Al-Najm: 9]. He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel in his form, having six hundred wings. And in the two Sahih books on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When the Quraysh denied me, I stood up in Al-Hijr, and God revealed to me the Holy House, and I began to tell them about its signs, while I was looking at it.” And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “You saw me in Al-Hijr, and the Quraysh You ask me about my journey, and you ask me about things from the Holy House that I did not confirm, so I was distressed like I have never been distressed before. He said: So God raised him up so that I could look at him. They did not ask me about anything except that I informed them of it.” The ascension of a human being with his body to heaven has been confirmed in the command of Christ.

Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, for he ascended to heaven, and will descend to earth, and this is something that Christians and Muslims agree upon. They say: Christ ascended to heaven with his body and soul, as Muslims say, and they say: He will descend to earth. Also, as Muslims say, and as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, told him in authentic hadiths, but many Christians say: He ascended after he was crucified, and that he rose from the grave, and many of the Jews say: He was crucified and did not ascend, and he did not arise from his grave.

As for Muslims and many Christians, they say: He was not crucified, but rather ascended to heaven without being crucified. The Muslims, and the Christians who agree with them, say: He will descend to the earth before the Resurrection, and that his descent is one of the signs of the Hour as The Qur’an and Sunnah indicate this. Many Christians say: His descent will be on the Day of Resurrection, and that He is God who will judge creation. Likewise, Idris ascended to The sky with his body, and likewise according to the People of the Book, Elias ascended to the sky with his body.
And whoever denies the ascension of a body to heaven from among the philosophers, then two things will befall him:
One of them is that a heavy body does not ascend, and this is extremely weak.

The rise of heavy objects into the air is something that has been widely reported in various matters, such as the throne of Bilqis, which was carried from Yemen. To the Levant in a moment, and when Solomon said:

{O eminent ones, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me submitting? - An ifrit from the jinn said, “I will bring it to you before you rise from Your position, and indeed I am strong and trustworthy in it. - The one who has knowledge of the Scripture said, “I will bring it to you before your party returns to you.” When he saw it settled Then he said, “This is from the bounty of my Lord, that He may try me as to whether I am grateful or disbelieve.” And whoever is grateful, he is thankful only for himself, and whoever is disbelievers, then indeed my Lord is All-Sufficient. Generous - He said, “Disgrace her throne. We will see whether she is guided or will she be of those who are not guided” [An-Naml: 38-41].

And like the wind carrying Solomon, peace be upon him, and his army when he was carrying the carpet in the air, while he was sitting on it with his companions, and like Carrying the villages of the people of Lot, then throwing them into the air, and like a journey to the Holy House, where the truthfulness of the Messenger’s information became clear. In this way their answer to their denial of the splitting of the moon appears, for their baptism in it

The sphere does not accept splitting, and the corruption of this has been known by reason and hearing, and it has been repeatedly reported from the prophets that they were informed of the splitting of The heavens, and clarifying the response to these people is that what they prove, that movement must have a direction and a determinant that determines the directions, only indicates The lack of a gender of the determiner does not indicate the need for a specific determiner.

So if it is assumed that he created another determiner behind the determiner, and he violated the first, then what was intended would be achieved, and so is the generality of their evidence. It only indicates something. Absolutely, but they specify it without justification, so they make mistakes in specifying it, as their evidence is the continuity of activity or movement, or its time, for that It does not indicate astronomical movement, and that time is the amount of movement. Rather, it indicates that God created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six Days, as the messengers were told about. Those were not the days in which God created the heavens and the earth. The movement of the sun is due to the same amount of time. He was created in those days.

Indeed, God Almighty has informed that His throne was over the water before He created the heavens and the earth, and He has informed that He created the heavens from Smoke, which is water vapor. If before these observed movements there were other movements of bodies other than these observed bodies, this would not be contradictory. When the mind indicates it.

Many men in our time and other times are carried from place to place in the air, and this is something that has been frequent among us and among those who know. That. Also, it is known that fire and light air are forced to move and fall, while heavy earth and water are forced to move. Then he ascends, and this is what is customary.

The second suspicion: Some philosophers, such as Aristotle and his followers, thought that the spheres do not accept division, and their argument for that is in Extremely weak, for they said: If it were to be split, then the determiner of the spheres, the One who moves them, would move in a straight motion. Straight movement requires an emptiness outside the world, and there is no emptiness there. This argument is invalid from several aspects: among them: it indicates that this is in the highest sphere, not in what is below it, like the sphere of the moon and others. This is what Al-Razi and others answered them with. Among them:

The existence of bodies outside the orbit, like the existence of the orbit in its space, requires a vacuum. And his statement denying the emptiness outside it is like his statement denying the emptiness outside it.

chapters.title: One of the signs of prophecy is that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked for rain and the rain fell due to his supplication
paragraphs: Its space. If emptiness is pure nothingness, then it is absent on both sides. If it is said: It is an existential matter that must be needed in both situations, then the statement by denying it is invalid. Likewise, what they mention about the ancients of the world. The people do not have a single sound, rational piece of evidence that contradicts what the messengers were told about, but it may contradict What some theologians believe is the religion of the Messengers as it has been explained elsewhere.
[Among the signs of prophecy are his prayer for rain, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the rain falling due to his supplication]

The second type: signs of the weather, such as his request for rain, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, his recovery, the clouds’ obedience to him, and the rain falling due to his supplication, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. Peace be upon him. In the two Sahih books, “On the authority of Anas bin Malik that a man entered the mosque on a Friday from a door that was towards the courthouse, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace He was standing and delivering the sermon. He met the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, standing, and then he said: O Messenger of God, the wealth has perished and been cut off. paths, so pray to God to help us. He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, then said:

Oh God, help us, Oh God, help us, Oh God, help us. Anas said: No, by God, we do not see any clouds in the sky or a speck, and the sky is like a glass bottle, and between us and Sila’ there is no house. By the One in whose hand is my soul, he did not put his hands until the clouds raised like mountains, then he did not come down from his pulpit until I saw the rain retreating from His beard. And in another narration: Then a cloud appeared behind him like a shield, and when it reached the middle of the sky, it spread out. Then

It rained. He said: No, by God, we did not see the sun on a Saturday. He said: Then a man entered through that door on the next Friday, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He was standing and delivering the sermon, so he met him standing and said: O Messenger of God, the property has perished and the paths have been cut off, so pray to God to keep it from us. He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, then said: O God, around us and not against us, O God, on the sleeves, the shoulders, and the stomachs. Valleys and tree beds. He said:

He did not point with his hand to a direction, but I looked until I saw the city in the shape of a deep hole, and the valley flowed in a canal for a month, and no one came from it. On the one hand, he informed of goodness.” And from this chapter: God’s victory with the wind about which God said: {O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when armies came to you. So We sent upon them a wind and armies that you did not see, and God is Ever Seeing of what you do.} [Al-Ahzab: 9]

chapters.title: His behavior, peace be upon him, with animals is one of the signs of prophecy
paragraphs: Mujahid said: He means the wind of youth, which was sent upon the parties on the day of the trench until it cupped their pots over their mouths and took off their rugs. And armies that you have not seen: meaning angels. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “I was victorious with youth, and Aad was destroyed with the hornet.” In battles and biographies, there is the story of the parties, and how the wind and the angels were sent upon them, and they were defeated without known fighting.
[His behavior, peace be upon him, regarding animals is one of the signs of prophecy]

The third type: its behavior with regard to animals: humans, jinn, and animals. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Ja’far, who said: “The Messenger of God sent me One day, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, he confided to me a story that I do not tell anyone about. He said: The most beloved thing was that of a target or a wanderer. A palm tree. Then he entered the enclosure of a man from the Ansar, and he saw a camel. When he saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he yearned and his eyes shed tears, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him. He, peace and blessings be upon him, wiped his head and left it at rest. He said: Who is this camel for? Then a young man from the Ansar came and said:

He is mine, O Messenger of God. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Do you not fear God regarding this animal that God has given you? He complained to me that you starve him and train him.” Muslim narrated some of it

Some of it is conditional, and it was narrated by Abu Dawud and others. Ahmad, Al-Darimi, and others narrated on the authority of Jabir, who said: “We went with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from a journey, until when we were pushed to A wall from the walls of Banu al-Najjar. When a camel was inside it, no one would enter the wall without being forced upon it. They mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he came. Until the wall came and called the camel, and it came, placing its blade on the ground, until it pooled between its hands. He said: Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Bring Wrong. So he snatched it and gave it to its owner. He said:
Then he turned to the people and said:

There is nothing between the heavens and the earth that does not know that I am the Messenger of God, except the disobedient jinn and mankind.” Al-Tabarani narrated, on the authority of Jabir, who said: “We set out on the Battle of Dhath al-Riqa’ until, when we were in Harra Waqim, a Bedouin woman presented with her son. To the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she said: O Messenger of God, this is my son, Satan has overpowered me. He said: Bring him closer to me, so I brought him closer. He said: Open his mouth, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spat in it and said: The most despicable enemy of God, and I am the Messenger of God, three times, then he said:

As for your son, there is nothing wrong with him, and nothing that befalls him will come back to him.” He mentioned the story of the two trees until he said: “So we camped in a valley of The valleys of Banu Muharib, and a man from Banu Muharib called Ghawarth bin Al-Harith appeared to him, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was wearing his sword, and he said: O Muhammad, give me this sword of yours. He unsheathed it and handed it to him. He looked at it for an hour, then he went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, who He prevents you

Mona? Then his hand trembled until the sword fell from his hand, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it and said: O Ghawrith, who will prevent you from me? He said: No one. He said: Then we came back, and a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came with a bird’s nest that he was carrying, and in it were chicks. His parents followed him and fell at the hand of the man. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned to those who were with him and said: Are you surprised by his action? This bird and its chicks? He added in one narration:

Your Lord is more merciful to you than this bird and its chicks. Then we returned, until, when we were free and standing, the woman who had come appeared to us. She gave her son a piece of sheep's milk, so she gave it to him, and he said: What has your son done? Did anything happen to him that was happening to him? She said: No, by the One who sent you with the truth, nothing befell him of what was befalling him, and he accepted her gift, then we returned, returning, even when we were At a landing in Al-Harrah, a camel came running, and said: Do you know what this camel said? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: This is a camel that came to me preparing for its master.

He claims that he had been plowing on it for years, until when he became bruised, weak, and old, he wanted to slaughter it. Go with him, O Jabir, to Its owner brought it. I said: I do not know its owner, O Messenger of God. He said: He will guide you to it. He said: So he left before me, hugging me, until he stopped by me in the gathering of Banu Khatma, and I said: Where is the master of this camel? They said: So-and-so, so I came to him and said: Answer the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he went out with me until he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him:

This camel of yours is attacking you. It is claimed that you plowed on it for a long time until you made it bruised, made it weak, and it became old, and then you wanted to slaughter it. He said: By which

He sent you with the truth that this is so. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: With his eyes. He said: Yes, O Messenger of God. So he bought it from him and then set it free in the trees until it reached a pinnacle. Whenever it rose, it mounted on some of the Muhajireen and Ansar. Among their washers was something he gave to him, and he stayed there for a while.” This hadith has evidence. The people of Sahih included from it the story of the two trees, and the story of the one who brandished the sword against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And peace be upon him. The story of the bird was narrated by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, and the story of the boy was mentioned by more than one person.

Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Ali bin Murrah Al-Thaqafi, who said: “Three things I saw from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, While we were walking with him, we passed by a camel that was leaning on it, and when the camel saw it, it ran away and put its calves on the ground, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood on it. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Where is the owner of this camel? Then he came and said: With his eyes. He said: Yes

We plundered it for you, and it belonged to a household who had no livelihood other than it. He said: When you mentioned this about him, he complained of a lot of work and a lack of fodder, so be good to him. And in a narration: They wanted to slaughter him. Then we walked and stopped at a certain place, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Go to these two trees, and say to them: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He, peace and blessings be upon him, says to you: to come together.

So I set out, and I told them that, and each one of them was torn from its roots, and each one descended to its companion, and they turned around. All of them, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fulfilled his need behind them, then when he finished, each one of them returned to its place at his command. A woman brought him a boy of hers who was suffering from a disease, and she said: O Messenger of God, this son of mine has had a disease for seven years, and it takes him every time. Twice on the day, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, spit in it and said: Bring out the enemy of God. I am the Messenger of God.

So he was healed. When we returned, the boy’s mother brought two rams and some gobs of corn. She said: By the One who sent you with the truth, we have never seen anything wrong with him since you. So he took one of the two rams, the one that was caught, and brought back the other ram.”

This story was narrated by Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili, on the authority of Usama bin Zaid, may God be pleased with him, and Al-Hakim narrated it in his Sahih, saying: I traveled with The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I saw something amazing about him, and he mentioned the hadith. In it, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: To the woman, when he expelled Satan from her son, if we return, let us know what he did. It was also narrated by Al-Darimi. Al-Darimi narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “that a woman brought her son to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she said:

O Messenger of God, my son is suffering from madness, and it takes him at our lunch and dinner, and he is malicious against us. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wiped And he laid down his breast, and called, and he bleated, and it came out from his belly like a black puppy, and he was healed. Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi narrated, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: “We were with the Messenger of God.

May God’s prayers and peace be upon him, he was on a journey, and a man entered a bush and took out a red egg from it, and the red color began to spread on the head of the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. Peace be upon him, and his companions, and he said: Which of you did this? Then a man from the people said: I took her egg. He said: Return it as a mercy to her. Al-Hakim narrated in his Sahih about the ship of the servant of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: We sailed on a ship, but the ship broke up. So I mounted one of its planks, and he threw me into a thicket where there was a lion, and no one grazed me except with him.

So I said: O Abu Al-Harith, I am the servant of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He lowered his head and winked with his shoulder. “I am miserable,” but he continued. He would wink at me and show me the way until he put me on the road. When he put me on the road, he hummed, so I thought he was bidding me farewell. Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, on the authority of Aisha, who said: “The family of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a beast when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out. May God bless him and grant him peace. He was intense and played and came and went. When he felt that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had entered, he crouched down and did not tremble. He hated to harm him.”
It was narrated by Abu Nu`aym.

Ahmed also narrated from her, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was with a group of the Muhajireen and Ansar, and a camel came and prostrated to him. Then his companions said: O Messenger of God, animals and trees prostrate to you, so we have more right to prostrate to you. He said: If I were to command anyone to prostrates to anyone. I would have commanded the woman to prostrate to her husband, and if he had commanded her to move from a yellow mountain to a black mountain, and from a It turned black into a white mountain, which she should have done.” Narrated by Ahmad, on the authority of Affan, and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Affan, he said:

Hammad bin Salamah narrated to us, Abi narrated to us, Ali bin Zaid narrated to us, Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Aisha. The story of this camel was narrated by a group. Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, who said: “Except for a wolf that attacked a sheep and took it, and the shepherd sought it and snatched it from him. So he fell down

The wolf was responsible for his sin and said: Don’t you fear God by taking away from me the sustenance that God has given me? He said: How strange, a wolf lying on its tail speaks to me like a human? The wolf said: Shall I not tell you something more amazing than that? Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Yathrib informing people of the news of what had happened previously. He said: Then the shepherd came to drive his sheep until he entered the city, so he moved it to one of its corners, then he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he informed him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that the prayer be called together, then he went out and said to the Bedouins:

He informed them, so he informed them, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He has spoken the truth, and by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the Hour will not come until the wild beasts speak. A human being, and a man speaks to the point of his whip and the shoelace of his sandal, and his thigh tells him what happened to his family after him.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated the end of it, and authenticated it. Al-Bayhaqi said: Its chain of transmission

It is true, and there is evidence from another side. It was narrated by Ahmad, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The shepherd was Jewish, so he converted to Islam. And he said about it: “More astonishing than this is a man in the palm trees between the two deserts, informing you of what happened in the past, and what will happen after you.” And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Anas, he said: “There was panic in Medina, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, borrowed a horse from Abu Talha, and he was gathering harvest. When he returned, He said: We found this horse of yours at sea, and after that he was unable to keep up.

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Salama bin Al-Akwa’ and Sahl bin Saad, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Khaybar, that he sent to Ali While he was blind-eyed, he said: I will give the standard to a man whom God and His Messenger love, and who loves God and His Messenger. God will grant victory over his hands. So he spat in his mouth. His eyes were healed, as if he had never had any pain, and he was given the standard. Ali said: O Messenger of God, shall I fight them until they are like us? He said:

Follow your messengers until you land in their square, then invite them to Islam, and inform them of what is obligatory upon them according to the right of God Almighty. By God, for God to guide one man through you is better for you than red camels.” On the authority of Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, “On the authority of his father, Qatada ibn al-Nu’man, that

His eye was injured on the day of Badr and it dripped down his cheek. They wanted to cut it out, so they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: No. He called him and touched his pupil with his palm, but he did not know which eye was injured, but it was the best of his eyes and one of them. And in a narration: He raised his eye until he placed it in its proper place, then he winked at it with his palm, and said: Oh God, make it beautiful. So he died, and whoever met him does not know which eye was injured.” Narrated by the people of Al-Maghazi.

And his son recited in the presence of Omar bin Abdul Aziz, who was a caliph. Those present approved of him and did not deny him: I am the son of the one whose eye ran down his cheek... 69 It was returned with the hand of the Chosen One whenever he responded. If it had not been known to the Followers, they would not have approved of it, as they only received this from the Companions. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Al-Baraa bin Aazib, he said:

“The Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, sent men from the Ansar to Abu Rafi’ the Jew, and appointed Abdullah bin Atik over them. Abu Rafi’ was in a fortress of his in the land of Hijaz, and when they approached him, he The sun had set, and the people were leaving. Abdullah said to his companions: Sit where you are, for I am going and approaching the gatekeeper so that I may enter. He said: And he approached until he approached the door, and told the story of his killing until

He said, "Then I put the sword in his stomach until he took it in his back. Then I knew that I had killed him, so I opened the doors one by one until I finished." To a point, so I put my leg down and I saw that I had reached the ground, so I fell on a moonlit night and broke my leg, so I bandaged it. With my turban, then I set off until I sat at the door and said: I will not leave until I know whether I killed him or not. When the rooster crowed, the mourner stood up on the fence and said: I mourn Abu Rafi’. He said: So I went to my companions and said: Rescue, rescue. God has killed Abu Rafi’. He said:
So we went to the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and we spoke to him, and he said: Spread your foot. So he spread it out and wiped it as if I had never hurt it.”

And in Al-Bukhari, “On the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ubaid, he said: I saw on Salamah bin Al-Akwa’’s leg traces of a blow, so I said: O Abu Muslim, what is this? The blow? He said: This is an attack that befell me on the Day of Khaybar, and the people said: Salamah was injured. He said: So I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he breathed on him three times. “Blowouts and I have not complained about them until now.” And in Al-Tirmidhi and others, “On the authority of Uthman bin Hunaif, that a blind man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Pray to God Almighty to He will heal me. He said: If you wish, you can be patient, and that is better for you, and if you wish, you may pray to God. He said:

So call him, he said: So he ordered him to perform ablution, so he performed the ablution well, prayed two rak’ahs, and made this supplication: Oh God, I ask you. And I turn to you by your Prophet Muhammad, the Prophet of Mercy, O Muhammad, I turn to you to

chapters.title: Influencing trees and wood is one of the signs of his prophecy, peace be upon him
paragraphs: My Lord, in this need of mine, fulfill it for me. Oh God, make him intercede for me.” In a narration, he said: O Messenger of God, I have no leader, and it has become difficult for me. He mentioned the hadith. Othman said: By God, we did not separate, and our conversation did not last long, until the man entered as if he had never been afflicted. Al-Tirmidhi said: An authentic hadith.
[Influencing trees and wood is one of the signs of his prophecy, peace be upon him]

The third type: its effects on trees and wood. In the two Sahih books, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said: “The mosque was roofed over the trunks of palm trees. Whenever the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon, he would stand on one of the trunks of it. When the pulpit was made and was on it, we heard a voice from that trunk. Like the voice of the tax collector, until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and put his hand on it and it calmed down. And in a narration, the palm tree shouted like a child’s cry. And in the Sahih on the authority of Jabir: “A woman from the Ansar said:

O Messenger of God, should I not make you something to sit on, for I have a carpenter boy? He said: If you wish. So she made a pulpit for him. When it was Friday, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat on the pulpit that had been made for him, and the palm tree on which he was delivering his sermon shouted until It was about to split, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came down and hugged her to him, and she began to moan like the moan of a boy who silences her until she calmed down.

And in Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Jabir, he said: “We walked with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until we descended on Wadi Afiha, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went. May God bless him and grant him peace. He was fulfilling his need, so I followed him with a bowl of water. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked and did not see anything that he could cover himself with. Then, there were two trees on the shore of the valley. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to one of them and took two of its branches and said: I will be guided by it, God willing.

So she led with him like a scratched camel that opposes its leader, until he came to the other tree and took one of its branches, and said: Follow me. Ali, God willing, so she agreed with him in the same way, until he was fair between them, so he reconciled between them, until he combined them, and said: They reunited. Ali - God Almighty willing - so they mourned over him. So I went out to prepare for fear that the Messenger of God would feel

He, may God bless him and grant him peace, was near me and then moved away, so I sat talking to myself, then a moment came to me, and then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was coming. And behold, the two trees separated, and each one of them stood on a stalk,” and he mentioned the hadith.

On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “A man from Bani Amer came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, show me the seal that is between Your shoulders, for I am one of the best of people. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Shall I not show you a sign? He said: Yes. He said: Then he looked at a palm tree. So he said: Leave that grape. Then he started jumping until he stood in front of him, and he said to him: Go back. So he came back.

And in Al-Tirmidhi’s narration: “A Bedouin came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: How do I know that you are a prophet? He said: If I call this stalk of this palm tree, you will bear witness that I am the Messenger of God. He said: Yes. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called her, and he began to descend from the palm tree until it fell to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he said: Go back. Then he returned and the Bedouin converted to Islam.” Al-Darimi narrated, on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, who said:

“We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a journey, and a Bedouin came and when he approached him, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Where do you want? He said: To my family. He said: Is there anything good for you? He said: What is it? He said: You bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. He said: Who can bear witness to what you say? He said: This is the Salamah. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called her while she was on the shore of the valley, and she approached the ground, until she stood before him, so he called her to witness three times. She testified three times that it was as he said, then she returned to her place of resting place, and the Bedouin returned.

To him, he said: If they follow me, I will bring them to you, but if not, I will return and be with you. It was also narrated by Al-Darimi, in which he said: Then the palm tree started jumping between his hands, then he said to it: Go back, and it returned to its place. And in the two Sahihs, on the authority of Maan bin Abdul Rahman, he said: I heard my father saying: I asked Masruq who had given the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, permission to call the jinn on the night before. Did you listen to the Qur’an? He said: Your father - meaning Ibn Masoud - told me that he said: A tree called him to them. In Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Ali, he said:

“I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca, so we went out to some of its outskirts, and not a tree or mountain met him without saying: Peace.” On you, O Messenger of God. Narrated by Al-Hakim in his Sahih. Imam Ahmad narrated, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: “Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, one day, and he was sitting sad. He was covered in blood. Some of the people of Mecca beat him and said to him: What is the matter with you? He said: So he said: These people did it and they did it. Then Gabriel said to him: Would you like me to show you a sign? He said: Yes. Then he looked at a tree beyond the valley, and said: Leave that tree.

So he called her and she started walking until she stood before him. He said: Order her to return to her place. So he said to her: Go back. So she returned until she returned to her place, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is enough for me. It was narrated by Abu Ya`la al-Mawsili in his Musnad.

chapters.title: Chapter on the abundance of water, food, and fruits from the signs of prophecy
paragraphs: [Chapter: Abundance of water, food and fruits are among the signs of prophecy]

The fourth type: water, food, and fruits, which were abundant in blessing beyond the norm. This is a wide section, and we will mention what is available: As for water: In the two Sahih books on the authority of Anas, “The Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, called for water, and a cup of water was brought to him, and he made the people perform ablution. He said: So I guessed between seventy and eighty.” In a narration from him:

The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “went out at some of its exits, and with him were some of his companions. They set off walking, and the time for prayer came, but they did not find anything They perform ablution with it. A man from the people went off and brought a cup containing a little water. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it, performed ablution, and then extended it. His four fingers on the mug, then

He said: Get up and perform ablution. They were seventy or so. It is also narrated on the authority of Anas that “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were at Al-Zawra’ - and the Zawra’ was in Medina at the market and the mosque after it - He called for a cup containing water, put his palm in it and made a spring between his fingers, and all his companions performed ablution.” And in the two Sahihs on the authority of him, he said:

“I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was time for the afternoon prayer. The people searched for ablution but did not find it, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came. He made the salutation and performed ablution, then put his hand in that vessel and ordered the people to perform ablution from it. He said: I saw water springing from under his fingers, until the last of them performed ablution.

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Jabir, he said: “You saw me with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the afternoon prayer had come, and we had no water other than water.” Excrement, so it was put in a vessel, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and put his hand into it, spread his fingers, and said: Come to ablution. And the blessing is from God. I saw water gush out from between his fingers, so the people performed ablution and drank, so I put some of it into my stomach, and I knew that it was a blessing. I said to Jabir: How old were you that day? He said: One thousand and four hundred. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, also on the authority of Jabir, he said:

“The people were thirsty on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a bowl of water in front of him, so he performed ablution, and the people rushed towards him, and he said: What is the matter with you? They said: We do not have water to perform ablution, nor do we drink except what is in your hands. So he put his hand in the bowl and made the water bubble between his fingers like springs, so we drank and performed ablution. I said: How old were you? He said: If we were a hundred thousand, it would be enough for us. We were fifteen hundred.
And in Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Al-Baraa bin Aazib, he said:

“You consider the conquest to be the conquest of Mecca, and the conquest of Mecca was a conquest, and we consider the conquest to be the Bai’at al-Ridwan on the day of Hudaybiyyah. We were with the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, fourteen hundred, and Al-Hudaybiyyah is a well, so we removed it and did not leave a drop in it, and that was conveyed to the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. Peace be upon him, so he came to her and sat on her shoulder, then he called for a vessel of water and performed ablution, then he rinsed his mouth and said supplication, then he poured it into it, so we left it without Then it let us go as long as we and our passengers wanted, and we were one thousand and four hundred, or more than that.”

And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Salama bin Al-Akwa’, he said: “We came to Al-Hudaybiyyah with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we were fourteen. One hundred, or more than that, and it had fifty sheep that could not be irrigated. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat on the pit of Al-Rakiyah, and either called Or he spat into it, saying: Then it boiled, so we gave it to drink and drew water.”

On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for Bilal, and Bilal asked for water, then he came and said: No, by God, I did not find water. He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Is there any harm? So he brought him a bush and he spread his palms on it, and a spring emanated from his hand. He said: Ibn Masoud used to drink while others performed ablution. On the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said: “We invaded or traveled with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we were on that day twelve And two hundred, then the time for prayer came, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Is there any purification among the people?

Then a man came carrying a vessel that had some water in it, and there was no other water among the people, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, poured it into a cup, then He performed ablution and performed it well, then he went away and left the cup, so the people mounted that cup and said: Wipe yourself, wipe yourself away. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: On your messengers. When he heard them say that, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, put his palm in the water and the cup and said: In the name of God.

Then he said: Purify yourself thoroughly. “By the One who tested me with my sight, I saw eyes - springs of water - emerging from between his fingers. He did not remove them until all of you had performed ablution.” Al-Darimi narrated them in his Musnad. And in Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, he said: “We used to consider the verses a blessing, and you considered them a fear. We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on a journey and the water became scarce, so he said: Ask for some leftover water. So they brought us a vessel containing a little water. He put his hand into the vessel, then said: Hail to the blessed ablution, and the blessing is from God.

I saw water springing from between the fingers of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we used to hear the glorification of food as it was being eaten.” Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal, who said: “We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the year of the Battle of Tabuk, and he was collecting The prayer, so he prayed the noon and afternoon prayers together, and the sunset and evening prayers together, until when it was another day he stopped the prayer, then he went out and prayed the noon and afternoon prayers. All together, then he entered and left after that, and prayed the Maghrib and Isha prayers together, then he said:

Tomorrow, God willing, you will come to the Spring of Tabuk, and you will not come to it until the daylight breaks. Whoever of you comes to it shall not touch any of its water. Nothing, until I come. So we came to it, and two men had preceded us to it, and a spring like a snare was bleeding with some water. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked them: Did Have you touched any of its water? They said: Yes. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed them and said to them whatever God wished to say. Then they scooped out the spring with their hands little by little, until Something came together, he said:

The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, washed his hands and face in it, then returned it to it, and the spring overflowed with flowing water, or he said: abundant water, so he watered it. People, then he said: It is about time - O Muadh, if your life is long - that you will see what is here filled with gardens.

And in Sahih Muslim there is a hadith by Jabir which was narrated by Ubadah ibn al-Walid, and the beginning of it was presented in the story of the two trees and their submission, then They separated, and he placed the branch on the two graves, and said at the end: “So we came to the army, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Jabir, He called out loudly. He said: No ablution, no ablution. He said: I said: O Messenger of God, I did not find a drop of water on the knees, and a man from the Ansar was cooling water in the water for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I complained to him, so he said to me: Go to so-and-so and see if there is anything in his accusations? He said:
So I went to him and looked into it, but I did not find anything in it except a drop of disgusting dirt, of which if I were to empty it, he would drink it dry.

So I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I did not find anything in it except a drop of grief, including if I I empty it to drink it dry. He said: Go and bring him to me. So I brought it to him, and he took it in his hand and started saying something, I don’t know what it was, and winking at him with his hand, then he gave it to me, then he said: O Jabir, He called out with kneecaps. So I said: Oh, ungrateful one. So I brought it to be carried and placed it in his hands, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said with his hand in the pot, and he said: Take it, Jabir, and pour it. Ali and say: In the name of God.

So I poured water on him and said: In the name of God. So I saw the water flowing from between his fingers, may God bless him and grant him peace, then the basin gushed and turned until it was full, so he said: O Jabir, call someone. He needed water. He said: So the people came and drew water until they had had enough water. He said: So I said: Is there anyone left who needs it? Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised his hand from the pot and it was full.” And in the two Sahihs, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, he said: “I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on his journey, and we spent the night until...

It was the dawn of our wedding day, and we closed our eyes until the sun rose. The first among us to wake up was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and we did not wake him up. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from his sleep, until he is the one who wakes up. Because we do not know what happened to him in his sleep, then Omar woke up and started saying “Allahu Akbar” until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, woke up, and when he raised He turned his head and saw that the sun had risen. He said: Leave.

So he walked with us until the sun had set, and he descended and led us in the morning prayer. Then a man from among the people withdrew and did not pray with us. When he departed, the Messenger of God said to him: May God’s prayers and peace be upon him: O so-and-so, what prevented you from praying with us? He said: I was in a state of ritual impurity and there was no water. He said to him: You have to go to the plain, for it is enough for you. So he performed tayammum in the desert and prayed, then he hastened me to ride in front of him to ask for water, and we were extremely thirsty. While we were walking, we saw a woman hanging her legs between two tents, so we said to her: Where is the water? She said: Oh, oh, you have no water. So I said:

How much distance is there between your family and the water? She said: A day's and a night's journey. We said: Go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: Who is the Messenger of God? We did not control her at all about her until we set out with her and met the Messenger of God with her.

May God’s prayers and peace be upon him, he asked her, and she told him the same as she told us, and she told him that she had died and had orphaned children. So he ordered it to be cooked and it smelt, so he poured into the two upper ones, then he sent for it to be cooked and we drank while we were forty thirsty men. Until we quenched our thirst, and filled us with every water supply, and filled us with every waterskin and tool, and washed our companion, except that we did not water a camel, and it is almost It was drenched from the water - meaning the two pods - and then he said: Bring what you have. So we gathered some shards and dates for her, and wrapped a bundle for her, and said to her:

Go and feed this to your children, and know that we have not excreted any of your water. When she came to her family, she said: I have met the magician of mankind, or he is a prophet as he claimed, and his matter was one and another. So God Almighty guided that people with that woman, so she converted to Islam and they embraced Islam.”

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Abu Qatada, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, addressed us and said: You will go on your eve and night, and you will come The water will come tomorrow - God willing - so the people set out, no one turning against anyone else. He mentioned the hadith of sleeping in the valley, and said: Then he called for a watering hole in which I was with me. Some water, so he performed ablution from it without ablution, and some water remained in it, then he said: To Abu Qatada: Save your water for us; There will be news for her. Then he said: In the morning the people lost their Prophet. He said: Abu Bakr and Omar:

The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a promise to you that he would not break your promise. The people said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is in your hands, so if you obey Abu Bakr and Omar, you will be guided. He said: So we came to the people when the day extended and everything was hot, and they were saying: O Messenger of God, we have perished due to thirst. He said:

No destruction will befall you. Then he said: Release my burdens for me. He said: He called for the water basin, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, started pouring it and Abu Qatada watered them, and the people no longer saw water in the water. The watering hole, they fell upon it. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Be well in public, all of you will be narrated. He said: So they did so, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, started pouring water, and I gave them water until no one remained except me and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then He poured it, and he said to me: Drink. So I said: I will not drink until the Messenger of God drinks. He said: The one who drinks the people will be the last to drink.

So I drank and the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, drank. He said: The people came to the water, drinking and drinking.” He said: Abdullah bin Rabah: I am narrating this hadith in a mosque.

Al-Jami’: Imran bin Husayn said to me, “Look at how you speak, for I was one of the passengers that night.” I said: You know best. He said: Who are you from? I said: from the Ansar. He said: You are more knowledgeable about your hadith. Imran said: I witnessed that night and I did not feel that anyone had memorized it as I had memorized it. In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, and it was narrated by Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili, on the authority of Al-Bara’ ibn Azib, he said: “We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So we came on a high note. He said: Then six descended, of whom I am the seventh, or seven, of whom I am the eighth. He said:

So a bucket was brought to me, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on the edge of the pail, so we put half of it, or close to two-thirds of it, so I was raised to The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was about to find a watering can to put it in my throat, but I did not find anything. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, immersed himself in water. He placed his hands in it, and said what God wished him to say, so the bucket and what was in it were returned to us. He said:

I saw the last of us being taken out in a dress for fear of drowning. He said: “And she walked.” In the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, and Ibn Majah, a part of it on the authority of Ziyad bin Al-Harith Al-Sada’i said in The end of it: “Then we said: O Prophet of God, we have a well that when it is winter we expand its water, and we gather over it, but when it is summer it becomes scarce.” Its water, so we were divided into waters around us, and we have submitted, and everyone around us is an enemy, so pray to God in our well that its water can accommodate us. So we will gather together over it and not separate. So he called for seven pebbles, rubbed them in his hand, and called for them, then said:

Take these pebbles, and when you come to the well, throw them one by one, and mention the name of God Almighty. Al-Sada’i said: “So we did what he told us to do, but we were not able to look at its bottom.”

Imam Ahmad narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, one morning and there was no water in the army, so he came to him.” A man said: O Messenger of God, there is no water in the army. He said: Do you have any? He said: Yes. He said: Bring it to me. He said: He brought him a vessel containing a little water. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, put his fingers in the mouth of the vessel and opened his fingers. He said: Then springs burst out from between his fingers, and he ordered Bilal and said: Call out among the people the blessed ablution.

chapters.title: Separating the stories of the abundance of food from the signs of his prophecy, peace be upon him
paragraphs: [Chapter: Stories of plentiful eating among the signs of his prophecy, peace be upon him]

As for plentiful food, it is mentioned in the two Sahih books: “On the authority of Jabir, who said: When the ditch was being dug, I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sitting down, so I retreated to... My wife, so I said to her: Do you have anything? For I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, severe distress. So she brought out for me a bag containing a saa’ of barley, and we have a domesticated animal. He said: So it was slaughtered and ground, and I had my free time, so I cut it whole. Then I turned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she said: Do not disgrace me with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those with him. He said:
So I came and walked with him, and said: O Messenger of God, we

We slaughtered an animal for ourselves, and I ground a sa` of our barley, so come you and let us go with you. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, shouted and said: Oh! People of the Trench: Indeed, Jabir has built a wall for you and greeted you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not go down with your turban, nor You are baking your dough until I come. So I came, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, leading the people, until I came to my wife, and she said: With you and with you. He said: I did what you told me. So I took out some dough for him, so he spat on it and blessed it. Then he went to our lump of dough and spat on it, blessed it, and then said:

Call for me a baker, and she will bake with me, and take my cup from among yours, and do not put it down. And they were a thousand, so I swear by God that they would have eaten until they left it and turned aside, and our wheat would be covered as it is, and our dough would be baked as it is.”

In a narration, “Jaber said: On the day of the ditch we were digging, and a severe calamity occurred, so they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: This is a calamity that was presented. He said: I am coming down. So he stood up with his stomach tied with a stone, and we stayed for three days without tasting anything. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the pick and struck it, and it came back as a dune. Ahil, so I said: O Messenger of God, give me permission to go home, so I said to my wife: I saw from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something about that. Patience, she said:

I have barley and a bunch of goats, so I slaughtered the bunches and ground the barley until we put the meat in the bunch, then I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The dough had broken, and the lump between the dough was almost cooked. So I said: It is my pleasure, so stand up, O Messenger of God, and one or two men. He said: How much is it? So I mentioned it to him, and he said: It is very good. He said: Tell her: Do not remove the twine or the bread from the oven until I come. He said: Get up. Then the Muhajireen and Ansar stood up. When he went to his wife, he said:

Woe to you, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought the Muhajireen and Ansar and those with them until he said: He continued breaking and scooping until they were satisfied. And a remnant remained. He said: Eat this, and calm down, for the people are struck by famine. And in the two Sahih books, “On the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said: Abu Talha said to Umm

Salim: I heard the voice of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, weak and I could tell he was hungry. Do you have anything with you? She said: Yes, so she took out discs of barley, then took her veil and wrapped some of the bread around, then put it under my dress and brought it back to me. With some of it, then she sent me to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: I went with him and found him sitting in the mosque and people were with him, so I got up. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Did Abu Talha send you? I said: Yes. He said: With food? I said: Yes.

Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to those with him: Get up. He said: So he set off, and I set off with them until I came to Abu Talha and informed him. Abu Talha said: O Umm Sulaim, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has come. May God bless the people, and we have nothing to feed them. She said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: So Abu Talha set off until he met the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came with him until he entered, and he said The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Come, Umm Sulaim, what do you have?

So she brought that bread and it was unpacked, and Umm Sulaym squeezed a piece of her own over it and baked it, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about it whatever he wanted. God said, then he said: Give permission to ten, so he gave them permission, and they ate until they were satisfied, then they left. Then he said: give permission.

For ten. So he gave them permission, and they ate until they were satisfied, then they left. Then he said: Give permission for ten. So he gave them permission until all the people had eaten and were satisfied, and the people were seventy or eighty men. Al-Bukhari narrated eighty, and he said in a narration: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Talha, Umm Sulaym, Anas, and Fadl ate. We gave it as a gift to our neighbors. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Salamah, he said: “We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Khaybar, and he ordered us to gather what was in our provisions - Meaning, of dates - so he spread out a piece of bread and we scattered our supplies on it. He said:

So I stretched out, and stretched out, and looked at him, so I leaned on him like a sheep, and we were fourteen hundred. He said: So we ate. Then, I stretched out, and looked at him. So I besieged him like the lamb of a sheep.” And in the two Sahih books on the authority of Abu Hurairah, Abu Sa’id, and Salamah ibn al-Akwa’, and the wording is by Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, he said

“We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a journey. He said: The people ran out of supplies until they were about to slaughter some of their camels. He said: Then Omar said: O Messenger of God, if you gathered what remained of the people’s provisions and prayed to God for them. He said: So he did, and Dhu al-Bir came with his wheat, and Dhu al-Tamar with his dates, and Dhu with the stones with his seeds. It was said: And what did they do with the pits? He said: They suck it and drink water over it. He said: So he called for it until the people filled their supplies, he said: Then he said:

“I bear witness that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God. No servant of God who does not doubt them will meet God with them except that he will enter Paradise.” In another word, he said: “On the day of the Battle of Tabuk, a famine struck the people, and they said: O Messenger of God, if you would grant us permission, we would sacrifice.” We drank, ate, and made oils, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do it. He said: Then Omar came and said: O Messenger of God, if you do that, the afternoon will be less. And in a narration: How long will they remain?

After their camels, but pray for them because of their camels, then pray for blessing for them, perhaps God will provide for that. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes. So he called for a bow and spread it out, then he called for the virtue of their offspring. He said: So he made the man bring a palm of corn, and he made the other bring a palm of dates, and he made the other bring a crumb until they agreed to agree on that. An easy thing. He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, invoked blessings, then said: Take it in your containers. He said: So they took their containers until they did not leave a container in the army without filling it. He said:

So they ate until they were satisfied, and some leftovers remained. Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of Salama bin Al-Akwa’, who said: “We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a campaign, and we were besieged by such hardship that We were about to slaughter some of our backs, so the Prophet of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, commanded us, so we gathered our vessels and spread out a place for him, so Zad gathered. The people are based on obedience. He said:

So I reached out to guess how much it was, so I guessed it like the size of a goat, and we were fourteen hundred. He said: So we ate until we were all satisfied, then We stuffed ourselves, then the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Is there any ablution? He said: Then a man came with a tool containing sperm, so he emptied it into a cup, so we all performed ablution, pouring fourteen hundred cents on it, gurgling it. Then eight came after that, and they said: Is there any purification? Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The ablution has been completed.

And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Jabir, “Umm Malik used to give a gift of ghee to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a plot of hers, and her sons would bring it to her.” So they ask the people, but they have nothing, so she goes back to the one she used to give gifts to the Prophet.

May God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and you find ghee in it. He said: Adam continued to keep her house for her until she squeezed it, so she came to the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and he said: Did you squeeze it? She said: Yes. He said: If you had left it, he would still be standing. Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Jabir as well, who said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking him for food, so he fed him half a measure of barley. The man, his wife, and their guest continued to eat from it, until they ate it. Then he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: If you had not eaten it, you would have eaten it. From him, and he came to you.”

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, married Zainab, and he went in with his family. He said: So my mother, Umm Sulaym, made a living room. So she placed it in a pile of stones and said: O Anas, go.

With this to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So say: My mother sent this to you, and she is greeting you, and saying: This is a little for you from us, O Messenger of God. He said: So I took it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: My mother greets you and says: This is a small thing for you from us. He said: Put it down, then he said: Go and invite so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so, and whomever you meet. And he named some men. He said: So I called whomever he named, and whoever I met. Al-Ja’d - who is the narrator of Anas - said: How many were they? He said:

They were about three hundred, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: O Anas, bring the Taurus. He said: So they entered until the row and the room were filled, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let ten by ten gather around, and let everyone eat. A person from the following. He said: So they ate until they were satisfied. He said: A group left, and a group entered until they had all eaten, and he said: O Anas, remove it. So I removed it, and I do not know whether it was more or less when it was placed. When I rose, he said: And groups of them sat talking. He mentioned the revelation of the verse about the Hijab.

Al-Bukhari narrated, “Also on the authority of Anas: Umm Sulaim took a handful of barley that she had ground, made a handful of it, and squeezed an ikka with her, then You sent me to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so I went to him while he was among his companions, so I called him. He said: Who is with me? So I came and said: He is saying: And who is with me? So Abu Talha came out to him and said: O Messenger of God, it is something that Umm Sulaym had made. So he went in and brought it, and said: Enter ten.

Until he counted forty, then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ate, then he got up and I started to see if anything was missing from it? On the authority of Samurah ibn Jundub, he said: “We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sharing a portion from morning until night. Ten people would get up and sit down.” Ten, so we said: What was extended? He said: What are you surprised by? Whatever it was

It extended from here, and he pointed with his hand to the sky.” It was narrated by Al-Nasa’i and Al-Tirmidhi, who said: It is a hasan and authentic hadith. It was narrated by Al-Darimi and Al-Hakim in his Sahih. And in Bukhari, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he used to say:

“By God, there is no god but Him, if I were to rely on the earth due to hunger, and if I were to tighten a stone on my stomach due to hunger, and I One day I sat on the road from which they were emerging, and Abu Bakr passed by, and I asked him about a verse from the Book of God. I only asked him so that he might follow me, but he did not. He did so, then Omar passed by and I asked him about a verse from the Book of God. I only asked him to follow me, so he passed by and did not do so, then Abu al-Qasim passed by me.

May God’s prayers and peace be upon him. He smiled when he saw me, and he recognized what was on my face and what was in my soul. Then he said: Abu Hurr. I said: At your service, O Messenger of God. He said: The truth, and he went on, so I followed him. He entered and asked permission, so he permitted me. So I entered and he found milk in a cup, so he said: Where did this milk come from? They said: It was given to you by so-and-so, or so-and-so. He said: Abu Hurr. I said: At your command, O Messenger of God. He said: Come to the people of Suffah, so leave them for me. He said:

The people of Suffah are the guests of Islam. They do not come to visit family or money. If an alms comes to him, he sends it to them and does not take any of it. Something, and when a gift came to him, he would send it to them, take some of it, and share it with them. That displeased me, so I said: What is this milk among the people of Adjective? ! I had the right to take this milk as a drink to strengthen myself, so when they came to me, I would give it to them, and whatever they might inform me of... This is the milk, and there was nothing wrong with obedience to God and obedience to His Messenger, so I came to them and invited them, and they accepted, so he gave them permission, and they took Their sittings from home, and he said:

O Abu Hurr, I said: At your service, O Messenger of God. He said: Take it and give it to them. So I took the cup and gave it to the man, so he drank until he had enough, then he returned the cup to me, so I gave him the other, and he drank until he had enough, then He responds to me

The cup and I gave it to the other, and he drank until he quenched his thirst, then he returned the cup to me until I reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people had quenched it. All of them, so he took the cup and put it on his hand, looked at me and smiled, and said: Abu Hurr, I said: At your service, O Messenger of God. He said: You and I stayed. I said: You have spoken the truth, O Messenger of God. He said: Sit, so drink. So I sat, so I drank, and he said: Drink.
