So I drank, and he kept saying: Drink, until I said: No, and by the One who has sent you with the truth, I will not find a path to Him. He said: Show me. So I gave him the cup, and he thanked God, said the supplication, and drank what was left over.”

And in the two Sahih books on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, he said: “We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, thirty and a hundred people, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Peace and blessings of God be upon him: Does any of you have any food? Then a man with a saa’ of food or the like was kneading it, then a tall, wiry man came with a sheep.

He drives it, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: For sale? Or a gift? Or did he say: a gift? He said: Rather, he sold, so he bought a sheep from him and it was cooked, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the black belly to be roasted, and I swear by God what is in the thirty And a hundred, except for those for whom the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, recorded a piece of the blackness of her stomach. If he was a witness, he would give it to him, and if he was absent, he would hide it. For him, he made a bowl of it, so they all ate, and we were satisfied, so the two bowls remained, so we carried them on the camel,” or as he said.

chapters.title: A chapter from the signs of prophecy: multiplying fruits
paragraphs: [Chapter: Among the signs of prophecy is the multiplication of fruits]

As for the abundance of fruits, in Sahih Al-Bukhari, “On the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah that his father was martyred, left behind a debt, and left behind six daughters, so when he attended The palm tree grove said: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: You have learned that my father was martyred on the day of Uhud and left behind a large debt, and I I would love for the lovers to see you. He said: Go and thresh all the dates in one place. So I did, then I called him, and when they looked at him as if they had been deceived by me at that hour, and when he saw what they were doing, he went around three threshing floors around the largest of them. مَرَّاتٍ، ثُمَّ جَلَسَ عَلَيْهِ، ثُمَّ قَالَ لِي:

Invite your friends for me. He continued to measure to them until God fulfilled his trust on my father’s behalf, and I accept that God fulfill his trust on my father’s behalf, and I will not return to my sisters. With a date,

So God saved all the threshing floors, to the point that I look at the threshing floor on which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was as if there was not a single date missing. “One.” And in a narration: “His father left behind thirty wasqs for a Jewish man, so Jabir waited for him, but he refused to see him, so Jabir spoke The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to intercede for him. He came to him and spoke to the Jew to take the dates from his palm trees with what was his. He refused, so the Messenger of God entered. God, may God bless him and grant him peace, picked the palm trees and walked among them, then he said to Jabir, “Give it something for him, so I will repay him.”

After the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he found for him thirty wasqs, and left for him seventeen wasqs, so Jabir came to tell him what He was, and he found him praying the afternoon prayer, and when he left, he told him of the virtue, and said: Tell that to Ibn Al-Khattab. So Jabir went to Omar and told him, and Omar said: I learned when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, walked there to bless them. Imam Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, and others narrated the hadith of Mazoud Abu

Hurairah, Ahmad said, Yunus told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Al-Muhajir, on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: “I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Peace be upon him, with dates, and I said: Pray to God to bless me in them. He said: So he arranged them in his hands. He said: Then he called and said to me: Put them in your jug, so put your hand in and do not scatter them. He said: So I made such-and-such a cup of it for the sake of God, and we would eat and feed ourselves, and it would not leave my loins. When Uthman was killed, my loins were cut off. And he fell.” It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Imran bin Musa Al-Qazzaz, on the authority of Hammad in a similar manner, and he said:

It is a good and strange hadith from this perspective. Al-Hafiz Abd al-Ghani and others narrated it through another path, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was He greeted a group of soldiers, and they were afflicted with a lack of food. He said: “O Abu Hurairah, do you have something?” I said: Some dates in a bowl of mine. He said: Bring them. So I brought the food supply, and he said: Bring some food. So I brought the date and he spread it out, then he put his hand in and grabbed the dates, and it was twenty-one dates. He said: Then he said: In the name of God.

So he started placing each date and naming until he came to the dates, so he said to them like this, then he gathered them together and said: Call so-and-so and his companions, so they ate and were satisfied. They left. Then he said: Call so-and-so and his friends. They ate and were satisfied, and left. He said: There were dates left over. He said: So he said to me: Sit. So I sat down and he ate, and I ate, he said, and some dates remained, so he took them and put them in the water supply, and said: O Abu Hurairah, if you want something, go in.

Your hand is not repaid, and it will be repaid to you. He said: I was not looking for dates until I put my hand in and took fifty wasqs of it for the sake of God Almighty, and it was hanging behind my back, and it fell. Othman's time passed and he left. He narrated it on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Mansour, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “I was afflicted with three things: with the death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, I was his companion and his servants, and after the killing of Othman, and what was provided, we were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he attacked the people. Feasted, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me:

Is there anything, Abu Hurairah? I said: Yes, some dates in a basket. He said: Bring it to me. So I brought it to him, and he put his hand in and took out a fist and spread it out, then he said: Leave for me ten. So they ate until they were satisfied, then he put his hand in and took out a fist and spread it out, then he said: Leave me ten. He continued doing this until he fed the whole army and were satisfied. Then he said: Take what you have brought, and put your hand in and hold, and do not

It's enough for him. He said: Abu Hurairah: So I seized more than what I brought, then Abu Hurairah said: Shall I not tell you about what I ate from? I ate the life of the Messenger of God. May God bless him and grant him peace, and I was fed, and Abu Bakr’s life and I was fed, and Omar’s life and I was fed, and Uthman’s life and I was fed, and when he was killed Othman, my house was looted and the supplies were gone.” Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, on the authority of Ali bin Ubaid, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Qays, on the authority of Dukayn bin Saeed Al-Muzani, who said: “We came We asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forty and four hundred men for food. He said to Omar:
Go and feed them. He said: O Messenger of God, all that remains is

A handful of dates that I see wakes me up. He said: He said: So feed them. He said: Listening and obedience. He said: So Omar took the key out of his wallet, opened the door, and saw something like a group of dates sitting down, and he said to us: Take it. So each man took what he liked, then turned around, and I was one of the last of the people, as if we had never seen a date.” It was narrated by Abu Dawud, on the authority of Abd al-Rahim ibn Mutarrif, on the authority of Issa ibn Yunus, on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Khaled, on the authority of Qais ibn Abi Hazim, on the authority of Dukin, he said: Abu Abdullah Al-Maqdisi: and its chain of transmission is according to the condition of authenticity.

chapters.title: The chapter on harnessing stones for him, peace be upon him, is one of the signs of his prophecy
paragraphs: [Chapter: The subjugation of stones to him, peace be upon him, is one of the signs of his prophecy]

As for the fifth type: His influence on the stones, his control over them, and his subjugation of them to him, it is mentioned in Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Anas, who said: “The Prophet ascended May God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and with him were Abu Bakr, Omar, and Othman. The mountain shook with them, and he said: Be still. He struck him with his foot, and you have no choice but to do so. A prophet, a truthful, and two martyrs.” And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Jabir bin Samra, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “I know of a stone in Mecca who used to greet me before he I am sent, I know him now.” And in Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Ali, he said:

“I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca, and we went out to some of its outskirts. No tree or mountain met him without saying: Peace be upon you. O Messenger of God. It was narrated by Al-Hakim in his Sahih.
In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Salama bin Al-Akwa’, he said:

“We invaded Hunayn with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When we faced the enemy, I went up to him and went up a hill, and a man from the enemy met me. So I shot him with an arrow and he hid from me, so I did not know what he had done. I looked at the people and they had emerged from another corner and met them. And the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away, and he returned defeated, wearing two cloaks, one of which was girded around him. wearing the other, so he released my garment, so I gathered them all together and passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, defeated, while he was riding his mule. The martyrs, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said:
He saw

Ibn Al-Akwa' was terrified. When they cheated, the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, got off the mule, then took a handful of the ground and turned to face their faces, and said: “You have watched.” The faces. Then God did not create any of them except that He filled his eyes with dust with that fist, and they turned away, turning away, but God defeated them. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Al-Abbas bin Abdul-Muttalib, he said:

“I witnessed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hunayn, and I and Abu Sufyan bin Al-Harith bin Abdul Muttalib joined the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. We did not separate from him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on a white mule of his that Farwa bin Nafatha al-Jadami had given him as a gift to him. When the Muslims and the infidels met,

The Muslims turned away, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began running his mule ahead of the infidels. Al-Abbas said: I am holding the reins. The mule of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, encumbered it, and Abu Sufyan was holding the mounts of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanting not to She hastened, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, Abbas, call the people of the tree. By God, it was as if their compassion when they heard my voice was like the compassion of cows for their children. Oh my God, my God. He said: So they fought with the infidels, and the call among the Ansar said:
O people of Ansar, then the invitation was limited to Banu Al-Harith bin Al-Khazraj, and they said: O Banu Al-Harith bin Al-Khazraj. Then the Messenger of God looked

May God’s prayers and peace be upon him, while he was riding his mule like one riding on it to fight them. The Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: This is when he became hot. The intercourse. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took pebbles and threw them in the faces of the infidels, then said: They are defeated, by the Lord of the Kaaba. He said: So I went to look, and behold, the fighting is as it is as I see it. By God, it is not just that he threw his pebbles at them, and I still saw their edge. And He commanded them to turn back until God defeated them, and God Almighty said: Concerning the day of Badr: {And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw} [Al-Anfal: 17] »

Ibn Ishaq narrated, on the authority of a group of them, Urwa, Al-Zuhri, Asim bin Omar, and others, who said: “Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, He and Abu Bakr greeted each other in Al-Arish, and no one else was with them. The people were close to one another, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made He asked his Lord for his promise of help and said: O God, if this group perishes, you will not be worshipped. And Abu Bakr said: After you appeal to your Lord, O Messenger of God, God will fulfill what He promised you of His help.

Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, shook with a heartbeat, then rose up, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Give good news, O Abu Bakr, victory has come to you. God Almighty, this is Gabriel, holding the reins of his horse and leading him, with dust on his shoulders - he says: dust - then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out. He greeted him, mobilized his companions and prepared them, and said: Let not any man among you hasten to fight until we give him permission. If the people attack you - he says:

They approached you - so spread arrows from them, then the people crowded together, and when some of them approached one another, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out. So he took a handful of pebbles and faced the Quraysh with it, and blew their faces with it, and said: The faces became astonished. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said Peace and blessings of God be upon him: Charge against them, O community of Muslims. So the Muslims took charge

And God defeated the Quraysh, killed those of their nobles who were killed, and captured those of them who were captured. In the hadith of Ibn Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Gabriel said to him: Take a handful of dirt. So he took a handful of dust and threw it in their faces. There is not a single person among the polytheists who did not get dust from that dust on his eyes, nostrils, and mouth. grip, so they turned away, turning away.”

chapters.title: A chapter from his signs, may God bless him and grant him peace, God’s support for him through his angels
paragraphs: [Chapter: Among his signs, may God bless him and grant him peace, is God’s support for him with His angels]

The sixth type: Among his signs, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, is God’s support of him with His angels. God Almighty said: {When you sought help from your Lord, and He answered you. Indeed, I will support you with a thousand of the angels following each other} [Al-Anfal: 9] verse. And the Almighty said: {When you said to the believers, “Is it not sufficient for you if your Lord provides you with three thousand angels sent down? Yes, if you are patient. And fear Allah, and they will come to you immediately. This is what your Lord will provide you with five thousand angels appointed in harmony.} [Al Imran: 124], and the Almighty said: The ditch:

{When armies came to you, and We sent upon them a wind and armies which you did not see, and God is ever Seeing of what you do} [Al-Ahzab: 9]. And God Almighty said in Hunayn: {Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down armies which you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved, and that is The reward of the disbelievers} [At-Tawbah: 26]. And God Almighty said in the Hijra: {The second of the two, when they were in the cave, when he said to his companion: Do not be sad. Indeed, God is with us. So God sent down His tranquility. And he supported him with armies that you did not see, and He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, and the word of God the highest.} [At-Tawbah: 40].

And God Almighty said at Badr: {When your Lord revealed to the angels, “Indeed, I am with you, so make firm those who believe. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve” [Al-Anfal: 12]. And in the two Sahih books, and the wording is by Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Omar Ibn Al-Khattab, he said: “When it came on the day of Badr, the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, looked at

He handed over to the polytheists, who were one thousand, and his companions were three hundred and seventeen men, so he received the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Qiblah, then he extended his hands and began to chant to his Lord: “O God, fulfill for me what you promised me, O God, give me what you promised me, O God, if this A group of people of Islam are not to be worshiped on earth.” So he continued to call out to his Lord, extending his hands facing the Qiblah until his cloak fell. On his shoulders, so Abu Bakr came to him, took his cloak, and threw it on his shoulders, then he pulled him behind him and said:
O Prophet of God, stop calling upon your Lord, for He will fulfill for you what He promised you. Then God Almighty revealed:
{When you sought help from your Lord, and He responded to you. Indeed, I will assist you with a thousand of the angels, following one another} [Al-Anfal: 9]
So God provided him with angels.

Abu Zumail said: Ibn Abbas narrated to me, saying: While a man from among the Muslims on that day was fiercely pursuing a man from among the polytheists in front of him, when He heard the crack of a whip above him, and the knight's voice said: Come, Haizum. So he looked at the polytheist in front of him, and he fell down, lying down. He looked at him and saw that his nose had been pierced, and his face had been split open like a stroke with a whip, and that turned green. All in all, then the Ansari came and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrated that and said: “You are right. That is from the extension of the third heaven.” So they were killed. On that day, seventy, and they captured seventy,” he mentioned the hadith.

Al-Bukhari mentioned in this hadith: “Then he came out, meaning the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and he said: ‘The crowd will be defeated and they will turn their backs’ [Al-Qamar: 45].”

Ibn Ishaq said: Abdullah bin Abi Bakr bin Hazm told me on the authority of some of Banu Sa’idah. He said: “I heard Abu Usayd Malik bin Rabi’ah After his sight was damaged, he said: If I were with you at Badr now and had my sight, I would tell you about the people from which the angels emerged. I have no doubt. And I don't mind. When the angels descended and Iblis saw them, and God revealed to them {Indeed, I am with you, so strengthen those who believe} [Al-Anfal: 12]

And their confirmation is that the angels come to a man in the form of a man he knows and say to him: Rejoice, for they are nothing, and God is with you. Repeat. Upon them, when Iblis saw the angels, he turned on his heels and said: “I am disavowed of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see” [Al-Anfal: 48].

It was in the form of a robbery, and Abu Jahl came to exhort his companions and said: Do not be frightened by the abandonment of a robbery, for he is on a date. From Muhammad and his companions. Then he said: By Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, we will not return until we tie Muhammad and his companions to ropes, so do not kill them, but take them by force.

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Saad bin Abi Waqqas, he said: “On the day of Uhud, I saw to the right of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to his left two men wearing clothes. Two white men fighting on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The fighting was intense. I had never seen them before that day or after it. He means Gabriel. And Michael, peace be upon them.”

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Aisha, she said: “Saad was injured on the day of the ditch, and a man from the Quraysh (Ibn al-Irqah) threw him into the water and hit him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set up a tent in the mosque, which he returned from nearby. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from the trench, he put down the weapon. So he washed himself, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him while shaking the dust from his head and said, “You have laid down the weapon, by God, we have not put it down. Go out to them.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Where?

He pointed to the Banu Qurayzah, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought them, and they submitted to the ruling of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, responded. God, may God bless him and grant him peace, conveyed the ruling regarding them to Saad. He said: I rule regarding them that the female fighter be killed, and that the offspring and women be taken captive. And their wealth will be divided.” And in some of Bukhari’s ways, Gabriel came to him with dust covering his head.

Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Anas who said: “It is as if I am looking at the dust shining in the alleys of the sheep of the procession of Gabriel, may God’s prayers be upon him, when he walked.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Banu Qurayzah, and in the battles, in a different way, that the Companions saw Gabriel in the form of Dihya al-Kalbi. And he was covered with a turban, the end of which fell between his shoulders, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God sent him to the Banu Qurayzah to shake them.” their fortresses, and cast terror into their hearts.”

Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “that the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said on the day of Badr: ‘This is Gabriel holding the head of his horse with a tool on it. “War”

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Aisha, she said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “O Messenger of God, has a day ever come upon you that was more severe than On a Sunday? He said: I encountered some of your people, and the worst I encountered from them was on the day of Aqaba, when I presented myself to Ibn Abd, O Lail Ibn Abd. He was tired and did not answer what I wanted, so I went off with worry on my face. I did not wake up until I was by the horn of a fox, so I raised my head and behold... I was surrounded by a cloud that shaded me, so I looked and there was Gabriel in it. He called me and said:

God has heard what your people said to you, and they did not respond to you, and He has sent to you the Angel of the Mountains so that you may command him whatever you wish regarding them. He said: Then the King of the Mountains called me and greeted me and then said: O Muhammad: God has heard what your people said to you, and they did not respond to you, and I am the King of the Mountains. Your Lord has sent me to you so that you may order me to do whatever you wish, if you wish, so that I may close the two woods on them. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Rather, I hope that
God will bring forth from their descendants those who worship God alone and do not associate anything with Him.”

chapters.title: Chapter: May God protect his Prophet from the signs of his prophecy
paragraphs: [Chapter: May God protect His Prophet from the signs of his prophecy]

The seventh type regarding God’s sufficiency against his enemies, and His protection from people, and this is a sign of his prophecy in many ways: among them: that this Confirmation of the Almighty’s saying: {So proclaim what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists. Indeed, We are sufficient for you with the mockers who create with God another god. Then they will know} [Al-Hijr: 94]

This is God’s message that He will suffice the mockers of the polytheists, and He has informed that He will suffice the People of the Book by saying, “Say, ‘We believe.’” By God, and what was revealed to us, and what was sent down to Abraham, and Ishmael, and Isaac, and Jacob, and the tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus, and what was given to the prophets. Their Lord, We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit. So if they believe in what you believe in, then they are guided, but if they turn away, then it is only They are in discord, so God will suffice you for them, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.” [Al-Baqarah: 136]

So God told him that He would suffice him for those who were difficult for him among the People of the Book, and He told him that He would protect him from all people, according to the Almighty’s saying: {O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and if you do not do so, then you have not conveyed His message, and God will protect you from the people} [Al-Maeda: 67]
This is general news and God will protect him from all people.
Each of these three general news occurred as it was reported, and there are several verses in this, including:

He saved his enemies from strange ways that went beyond the known custom, including the fact that he supported him despite the large number of his enemies. And their strength, and their victory, and that he alone was open in his hostility towards them, and insulted their fathers, and insulted their gods, and belittled their dreams, And impugning their religion, and this is one of the extraordinary matters, and the mockers were among the greatest lords of Quraysh, and the greatest of the Arabs, and he The people of Mecca, the people of the Sacred Mosque, are the most esteemed and honorable of people. They are venerated by all nations. As for the Arabs, they were indebted to them, and as for others... Nations and they were

They magnify them because of it, especially since what happened to the people of the Elephant, just as the nations used to magnify the children of Israel because of the signs that appeared among them. It did not appear that these are the children of Israel, the son of God’s friend, and these are the sons of Isaac, the son of God’s friend, and both of them are among those whom God promised to Abraham in The Torah was among them because of what God had promised him of the blessings God had bestowed upon him, a blessing that God had not bestowed on anyone else. The people of Mecca were venerated because they were neighbors. House, and because they are the most noble of the children of Ishmael, God chose Kinana from among the descendants of Ishmael, and chose Quraysh from Kinana, and chose Hashim from Quraysh, and he chose Muhammad from Banu Hashim, and the nobles of these people were hostile to him, just as the Messiah was hostile to the nobles of the Children of Israel.

And these and those exchanged the blessing of God for disbelief, and made their people an abode of desolation. God, His Messenger the Messiah, sufficed those of them who were hostile to Him, and He did not Their lineage benefits them, but the virtue of their city does not benefit them. Likewise, God suffices Muhammad from those who antagonize him and take revenge on them. Their lineage does not benefit them, nor The virtue of their city, for God only establishes it by faith and piety, not by country or lineage, and God Almighty says: {And your people deny it, but it is the truth. Say: I am not a representative over you.} [Al-An’am: 66] (66) {For every report that is confirmed, and you will know} [Al-An’am: 67]
And he said: {And there is no town that is stronger in strength than your town that expelled you. We destroyed them, and there was no one to help them} [Muhammad: 13]

And he said: {And God sets forth an example of a town that used to be safe and secure, and its provision comes abundantly from every place. But it denied the blessings of God, so He made it taste of it. God is a garment of hunger and fear because of what they were doing.} [An-Nahl: 112] (112) {And there came to them a messenger from among themselves, but they rejected him, so the torment seized them while they were Unjust} [An-Nahl: 113]

The scholars have named some of those whom God has protected from mockers, and they were well-known and famous among the Companions for their leadership. And greatness is in this world, so mention them so that this great matter with which God honored His Prophet may be known.

In the two Sahih books, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: “Abu Jahl said: Will Muhammad wipe his face in front of you? It was said: Yes. He said: By Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, if I saw him doing that, I would have trampled on his neck. When they suddenly noticed him, he was turning back on his heels and protecting himself with his hands. Then it was said to him: What is the matter with you? He said: Between me and him there is a ditch of fire and terror and wings. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If he had come near me, the angels would have snatched him up, limb by limb.” And God Almighty revealed: {Have you seen the one who He forbids} [Al-Alaq: 9] (9) {A servant when he prays} [Al-Alaq:

10] (10) {Have you seen that he was upon guidance?} [Al-Al-Alq: 11] (11) {Or commanded piety} [Al-Al-Alq: 12] (12) {Have you seen that he lied and turned away?} [Al-Al-Alq: 13] (13) {Did he not know? That God sees} [Al-Al-Alq: 14] (14) {No, if it does not end, we will certainly strike the forelock} [Al-Al-Alq: 15] (15) {A lying, sinful forelock} [Al-Al-Alq: 16] (16) {So let him call on his caller} [Al-Al-Alq: 17] (17) {We will call on the immoral woman} [Al-Al-Alq: 18] (18) {No, do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near} [Al-Al-Alq: 19]

And in the two Sahihs there is a hadith of Al-Baraa bin Aazib, the hadith of “the migration of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr from Mecca to Medina, in which he said: We followed Suraqa bin Malik bin Jasham, and we were in the middle of the land, so I said: O Messenger of God, we have come. He said: Do not be sad, for God is with us. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, supplicated against him, and his horse struck her stomach, and he said: I know that you have both supplicated against me, so pray for me. I swear to God that I may refute your request. So he called upon God and was saved. He returned without meeting anyone except that he said:
What is here has sufficed for you, and it will not meet anyone without turning it back.

And in another version: “His horse trampled the ground to its belly, and he jumped off and said: O Muhammad, I know that this is your deed, so pray to God to He will save me from the state I am in, and you will be against me so that I will blind those who are behind me.”

And in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Shihab, from “the narration of Suraqa himself, he said: Messengers of the infidels of Quraysh came to us to make a statement about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” He greeted Abu Bakr and each one of them paid blood money to whoever killed him or captured him. While I was sitting in the gathering of my people, Bani Mudlij, when a man from among them approached until he rose up against us while we were sitting and said: O Suraqah, I saw Above, there were lions on the coast that Muhammad and his companions saw. Suraqa said: Then I knew it was them, so I said:

They are not among them, but you saw so-and-so and so-and-so, then I stayed for an hour, then I got up and entered my house, so I ordered my maid to bring out my horse while she was behind her. And you confined it to me, and I took my spear and went out with it from the back of the house and struck the surface of the earth, and I lowered its hilt until I came My horse, so I mounted her and raised her, bringing me closer until I approached them, and my horse stumbled over me, so I fell down from her, so I got up and lowered my hand to my quiver. So I extracted the arrows from it

So I swore by it, and the one I hated came out, so I rode and disobeyed the men, so she brought me closer until I heard the recitation of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said hello and he did not turn around, and Abu Bakr turned around a lot. My horse’s hands went deep into the ground until they reached the knees, so I got down from her and then I rebuked her and she got up, but she could hardly take out her hands. When she was standing upright, bright dust appeared on her hands in the sky like smoke, so she swore. With shackles, then the one I hated came out, so I called them to safety, and they stopped, so I rode my horse until I came to them, and I fell into myself when I met what I had met. Detaining them until the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, becomes known.
. » He mentioned the entire hadith.

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Jabir, he said: “We invaded with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, an army before we found, so we overtook the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He greeted the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a valley full of snakes. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, descended under a tree and hung his sword on one of its branches. The people dispersed in the valley, seeking shade from the trees, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A man came to me while I was sleeping and took the sword.” So I woke up and he was standing over my head, with the sword in his hand, and he said: Who will protect you from me? I said:

God, so he drew the sword, and here he is sitting.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not present it to him, and he was the king of his people, so he departed when He pardoned him and said: “I will not be among a people who are at war with you.”

And in Sahih Al-Hakim, on the authority of Abdul-Rahman bin Abi Bakr Al-Siddiq, he said: “So-and-so was sitting next to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and when he spoke The Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, had a tremble on his face, and the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: “Be like that.” He continued to tremble until he died.

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said: “There was a Christian man who converted to Islam, and he recited Al-Baqarah and the Family of Imran, and he used to write to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he became a Christian and used to say: Muhammad does not know except what I have written for him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O God, make him a sign.” So God caused him to die, and in the morning the ground had vomited him out, so they said: This is what he did. Muhammad and his companions, when he fled from them, they searched for our companion and threw him.

So they dug for him, as deep as they could, and in the morning the earth had spit out of him, so they said the same as the first, so they dug for him and as deep as they could, and the third spit. “So they knew that it was not the work of people, so they left it rejected.”

Imam Ahmad narrated from the hadith of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yahya bin Urwa told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, who said: “I said to him: How often have you seen the Quraysh attack the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in terms of their hostility toward him? He said: I attended them, and their nobles gathered one day in Al-Hijr, and they mentioned the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: We have never seen anything like it. We have never been patient with this man’s affairs. He made our dreams belittle, insulted our fathers, criticized our religion, divided our groups, and cursed our gods. We were patient with him over a great matter.

Or as they said. While they were in that, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appeared upon them and began walking until he reached the corner, then passed by them, circling the House. When he passed by them, they winked at him and said something. He said: I recognized that in his face, then he went on, and when he passed the second time, they gave him a similar wink, so I recognized that in his face, then he went on and passed by them. The third time, they winked at him like that, and he said:

“You have heard, O people of Quraysh, by the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, I have come to you with a sacrifice.” So the people took his word until not a man among them Except as if a bird was perched on his head, until the strongest of them was a guardian of it before that, to comfort him with the best words he could find until It is to say: Go away, Father.

Al-Qasim, go away wisely, for by God you were not ignorant. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left, and the next day they gathered in the Hijr and I was with them, and they said to each other: You mentioned what he told you about him, and what he told you about him, to the point that when he told you something you disliked, you abandoned him. While they were in that, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came up and they jumped towards him like a single man, and they surrounded him, saying to him: You are the one who She says such and such, because he was telling them about the defect of their gods and their religion. He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, says:
“Yes, I am the one who says that.” He said: I saw a man among them taking hold of his robe, and Abu Bakr stood up beside him and said while crying.
{Will you kill a man because he says: My Lord is God?} [Ghafir: 28]
Then they turned away from him.”

Al-Bukhari mentioned after the hadith of Urwa, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, he said: And Abdah said: On the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father, it was said to Amr bin Al-Aas, and Saeed bin Jubayr narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas in the Almighty’s saying: {Indeed, We are sufficient for you with mockers} [Al-Hijr: 95]

He said: The mockers were Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah, Al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth Al-Zuhri, and Al-Aswad ibn Al-Muttalib Abu Zam’ah from the Banu Asad bin Abdul-Uzza, Al-Harith bin Aital Al-Sahmi, and Al-Aas bin Wael. Gabriel gestured to Akhal Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah and said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked him: What have you done? He said: That's enough for him, and he pointed to Al-Aswad bin Al-Muttalib with his eyes and said: What did you do? He said: That is enough for him, and he pointed to the head of Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghouth and said: What did you do? He said: It is enough for him, and he pointed to Al-Harith Al-Sahmi to his stomach and said, What did you do?

He said: That is enough for him, and he pointed to Akhmas bin Wael and said: What did you do? He said: That is enough for him. As for Al-Walid, he passed by a man from Khuza’ah while he was feathering his arrow, and he hit his ankle.

So he cut it off, and as for Al-Aswad ibn Al-Muttalib, he was blind. Some of them say that he was blind like that, and some of them say: He descended under a sunburst, so he began to say: O my children, will you not turn away from me and say: We do not see anything? Then he began to say: I am destroyed. Here I am, being pierced in the eyes with thorns. So they started saying: We did not see anything. He continued like that until his eyes became blind. As for the black one, sores broke out on his head and he died from them. As for Al-Harith bin Aital, the yellow water in his stomach took him until his excrement came out of his mouth and he died.
As for Al-Aas bin Wa’il, he rode to Taif on a donkey, and he was struck by a thorn, which entered the sole of his foot, and he died. It was said: A lightning bolt entered his head and he died.

Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim in his interpretation. He said: Yunus bin Habib told us, Abu Dawud told us, Abu Awanah told us, Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed, and he narrated with his chain of transmission on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas. He said: “The owner of Yemen wanted to see the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so Al-Walid came to him and claimed that Muhammad was a magician, and Al-Aas bin Wael came to him.” So he told him that Muhammad had learned the legends of the ancients, and another came to him and claimed that he was a priest, and another claimed that he was a poet, and another said that he was crazy.

So God destroyed them, and each of them was afflicted with a torment other than the torment of his companion, and He mentioned the details of their torment.” He narrated a similar example on the authority of Ikrimah.

Muhammad bin Ishaq said, narrated by Yazid bin Roman, on the authority of Urwa and other scholars, “Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they They went around the House, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood next to him, and Al-Aswad bin Al-Muttalib passed by him and threw a paper in his face. Green and he became blind, and Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth passed by him and pointed to his stomach, and he drew water and died from it, and Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah passed by him He pointed to a wound on the bottom of his heel, which he had sustained when he passed by a man sharpening his arrow. He scratched his leg, but not anything, so he jumped up and died.

Al-Aas bin Wa'il passed by him and pointed to the sole of his foot. Many ways on the authority of a group of followers, and among the well-known among the scholars and others is his supplication for Utaiba bin Abi Lahab, “And Abu Lahab: When he was hostile to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he ordered his two sons to divorce the two daughters of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

He greeted Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum before entering, and Utaiba said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: I disbelieved in your religion and separated from your daughter. You love me and I do not love you. Then he attacked him by harming him and tore his shirt. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O God, send over him a dog of “Your dogs.” So he went out with a group of Quraysh until they camped in a place in the Levant called Az-Zarqa at night, and Assad went around them that night and made Utaiba He says: Woe to my brother, by God, he is the one who will eat me, as Muhammad called on me.

He killed me while he was in Mecca and I was in the Levant. Then a lion from among the people attacked him, took its head and slaughtered it. In the narration of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, said: When the lion came around them that night, and departed from them, they rose up and placed Utaiba in the midst of them, and the lion approached. He passed them until he took Utaiba’s head and bit him.”

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, he said: “While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying at the House, Abu Jahl and his companions He had a seat, and camels had been slaughtered yesterday, so Abu Jahl said: Which of you would go up and cut the camels of the tribe of so-and-so and take them and put them on my shoulder? When Muhammad prostrated? Then the most wretched of the people ran and took it, and when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prostrated, he placed it between his shoulders and said:

They laughed, and some of them leaned on one another, while I stood and watched. If I had had the strength, I would have pushed him away from the back of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, was prostrating and did not raise his head until a person went to Fatima and she, a Juwayriyah, came and threw him down, then She came to them cursing them, and when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished his prayer, he raised his voice and then supplicated against them. And when he called, he called three, and when He asked three questions, then he said:

“O God, bless the Quraysh” three times. When they heard his voice, their laughter stopped, and they were afraid of his call. Then he said: O God, bless Abu Jahl bin Hisham, Utbah bin Rabi’ah, Shaybah bin Rabi’ah, Al-Walid bin Utbah, Umayyah bin Khalaf, and Uqba bin Abi Mu’ayt, and he mentioned Seventh, I did not memorize it. By the One who sent Muhammad with the truth, I have seen the One who named my epilepsy.
On the day of Badr, then they were dragged to the heart of Badr.”

On his authority, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, faced the Qiblah and called for six people and mentioned them. In a narration: However, Umayyah bin Behind him was a huge man, and his limbs were cut off, so he was not thrown into the well. He said: The sun changed them, and it was a hot day.

And this includes what people still see and hear about, God’s vengeance on those who curse him and censure his religion in various ways. Punishments, and this is one of the many stories that this topic is too narrow to expand on, and we have seen and heard of that which would take a long time to describe. Of God’s vengeance on those who harm him with various kinds of wondrous punishments that demonstrate God’s faithfulness to His honor, His victory, and His glorification. Because of his destiny

chapters.title: Answering his prayers, peace be upon him, is one of the signs of his prophecy
paragraphs: And He raised it up for the remembrance of Him, and there is not a group of people except that they have from this chapter something in which there is an example for those of understanding, and from what is known. What is well known among the Muslim soldiers in the Levant, when they besiege some of the fortresses of the People of the Book, is that it is difficult for them to conquer the fort, and it takes a long time. The siege until the enemy curses the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, then the Muslims will rejoice in the conquest of the fortress and God’s vengeance on those who The enemy, for that will be soon, as the Muslims have experienced it more than once, in fulfillment of the Almighty’s saying: {Indeed, your affair is the amputee} [Al-Kawthar: 3]
When Khosrau tore up his letter, God tore up the kingdom of the Aksaraites in every tear, and when Heraclius and Al-Muqawqis honored his letter, theirs remained theirs.
[Answering his prayers, peace be upon him, is one of the signs of his prophecy]

The eighth type is in answering one’s supplication, and answering one’s supplication is something that is usual for many of God’s servants, such as singing. And well-being, and the like, and among them is what is called for that is contrary to customs, such as eating and drinking in large amounts outside the norm. And feeding the palm trees twice a year, although the custom is once for the same, and restoring the sight of the blind, and similar things to what follows, and what was mentioned above. I prayed for him.

It is known that whoever God promises to answer his supplication can only be one of his righteousness and religion, and whoever claims prophethood can only be one of the most righteous of people. He was truthful or one of the most immoral of them if he was a liar, and when God promised him the answer to his supplication, he was not an immoral person but rather righteous, and if he did not have a supplication Prophethood, except for a righteous person who is certain to be a truthful prophet, for this prevents him from deliberately lying, and prevents him from being misguided and thinking that he A prophet, and the one who comes to him is an angel, and he is lost in that, and the one who comes to Satan, then this is the state of one who is ignorant of his own condition. And the condition of the one who comes to him, and someone like this is neither more astray than him, nor more ignorant than him, because God Almighty has placed between the angels and the devils, and between True prophets, and between the liars who imitate them there is such a difference that no one else can count. Rather, He created between the righteous and the unrighteous. Of the differences greater than between night and day, and because what the prophets bring of news and orders is contrary in every way to what Satan brings it, and whoever studies the conditions of the messengers and their followers, and the conditions of the soothsayers and magicians, it will become clear to him what makes that happen.

The devil who says to someone who is not a prophet: You are a true prophet, and God has sent me to you, is one of the greatest liars of people, and lying It entails immorality, so he must command him to do something that is not righteousness but sinfulness, and tell him something that is not truthful but a lie, as is the reality of those whom you mislead. The devils are from the ignorant of the servants, and from those to whom it appears that they are a prophet, or that they are the Mahdi, or the Seal of the Saints, and all of these must The devils command him to commit a sin, and he must lie about some of what they tell him, in fulfillment of the Almighty’s saying: {Shall I inform you upon whom it was revealed? The devils} [Poets:
221] (221) {It descends upon every sinful creature} [Al-Shu’ara’: 222]

Then such a thing would not be the case with the call to prophecy from the righteous whom God has promised to answer their supplications in an answer outside of customs, but no one will be with the claim of prophethood except among the immoral and immoral people, and if he is truthful in the claim of prophethood, knowing that he is truthful, it is proven He is a prophet.

The prophets are infallible from admitting error in what they convey about God, by agreement of the people, and in that case everything they convey about God is It is the truth, and it is what is desired, and whoever comes to it is both truthful and a liar, like the son of a fisherman, and like many of the servants who have inspiration. From the angel, and a whisper from Satan that he is a prophet, and he says: I have been sent by God, so his lie must be revealed, even in some ways. Such as telling him a lie, for such a devil who told him that he is a prophet must lie about what he tells him.

Such as the truthful person telling him that this is a lie. If Satan comes to him with a lie, the truthful person to whom he is coming must tell him what This differs from the fact that informing him of partial matters, as telling him that he is a true prophet even though he is not so would destroy him completely. Great, and it spoils for the truthful everything that he tells him, because that requires that that liar to believe in everything that he tells him, as he has He believed that he was a prophet, and in that case he would not be a liar in his eyes, nor would he know that he was a liar, so he would not be like the son of a fisherman and the like, among those who are known Indeed, there will come to him a truthful and a liar, but even more astray than these:

He thinks that everything that comes to him is truthful, and for this reason everyone who receives true royal news and false satanic news must To know that a liar is coming to him, because it has become clear to him that what the lying Satan tells him is false, as it is the reality.

That is why there are soothsayers who know that the one who tells them a lot is lying, as well as the servants who have speeches and revelations, some of which Some of them are satanic and some of them are angelic. It becomes clear to them that they are lying in what Satan brings them, as is the reality. There is no sheikh who worships him in any condition. Satanic, unless he tells him a lie that will appear to him to be a lie, and in that case, if this liar is truthful in telling him the prophecy He was believing the liar, and because the truthful person who comes to him informing him of the truth and advising him must explain that to him, so he does not insist on believing Indeed, whoever comes to him is telling the truth, while in the same matter he is a liar, and no one knows that he is a liar except one who is deceitful and sinful, and God Almighty says:
{Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?} [Al-Shu’ara’: 221] (221) {On whom do the devils descend?} [Al-Shu’ara’: 222]

So it descended upon the sinful licentious, and as for the descent of Satan once or twice, it may be upon whoever is not a sinful licentious, for whoever is not He was not claiming to be a prophet in this regard, and if he was claiming to be a prophet, then it is impossible for the truthful person who comes to him to acknowledge that, rather no. This must be explained to him, if that is permissible.
The people disputed: Is it permissible for Satan to put into the mouth of the Prophet what God abolishes and erases, or is that not permissible? In any case, he refrains from admitting a mistake.

What is meant here is to mention some of the supplications of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, which were seen to be answered. Some of his supplications have already been mentioned, such as His supplication was made public by the Quraysh, and they were killed on the day of Badr, and thrown into the pit, and his supplication was similar to that of Utaiba bin Abi Lahab, and the same was his supplication on Who lied about him by making him a sign, and like his supplication when the provision was scarce and they gathered it to a trickle, so God multiplied him with the blessings of his supplication until it was enough. The great army in the Battle of Tabuk, and similar to his supplication in the Battle of the Trench: Enough food, which is a saa’ of barley for a thousand people, and likewise His supplication when the well of Al-Hudaybiyyah was drained and its water increased until it was enough for the caravan, which was one thousand five hundred and their passengers.

His supplication was presented for the one whose sight had gone and he saw, and his supplication was for rain, but he did not raise his hands until the sky had rained, and his supplication was for rain. recovery, and his pointing to the clouds, so his watch was interrupted, and his invitation to Suraqa bin Jasham when he followed them in the migration, so it sank His horse is in the land, and his supplication was on the day of Badr and on the day of Hunayn, and God said to him on the day of Badr: “When you sought help from your Lord, and He answered you. He will provide you with a thousand of the angels following each other} [Al-Anfal: 9]
And similar things to that, and in the two Sahih books on the authority of Jabir, he said: “When it was revealed: {Say: He is capable of sending upon you a torment from above you} [Al-An’am: 65]
The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I seek refuge in Your Face” {or from under your feet} [Al-An’am: 65]
He said: “I seek refuge in Your Face” {Or He will divide you into factions and make some of you taste the violence of one another} [Al-An’am: 65]
He said: “These two are easier or easier.”

And in the two Sahih books on the authority of him, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “I asked my Lord for three, and He gave me two, but withheld one from me. I asked Him not to destroy my nation.” With a general Sunnah, so he gave it to me, and I asked him not to let an enemy from other than them dominate them and invade them, so he gave it to me, and I asked him not to make Because of their wrath among them, so he prevented it, and the turmoil will not cease until the Day of Resurrection.”

And in Sahih Muslim, from “the hadith of Salama bin Al-Akwa’, he said: It made my uncle tremble and say: By God, had it not been for God, we would not have been guided... and do not give us charity or give charity.” We have prayed, and we are not of Your help. So, make our feet firm when we meet us, and send down tranquility upon us. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He said: “Who is this?” They said: “Amer.” He said: “Your Lord has forgiven you.” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not ask forgiveness of anyone special to him except that he was martyred. He said: Then Omar bin Al-Khattab, while he was on his camel, called out: O Prophet of God, if we had not given Amer a treat. He said:
When we came to Khaybar, their king came out welcoming, brandishing his sword and saying:

Khaybar has learned that I am welcome... The one who wields weapons is a proven hero when wars come to rage. He said: And my uncle Amer appeared to him and said: Khaybar has learned. I am Amer... The one who wields the weapon is an adventurous hero. He said: Then they struck each other and Marhab’s sword fell into Amer’s shield, and Amer went to draw his sword and his sword came back. He cut off his ankle, while his soul was in it. Salamah said: Then I heard a group of the Prophet’s companions, may God Almighty’s prayers and peace be upon him, say: Amir’s work was vain, he killed himself. He said: So I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while crying and said:

O Messenger of God, Amer’s work has been in vain? The Messenger of God, may God Almighty’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: “Who said that?” I said: Some of your friends. He said: Whoever said that lied, but he will have his reward twice.

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said: “Umm Sulaym said: O Messenger of God, your servant Anas, pray to God for him.” He said: “O God, increase his wealth and his children, and bless him in what You have given him.”

Al-Bukhari narrated that he said: “The Prophet, may God Almighty’s prayers and peace be upon him, went to Umm Sulaim and brought him dates and ghee. He said: ‘Put your ghee back in his watering can. “And he put your dates in his bowl.” Then he got up toward the house and prayed something that was not written down, so he called for Umm Sulaym and her family. Umm Sulaym said: O Messenger of God, I have a special choice. He said: “What is it?” She said: Your servant Anas. He said:

He did not leave behind the Hereafter or this world except that he supplicated, “O God, grant him wealth and a child, and bless him in it.” For I am the most wealthy of the Ansar. My daughter Amina told me that a hundred and twenty-four were buried for my descendants at the beginning of the pilgrims’ journey in Basra. And in a narration by Muslim: “He prayed for me three times, two of which I saw, and I hope for the third in the afterlife.”

And in Al-Tirmidhi, and he classified it as hasan, on the authority of Abu Khaldah, he said: I said to Abu Al-Aliyah: “Did Anas hear from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace?” He said: He served him for ten years, and the Prophet, may God Almighty’s prayers and peace be upon him, prayed for him, and he had an orchard that bore fruit twice a year, and he There is a fragrance in it, from which comes the scent of musk.”

And in Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: I was calling my mother to Islam, and she was a polytheist, so I called her one day and she made me listen to the Messenger of God.” God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what I hate, so I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I was crying, and I said: O Messenger of God, I was praying My mother converted to Islam but she refused me, so I called her today and she told me about you what I hate, so pray to God to guide Abu Hurairah’s mother, and he said The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace:

“Oh God, guide Umm Abu Hurairah.” So I went out, rejoicing in the call of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so I went to the door and found it was empty. So my mother heard my feet tapping and said: Where are you, Abu Hurairah? And I heard the chucking of the water, so she bathed, put on her armor, and hastened. She put on her veil and opened the door and said: O Abu Hurairah, I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. So I came to him crying with joy and said: O Messenger of God, give good news, for he has lost good news.

God answered your prayer and guided Abu Hurairah’s mother. He thanked God and said good, so I said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to make me and my mother love forever. His faithful servants, and He makes them beloved to us. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Oh God, make this servant of Yours beloved, meaning Abu Hurairah. And his mother to Your faithful servants, and make the believers endear to them. “So God has not created a believer who hears of me or sees me but that he loves me.”

And in the two Sahih books, “On the authority of Anas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw traces of yellowness on Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and said: “What is this?” He said: Oh. Messenger of God, I married a woman. He said: “How much did you drive for it?” He said: The weight of a stone of gold. He said: “May God bless you. Do you know even a sheep?”

And in the two Sahih books: “When he came, the brother of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came between him and Sa’d bin al-Rabi’ al-Ansari, and Sa’d proposed to him that He was fair with his family and wealth, so Abdul Rahman said to him: May God bless your family and wealth. Show me the market.” Then the blessing of the call of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became clear, and Abdul Rahman’s wealth amounted to what Al-Zuhri said: He gave four hundred thousand dinars in charity, and carried five hundred horses for the sake of God, and five hundred camels for the sake of God. He said: Most of his money came from trade.
Muhammad ibn Sirin said: The wives of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf divided their price, and it was three hundred and twenty thousand.
Al-Zuhri said: Abd al-Rahman advised those who witnessed Badr, and they found a hundred, for each man of them four hundred dinars.

Abdullah bin Jaafar said: Umm Bakr bint Al-Miswar told me that Abdul Rahman sold land for forty thousand dinars and divided it among the poor. Bani Zahra, among the immigrants, and the mothers of the believers.

Muhammad bin Amr said: On the authority of Abu Salama that Abdul Rahman bequeathed a garden to the mothers of the believers, so its value was one hundred thousand. It is narrated in Al-Tirmidhi and he authenticated it, and Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O God, honor Islam is based on the two men most beloved to you, Omar ibn al-Khattab or Abu Jahl ibn Hisham. Omar ibn al-Khattab was the most beloved of them to God. So Omar converted to Islam.” It was narrated that the invitation was on a Wednesday, so he converted to Islam on a Thursday, and God glorified Islam through him. He said: Abdullah Ibn Masoud:

We are still proud since Omar converted to Islam. Narrated by Al-Bukhari. He emerged from the glory of Islam in his emirate, east and west, and conquered the Levant, Iraq, and Egypt, and defeated the armies of Chosroes and Caesar, which he achieved. Answering the call.

“And in the two Sahih books, Ibn Abbas performed ablution for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he went to the toilet to perform ablution, and he said when he left: “Who placed this?” It was said: Ibn Abbas said: “O God, grant him understanding of religion, and teach him interpretation.”

In one narration, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, hugged me to his chest and said: ‘O God, teach him the Book.’ And in the narration, ‘Wisdom’.” The answer to his call appeared until it was called: the sea.

Ibn Masoud said about it: If Ibn Abbas had touched our teeth, none of us would have touched him. Omar used to introduce him and introduce him with the major companions, and the knowledge of Ibn Abbas was famous among the nation.

And in the two Sahih books, “On the authority of Jabir, he said: I was walking on a camel that had become tired, and I wanted to let it go. He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, caught up with me, hit him, prayed for him, and he went on a journey he had never walked before. And in a narration: He said to me: “What’s wrong with your camel?” And I said: He’s sick. He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, lagged behind, so he rebuked him and called for him. He continued to walk in front of the camels, and he said: “How do you see?” “With your camel?” I said: “Okay, your blessing has reached him.” He said: “Then follow him....” He mentioned the hadith.
And in Al-Tirmidhi and others: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O God, answer Sa’d when he calls upon you.” And in another version: “O God, answer his call.”
And he aimed well at his shot. “Saad would not throw without hitting it, and would not make a supplication without being answered.”

Al-Hakim narrated in his Sahih, “On the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: I fell ill and the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, visited me, and I said: Oh God, if My time has come, so give me comfort, and if it is late, raise me up, and if it is a calamity, give me patience. He said: “O God, heal him, O God, grant him health.” Then he said to me: “Get up.” So I got up, and that pain did not return to me again.

And in the two Sahihs it is narrated on the authority of Umm Khalid that she said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought clothes with a small black khamis on them, and he said: ‘Who do you see? Did they cover him with this khamis? Then the people remained silent, so he said: “Bring me Khalid’s mother.” So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought to me and he dressed me in her. He said: “Behave and behave” twice, then he looked at the flag of the khamisah and pointed to me with his hand and said: “O Umm Khaled, this is a Sunnah.” And the Sunnah In the beautiful Abyssinian tongue, it remained until darkness,” “On the authority of Abu Yazid Amr bin Akhtab Al-Ansari, he said:

The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: “Come closer to me.” He wiped his hand over my head and my beard, then said: “O God, make him beautiful, and perpetuate his beauty.”

The narrator said about him: He was eighty-two years old, and there was no white in his beard except a small trace, and his face was flat, and he did not His face would shrink until he died.” It was narrated by Imam Ahmad, and Al-Bayhaqi said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it, and he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wiped May God bless him and grant him peace. He placed his hand on my face and prayed for me. “He said: Ezra: He lived for one hundred and twenty years, and there were nothing on his head except white hairs.” He said: It is a good hadith.

Al-Bukhari said in his history: Ya’qub bin Ishaq narrated to us, “On the authority of Hanzalah bin Hanifa bin Hudhaym. Hudhaym said: O Messenger of God, I am a man.” He has a tooth, and this is my youngest son, so she named him. He said: “Come, boy.” So he took my hand, stroked my head, and said: “May God bless you” or “May God bless you.” Then I saw Hanzalah being brought to the man. The tumor goes away, and he wipes it with his hand and says: In the name of God, and the tumor goes away. And in one narration: And the sheep, and the camel.

It is mentioned “on the authority of Abu Sufyan, whose name is Madluk, that he went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he converted to Islam, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed for him.” He greeted him, wiped his head with his hand, and prayed for his blessing. The front of his head, where the hand of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was black, and the rest of it was white.” Al-Bukhari also mentioned it in his history and narrated Ahmad in his Musnad, with his chain of transmission, on the authority of Abu Al-Ala, said: “I was with Qatada bin Malhan during his illness in which he died, and a man passed by at the back of the house. I saw him in the face of Qatada. He said:
The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was wiping his face. He said: Before I saw him, I saw him as if he had paint on his face.

And in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, “On the authority of Urwa ibn Abi al-Ja’d, he said: A burden was offered to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he gave me a dinar, and he said: ‘i.e. “Bring the saddlebags and buy a sheep.” So I brought the saddlebags and bargained with its owner and bought two sheep from him for a dinar. I came to drive them and a man met me. So he bargained with me and I would sell him a sheep for a dinar, so I brought the dinar and I brought the sheep, and I said: O Messenger of God, this is your dinar, and this is your sheep. He said: “And how did you do it?” So I told him the hadith and he said:

“Oh God, bless him in his right hand.” I saw me standing in the Kufa church and winning forty thousand before I reached my family. It was narrated by Imam Ahmad, and in one word: “If he had bought dirt, he would have made a profit from it.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari on the authority of his people.

And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Salama bin Al-Akwa’, “A man ate with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with his left hand, and he said to him: ‘Eat with your right hand.’” He said: I can't. He said: “No, you can’t.” Nothing prevented him except pride. He said: He did not raise it to his mouth.

Malik narrated in his Muwatta on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, “On the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Sulami, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in The Battle of Banu Anmar. Jabir said: While I was camping under a tree, I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: Come, O Messenger of God. To the shadow. He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, descended. Jabir said: So I went to a cave of ours, searched for it, and found in it a bunch of gourds.

So I broke it, then brought it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “Where did you get this?” We said: We took it out of Medina. He said: We have a friend who we prepare for and he goes and takes care of us. He said: So I prepared him, then he turned around and went to the back, wearing two garments of his own that he had created. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked and said: “ Does he not have two garments other than these? I said: Yes, O Messenger of God. I covered them with two garments for the defect. He said: “Call him to wear them.” Then he turned to go, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said:

“What is the matter with him that God beheaded him? Isn’t that better for him?” Then the man heard him and said: O Messenger of God, for the sake of God? He said: “In the path of God,” so the man was killed in the path of God. It was narrated by Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Sa’id bin Sulaiman, on the authority of Al-Layth, on the authority of Hisham bin Sa’id.
On the authority of Zayd bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Jabir.

chapters.title: Chapter on six major ways to interrupt the prophecy of Muhammad, peace be upon him
paragraphs: [Chapter: Six major ways to interrupt the prophecy of Muhammad, peace be upon him]
In the ways in which this news has been shown to benefit science.

Some of these reports are what is in the Qur’an, and some of them are frequent and known to both the general public and the private, such as a spring of water from between His fingers, eating a lot of food, bending the trunk, and the like. News about each of these has been frequent and extensive, and has been transmitted. The nation, generation after generation, and successor to predecessor. There is no class of the nation without these verses being transmitted, widely known, and widely known. In it, he transmitted it more than those who transmitted much of the Qur’an, and he transmitted it and heard it from the nation more than those who heard and quoted many of the verses. The Qur’an, and most of those who heard and transmitted that he used to prostrate two prostrations of forgetfulness in prayer, and among those who heard and transmitted the obligation of zakat and its obligations, rather, specific times Prayer and its numbers, but it has become common to transfer it in order to practice it regularly.

As for these verses, more people reported the times of prayer in terms of specific information, and that is because the Messenger’s verses were many. From it there will be a spectacle of great creation, and they will see those signs as the people of Al-Hudaybiyyah, who were one thousand five hundred, saw the spring of water. From between his fingers, and a lot of water appeared from the well of Al-Hudaybiyyah when they displaced it, and they did not leave a drop in it, and it increased until the soldiers narrated, And as the soldiers saw in the Battle of Dhath ar-Riqa’, there was little water when Jabir poured it into the basin and it was filled, and the entire army filled from it, and as The army, on their return from the Battle of Khaybar, witnessed the two auctions with the woman, and they filled each vessel with them and drank, while they were full as they were.

And as the people of Khaybar, who were one thousand five hundred, saw the food that was like the flesh of a sheep, it satiated the whole army, and as the army witnessed The Great, and they were about thirty thousand in Tabuk, the spring, when it was scarce in water, and its water increased until it was enough for them, and they saw the food they had gathered on the He obeyed, and they took from him until they had enough, and as the people of Khandaq saw, who were more than a thousand, there was an abundance of food in Jabir’s house after he had been A saa of barley and a bunch of grapes, and they all ate after being hungry until they were satisfied, and there was leftover, and as the eighty people saw, there was a large amount of food when they ate. In the house of Abu Talha, and as the three hundred witnessed the abundance of water when they performed ablution from a cup, and the water came out from between his fingers, until it was enough for them. For ablution, and likewise for Zainab’s feast, there were three hundred of them, and they ate food in a stone tent, which was

remained, so Anas thought that it was more than it was, and they were sharing a portion from morning until night, ten would stand up and ten would sit, as in The hadith of Samurah ibn Jundub and the people of Suffah: When they all drank a little milk, it was enough for them and some leftover, and they were transmitting that among themselves. It is famous and transmitted by some of those who witnessed it to those who missed it. The extent of its verses, their fame, and their frequency among the nation was greater. From the frequent prostration of forgetfulness in prayer, this was only a few times, and it was only attended by those praying behind him for that prayer, and likewise They quoted the status of zakat and its duties, for only a small group heard this from him, and they quoted it.

The same applies to his ruling on pre-emption for what is not divided, his ruling that the blood money for a mistake is due on the sane woman, and his ruling that the child should be given to the bed. The prostitute is subject to stone, and he is forbidden to marry unmarried men, and he is forbidden to divorce a menstruating woman and to divorce a woman who has intercourse before it becomes clear that she is pregnant, and that A woman who is freed under a slave is given the right to choose, inheriting one-sixth from her grandmother, and prohibiting a woman from marrying her paternal aunt and paternal aunt. And his saying, “For what the sky watered, a tenth, and for what was watered by the pedestals and the basins, half of the tenth,” and similar things, were only heard by a group of the nation. They are much fewer than those who witnessed its signs, and then the nation is agreed on the transmission of that, and these rulings are known to have been transmitted from him. By being forced to leave his religion.

If things like these were frequent in the nation, and they agreed to transmit it, then how about since it was more famous and apparent to those who witnessed it? The knowledge of those who saw him about it was more evident than their knowledge of these rulings, and they conveyed that to those who were absent from them, for it is definitely The frequency of these verses among the nation must be greater and clearer, and for this reason there is hardly a Muslim who does not know many of these. The verses, and he heard them and transmitted them to others, contrary to many of the Mutawatir rulings about him, which are agreed upon among the scholars regarding their transmission. Many people do not know it, nor have heard of it.

And if the speaker says: These are among the things that there are aspirations and reasons for conveying, then if they were present, then the aspirations and reasons would be present for them. He transmitted it, and if that had been the case, it would have been repeated. We said:

Likewise, praise be to God, there were more aspirations and reasons for quoting it than there were efforts and reasons for quoting most of the verses. The prophets before him, and more than what was available, were motivated and motivated to convey amazing news from the lives of kings and caliphs. He pondered the transmission of these verses and found their fame at all times, and the appearance of news about them is greater than the fame of the news that was transmitted.
