Prophets and the biographies of kings and states that usually had the inspiration and reasons for conveying them, such a situation is not obligatory in its being It is common for it to happen frequently to everyone.

If the conditions of its predecessors are most frequently heard by each nation, many nations may not hear it from others, let alone its frequency. They have such that many nations who do not know the prophets have never heard of the names of the prophets or their information. In addition to the fact that it was repeated among them, and most of the followers of the prophets did not receive news of the kings and their lives as much as they did. According to others, even most Muslims have not heard of the names of the caliphs of the Umayyads and the Abbasids, and the names of their ministers and deputies. And their pimp.

And the wars that took place between them, and they do not know the great facts of the wars that took place between the Muslims and their enemies, like the day Ajnadayn, and the day of Marj al-Safar, and the day of Fahl, and the like of the day of al-Hurra, and the day of Marj Rahit, and the temptation of Ibn al-Muhallab, and the temptation of Ibn Al-Ash'ath and Al-Qur'a with Al-Hajjaj, the war of Mus'ab bin Al-Zubayr with Al-Mukhtar bin Abi Ubaid, and the strife of Al-Mansur with Muhammad bin Abdullah Bin Hassan bin Hassan in Medina, and with his brother Ibrahim in Basra, and such as Jisr Abu Ubaid, the Day of Yarmouk, and the Day of Al-Qadisiyah, They do not know that the Muslims conquered Cyprus, nor invaded Constantinople twice, once in the time of Muawiyah, and once in the time of Bani Marwan.
And likewise the temptations that occurred among Muslims.

Indeed, most of the common people had not heard of Abu Muslim, the one who preached the call, or of Abdullah bin Ali bin Abdullah bin Abbas, and what happened to them. From the wars with the soldiers of Marwan, the last caliph of the Umayyads. They also did not hear of the entry of Abd al-Rahman ibn Hisham into Andalusia, and what happened. He has no right to it, nor because of the strife that broke out between the two sons of Al-Rashid, Al-Amin and Al-Ma’mun, although these matters are frequent according to people of knowledge about biography. And the news of people and histories, and the appearance of these verses, which are the evidence and signs of prophecy, are well-known among the nation as a whole. Its specificity in every time is greater than the appearance of these recurring news, so it is more worthy of being made frequent than this, and the transfer of this Verses from the special ones:

The people of knowledge, and the books of hadith, interpretation, mysteries, biographies, and books of principles and jurisprudence in which these reports are found, are more correct. Quoting, according to the agreement of the people of reason and knowledge, from the transmitted history books, many of its narrations have a broken chain of narration, and there are Lies are what no one can count except God, even if the origin of the story may be mutawatir, and these verses that are well-known in the nation are many. Its types are frequent among scholars, and many of its types are frequent among the elite.

Indeed, many of the jurists and theologians, or most of them, do not know the number of battles of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in which he fought. His enemies, and these are well-known events, each of which is frequently reported and apparent to the people of knowledge, such as the day of Badr, the day of Uhud, and the day The Trench, the Battle of Banu Mustaliq, the Battle of Khaybar, the Conquest of Mecca, the Day of Hunayn, and the Siege of Taif.

Many people of knowledge, as well as the common people, even if they have heard of these names or some of them, do not know which one it was before. The other, and they do not know which area those invaders were in, nor do they know who the enemy was in, nor what it was like. Rather, most of the common people do not They distinguish between Badr and Hunayn. Rather, their speaker says: The day of Badr and Hunayn, and they think that that is one day, and that it is one battle. And they did not know that they had invaded each other for about six years.

Badr was in the second year of the Hijra, and Hunayn was in the eighth year after the conquest of Mecca, and Badr was a place between Mecca, Medina is on the northern side of Mecca, and the Yemeni side of Medina, and Hunayn, a valley near Taif, east of Mecca, but He linked them together in the name because God He sent down the angels therein, and supported His Prophet and the believers with them until they defeated their enemy with the enemy’s strength at Badr, and with a greater defeat. Muslims first with compassion, and God was grateful for that in His Book in His saying:
{And God certainly gave you victory at Badr while you were humiliated, so fear God that you may be grateful} [Al Imran: 123]

And in his saying: {And on the Day of Hunayn, when I astonished you by your multitude, but it was of no avail to you at all, and the earth became too narrow for you because of its spaciousness. Then you turned back. Reversing} [Al-Tawbah: 25] (25) {Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down armies that you did not see} [Al-Tawbah: 26]. . .

Even some of the most famous imams of Fatwa and his friend said to him when he denied him the request to follow: Be silent, otherwise I will ask you in front of the people: Whichever it was before, Badr or Uhud, I know that you do not know it. Although it is among the recurring reports that no one who has the slightest knowledge of the news would doubt about, that Uhud was defeated after Badr, and at Badr he was victorious. Muslims against the infidels, and on the day of Uhud the infidels demonstrated.

Indeed, many of the great Muslim scholars do not know what is frequent among the People of the Book, and even among other Muslim scholars. Such as the destruction of the Holy House twice, and the coming of Nasr’s ship to the Holy House, and God Almighty has mentioned both times in the Qur’an, saying:

{And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Book that you will certainly spread corruption in the land twice and that you will declare great exaltation} [Al-Isra: 4] (4) {So when the promise of the first of them came to pass. We sent against you servants of Ours who were endowed with great might, so they spied through the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled.} [Al-Isra: 5] (5) {Then We returned the attack to you upon them. And We have provided you with wealth and children, and made you more numerous in army.} [Al-Isra: 6] (6) {If you do good, you do good to yourselves, but if you do evil, it is yours. Then when the promise of the Hereafter comes, they will disdain your countenance and enter the mosque as they entered it the first time, and they will completely disavow what they have risen above.} [Al-Isra: 7]
It was the first after Solomon, and it was the second after Zechariah, Yahya, and Christ, when they killed Yahya bin Zakariya, whom the people of The book of John the Baptist.

Many of those mentioned in knowledge believe that Bakht Nasr was the one who came to the Levant when Yahya ibn Zakariya was killed, and this is according to the people of Knowledge from the People of the Book, and from those who have experience among the Muslim scholars, is false, and what is frequently reported is that (Bakht-e Nasr) was the one who came forward at one time. The first, and also the fact that Shuaib the Prophet was the father-in-law of Moses, peace be upon him, as a group of ignorant people say, and what is widely reported among the People of the Book, According to the Muslims, including the Companions, the Followers, and others, there is a different opinion of that, and according to the Christians, from their news and the news of their scholars and kings. Mutawatir is something that Muslims and Jews do not know, and when
The Muslims, from the repeated reports of their scholars and kings, are something that most nations do not know.

Rather, every sect of Muslims has the circulating news of their sheikhs, their princes, and their countries, unless it is heard from others, and this is not the case. In the same position as someone who claimed news that was not known to those who witnessed that case, as if an accuser claimed that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed Hajj after... The migration was more than one Hajj, and that he used to fast the month of Ramadan in Mecca, and that there was a call to prayer in Mecca or that he was among his soldiers, And the armies of his caliphs were bears and trumpets, or he used to give the call to prayer for the two Eids, or he used to deliver the sermon for the two Eids before the prayer, or he used to pray In Medina on more than one Eid, or that he prayed four times while traveling, or that he prayed the Eid al-Sacrifice prayer in Mina, or that he stated that Ali ibn Abu Talib, may God be pleased with him, or someone else, declared the caliphate clearly and well-known, or that he removed Abu Bakr from the emirate in the Hujjah and appointed him Ali, or that someone other than Abu Bakr prayed during his death illness, and other such reports that are known to be false and false due to the frequent occurrence of
Its opposite, and because if it were true, it would be something that there were aspirations and reasons to transmit and make known, even though he did not have it. Mention in ancient times.

Likewise, what many ignorant people transmit, such as what they make of the miracles of the Messenger or someone else, and there is no narration from The people of knowledge about its circumstances, rather they deny its transmitter, as many of the common people say:

The clouds always shaded him. This is not found in any of the books of the Muslims known to their scholars, nor was it transmitted by any of their scholars. Rather, it is a lie according to them, even if many people narrate it. Rather, it was narrated that a cloud shaded him when he was young and he came with his uncle. He went to the Levant as a merchant, and the monk Bahira saw him. However, this does not confirm its authenticity, nor does some of them say that it was If he stepped on the stone or the sand, it had no effect. This was not narrated by the people of knowledge about its circumstances, not one of them. Rather, it is Lying to him.

The same applies to what a group of people narrate about the large number of killings in his wars, or the many battles the likes of which the author of the book mentions. He called it “Naqlāt al-Anwār” and it is called al-Bakri, since most of these are not found in the known books of the Muslims, nor were they transmitted. Their scholars, in fact, there have been reports that contradict it, and it is an obvious lie according to the people of knowledge of its circumstances, even if many of the people are ignorant. In his circumstances, he may believe it.
And similar to what a group narrates is that in the Battle of Khaybar, Ali bin Abi Talib set up his hand to force the army to pass over it, and that the mule He passed by her and said:

God cut off your lineage, so her lineage was cut off. This is not in any of the books of the people of knowledge about its circumstances, and not one of them reported that. This is only reported by someone who is known to lie or is ignorant, and for this reason this is a lie that scholars condemn as a lie. Muslims, and they know that its opposite has been frequent, and that there was not a single mule in the Battle of Khaybar, and it was neither in Medina nor in Mecca. A mule, except for his mule, which was given to him by Al-Muqawqis the Christian, King of Egypt and Alexandria, but he gave it to him after the conquest of Khaybar when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to

The kings of the Taifas calling them to Islam, and he only sent to the kings of the Taifas after Al-Hudaybiyyah and Khaybar when he returned from Khaybar, and they know The mule is still cut off and has never had any offspring.

Likewise, what some liars narrate is that a group of the Ahl al-Bayt were taken captive, so they rode a camel and two humps grew on it, and that it Al-Bukhati, this is what those who know the news have agreed is a lie. Muslims have never insulted anyone at any time. From the family of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, neither during the caliphate of the Umayyads, nor during the caliphate of the Abbasids, and the Bukhati camels are still like this. Her hump was not renewed in Islam, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when he mentioned what would happen to women after him. He said:
“On their heads are like the humps of a camel.”

Likewise, what was reported by a group of scholars that the sun rose when Ali missed the afternoon prayer because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell asleep. In his lap, and some of them considered this to be one of the miracles, and this hadith is not in any of the books of the Muslims that they rely on what is in it. movables,

Neither the Sahihs, nor the Musnads, nor the battles and biographies, nor anything else. Rather, the people of knowledge of the hadith have made it clear that this is a lie, and it has no chain of transmission. One, authentic and connected, but its purpose is to be narrated from someone whose truthfulness is not known, and no one narrated it except him, with the determination and reasons to narrate it. So they knew that it was a lie, and this is a broad chapter that shows that Muslim scholars distinguish between the narrations between truth and lies, so they reject the lie. Even if it contains some of the virtues of their Prophet and his notables and the virtues of his companions and his nation, which are great, and they accept honesty even if it is in it. A suspicion of confusion, and those who dispute them may use it as evidence.
Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi used to say: The people of knowledge write down what is theirs and what is owed to them, and the people of desires only write down what they have. To them.

Among these are the battles of Hamzah, which are common among many ignorant Turks and others. It is not found in any of the books of knowledge, but rather it was repeated among the people of Knowing that Hamzah did not witness a battle except the Battle of Badr and then the Battle of Uhud, and he was killed on the day of Uhud as a martyr. Wahshi bin Harb killed him. This is widely reported among the people of knowledge, and none of these verses were in the Sahih, and even many of them were not narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim, so these Its generality is such that the scholars of hadith are certain of its authenticity, and they are certain of that, and this according to them is extensive and frequent, although some This may not be frequent and widespread among others, as news may be frequent and widespread among a people without another, according to their attention. with it, and their request for it, and their knowledge of those who reported it, and their characteristics, and their amounts, and what evidence indicated their truthfulness, and the people of knowledge With the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, his actions, his biography, the reasons for the revelation of the Qur’an, its meanings, and other than that, they have this knowledge. They have such certainty in it that no one else has the like of it, just as the companions of Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Abu Hanifa, Dawud, and others, according to each sect, has some of the sayings, texts, and narrations of its follower that they trust, even if it is other than them. This is not known, and the doctors according to them are based on the words of Hippocrates, Galen, and Muhammad ibn

Zakariya and others like them are not certain about it, and others do not know that, and the people of the organization have it from the words of Ptolemy, and the observation Al-Mukhtaseen Al-Mamouni, Thabit bin Qurrah, and Abu Al-Hussein Al-Sufi what they themselves know, and others do not know that to the point that one is certain. These and those adhere to many of the schools of thought of medicine and arithmetic, the experiences of doctors, and the observations of arithmeticians, and others do not know. That.

Among the People of the Book, such as the Jews, there is information about Hilal, Samabi, and other of their sheikhs that no one else knows, and among the Christians there is News of the Apostles, and of Constantine, and the First Council of Nicene, and the Second, Third, Fourth, and Fifth Councils, And other than that from their councils, and their narrations are what their scholars are unanimously agreed upon, even if others do not know that.

The people of knowledge of the days of Islam know from the biography of Abu Bakr, Omar, and Othman, and their battles such as the battle of Ajnadin and Marj al-Safar. And others regarding the caliphate of Abu Bakr, and the battle of Yarmouk, and the news of Abu Ubaidah and the defeat of the Persians, and the conquest of Egypt, and other things that were In the time of Omar ibn al-Khattab, they were not certain of that, even if others did not know that.

The same applies to what happened after these, regarding the biographies of kings and events of existence. Rather, people with knowledge of men know of the condition of some of the Companions. And the followers and those after them, such as Abdullah bin Omar, Ibn Abbas, Abu Saeed, Abu Hurairah, Abdullah bin Masoud, and Anas bin Malik, Ubayy bin Ka’b, Muadh bin Jabal, Sa’id bin Al-Musayyab, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Alqamah, Al-Aswad, and others. No one else knows it.
And the people of knowledge of grammar know about the condition of Sibawayh, Al-Akhfash, Al-Muradid, Al-Zajjaj, Al-Fur’ and Al-Kisa’i, which he does not know. Other than them.
The readers know from the reading of Abu Amr, Ibn Kathir, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, Ibn Amir, Ya’qub bin Ishaq, and Al-A’mash. Ibn Hisham and Abu Ja`far left behind something that no one else knows.

If one of the scholars is one of the scholars of jurisprudence, medicine, arithmetic, grammar, or recitations, and even one of the kings teaches the elite... Among their affairs are what no one else knows and they are devoid of that, so how about one who, according to his followers, is higher in status than every scholar, and of a higher status? Of every king, they are the most desirous of people to know his conditions, and the greatest seeker of truth in them, and of repelling lies from them, to the point that they have compiled books. There is a lot in the news of everyone who narrated some of his news, and in it they mentioned the circumstances of the transmission of his hadith, and the wounds related to that. And they modified it, and they investigated that, and they exaggerated to an extent the likes of which has not been found for any of the nations, nor for any of this nation except the people of Hadith, this indicates that they are more knowledgeable about the condition of their Prophet than everyone and the condition of those who follow them, and that they are more knowledgeable about the truthfulness of the transmitter and his lie than anyone else. Everyone is truthful and untruthful to someone who reported on the authority of their followers.

If those who are narrating it from those who follow them agree on it and are certain that it is nothing but the truth, then they are certain of it. With the truth, and their agreement on the truth indicates that what they are certain of is true is nothing but truth.

In general, the narrations of the two Sahih books are those that the scholars of hadith agreed to believe in, and they were certain of that. However, they disputed over a few of the hadiths, In general, the verses of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that we have mentioned, which are in the Sahihs, are from the sources of their extensive consensus on which they affirm With its sincerity, it is not a source of their dispute. This is a path taken by those of the scholars who know it, and the best of its people knows those who are experts. Therefore, there are two ways of attesting these verses: the general frequency, and the specific frequency.
The third way:

Moral frequency, and this is what all sects have agreed upon, as people may hear separate news with stories that share common All of them in one matter, just as they heard various news that included the courage of Antarah, Khalid bin Al-Walid, and their likes, and included Sakha’ Hatim and Ma’an ibn Zaydah, and their likes, and it includes the dream of Al-Ahnaf ibn Qais, Mu’awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and their likes, It includes the poetry of Imru’ al-Qais, al-Nabigha, Labid, and similar predecessors, and the poetry of al-Farazdaq, Jarir, and Omar ibn Abi Rabi’ah. And their likes are among the Mawlids, and the poetry of Abu Nuwas, Al-Mutanabbi, and Abu Tammam, and their likes are among the hadith scholars, and they even heard sayings and fatwas Miscellaneous and includes the jurisprudence of Malik, Al-Thawri, Al-Layth bin Saad, Abu Hanifa, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad bin Hanbal, and Ishaq bin Rahawayh, and other scholars, and various reports including justice and good conduct from Umar ibn

Al-Khattab, Omar bin Abdul Aziz, and other rulers, and they heard various news that included abstaining from the example of Al-Hasan. Al-Basri, Al-Fudayl ibn Ayadh, Malik ibn Dinar, Ibrahim ibn Adham, and other ascetics, and they heard various news including The knowledge of medicine by Hippocrates, Galen, and the like, and from the totality of the information one obtains a necessary knowledge that the person is described with that. The epithet, even if each of the reports were isolated alone would not benefit knowledge, even if each of the stories was not transmitted alone. Frequently.

In this regard, there is the definite knowledge of faith and death, and other things through which the integrity of the premise of definite knowledge is achieved, such as the knowledge of people. That Khadija, Aisha, and the like are among the mothers of the believers, and that Fatima and Zainab are among the daughters of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that Aisha The daughter of Abu Bakr, and that Abu Bakr, Omar, and Uthman took over the caliphate after him, and that Abu Bakr and Omar were buried in his room, and when This is known, and these hadiths, many times as many as are narrated from any one of these, and I narrated them for the sake of Allah. It is more and better than the narration of the news of these people, which is complete and includes that Muhammad bin Abdullah, may God bless him and grant him peace, was going on... His hands contain extraordinary signs and great wonders, the likes of which are not known from anyone, and the Muslims’ knowledge of this is greater than The knowledge of the People of the Book about what they transmit of the verses of Moses, Jesus, and others. The transmission of verses of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, other than the Qur’an, is many times greater. Multiplying the transmission of the Torah and the Gospel, in addition to other reports of the prophets, as not all of the Torah was preserved for all the children of Israel is the same way that most Muslims memorize the Qur’an, and when the Holy House was destroyed, there were very few people who memorized it, to the point that people frequently quarreled. Transfer it

Likewise, the transmission of the Gospel is much less than the transmission of the verses of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And if the Christians said, “These were righteous.” And they had signs for them, as they mentioned among the signs of the disciples. For the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who followed them were righteous, and for them were signs. Greater than that of the disciples and other nations, and among them were those who carried the army on water, and those who drank deadly poisons, and those God revives the dead by His call, and whoever eats and drinks in abundance, and the signs of the good deeds of the saints therein are greater than what the people of The Book, and they transmit the news of the prophets and the righteous from books they have, such as the Book of the Disciples’ Chronicles, and the Book of Travel Kings, and the like, and no proof they cite regarding the validity of its transmission except the argument of the Muslims regarding what they transmit from their Prophet and his companions. The followers are more prominent and stronger.

The fourth way: That it may be said: These verses, some of which we have mentioned, were in the presence of many people, like the abundance of food on the Day of the Trench. For the people of Khandaq, their men and women, were in their thousands.

And likewise the spring of water from between his fingers, and the well overflowing with water on the Day of Hudaybiyyah, and they were one thousand five hundred on that day. They are all righteous people of Paradise, and no one among them is known to have deliberately told a single lie about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

Likewise, there was an abundance of water and food. In the Battle of Khaybar they were one thousand five hundred, and in Tabuk they were thousands upon thousands, and some of those who attended These scenes. He conveyed these verses in front of others who attended them, and conveyed them to people, and those people went and reported them. Those, and some of them believe one another, and he narrates this as he narrated this, without collusion or sympathy. The minimum condition for him is for him to acknowledge it and not He is denied narrating it, and we know that it is based on the innate custom that God created His servants with, and based on what the nation’s ancestors were upon. From their belief in honesty and their pursuit of it, and their belief that this is obligatory, and from their extreme avoidance of lying to their Prophet, and their veneration of that, as it has It was frequently reported that he said:
“Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in the Fire.”

We know that they did not acknowledge the one whom they knew was lying to him, and the one who told about him what they were witnessing, and he lied. They knew that he had lied to him, so when they agreed to acknowledge that, and to circulate it among them without any of them denying that, It is known for sure that the people were agreed on transmitting that, just as they agreed on transmitting the Qur’an and the Mutawatir Sharia, even if Their audience is not ready to teach the Qur’an. Rather, this one teaches it and this one hears it from this indoctrinated person. They do not deny each other. Reading, and this teaches this prayer:

The noon prayer in urban areas is four rak’ahs, the sunset is three rak’ahs, and the dawn is two rak’ahs, and this confirms this, since some of them used to confirm others on The transmission of that is known to be their agreement on the transmission of that, and this is the purpose of tawātur.

Likewise, what they transmitted of His laws, His verses, and His proofs, this shows that what some of them rejected, they denied to others, and they did not reject it. He agrees with him, and if they were later than the time of the Companions, then what about the predecessors, such as their dispute over whether he used to say the basmalah out loud or not?

Did he always recite Qunoot at dawn, or did he recite Qunoot sometimes for calamities, or did he recite Qunoot once and then abandon it? This is one of the easiest matters. And the easiest of them, since they all agreed on the validity of the prayer of the one who recited Qunoot, and on the validity of the prayer of the one who did not recite the Qunoot, the one who recited loudly, and the one who recited it in prayer, but since they disagreed Concerning what the Messenger did, they disputed over the ruling, and it was known from that that what was known among the nation about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and no one denied it. Of its scholars, the nation was unanimous in transmitting it just as they transmit the Qur’an and the apparent laws.

And the narration of that is greater than the narration of all other narrations of the prophets, scholars, kings, and ascetics, and so is his Hajj. They all agree on what has been reported about him, that he only performed one Hajj after the Hijrah, which is called the Farewell Hajj. He only lived after that for about three months, and when he performed Hajj, he commanded all of his companions, except for those of them who brought the sacrificial animal when he circumambulated. In the House and between Safa and Marwah, he is permitted to perform Umrah, and that neither he nor any of his companions who performed Hajj with him performed Umrah after the Hajj. Except for Aisha alone, and he himself did not complete his Hajj, nor did anyone who brought the sacrificial animal with him, but some of them became suspicious. Some of his words or some matters that are hidden from most people, and the Companions used to convey the enjoyment of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, What they meant by tamattu’ is that he combined Umrah and Hajj, so some people thought that they meant that he delayed ihram for Hajj until he had completed Umrah, and some of the companions said:

He was singled out for Hajj, so some people thought that he had performed Hajj, and he performed Umrah after Hajj. This was not transmitted by any of the scholars, rather they agreed on He did not perform Umrah after Hajj, and some of the Companions narrated that he performed the Qaraan, so some people thought that he circumambulated two times and did two sa’ys, and this was not the case. Someone quotes it from him, and one of the reasons why many people made a mistake was that they used those words in meanings other than what I used them. The Companions were involved in it, so some people made a mistake about some of the Companions, and as for what he did during Hajj that was well-known, it is

Mutawatir, on which the transmission and transmission scholars do not disagree, and whoever ponders this path will benefit from certain, definitive knowledge of the authenticity of these verses. On the authority of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as well as the previous methods. We have mentioned that what people are most in need of knowing, may God facilitate. His guidance to people is greater than the facilitation of anything else, and the need of people to believe the Messenger is greater than their need for all things, since by that Their happiness will be achieved in the Hereafter, and they will be saved from torment, and through it the righteousness of the servants will be attained in the Hereafter and their livelihood. The fifth path:

There is no type of scholar without a sufficient number of verses occurring among them, so the books of interpretation are full of mention. The verses are frequently mentioned in them, and the books of hadith are full of mention of the verses in them, and the books of biographies, mysteries, and histories It is full of frequent mention of verses, and the books of jurisprudence are full of frequent mention of verses, even if this is not the case. What is intended from them, and what is intended is the rulings, but within what they narrate of the rulings, they narrate in them signs that are It is frequent among them, and the books of principles and theology are full of mention of verses in them, and the narration of each of these groups Certain knowledge is beneficial, so what about what each of these sects transmits, and this path and others such as the path of acknowledgment and ratification, The path of moral frequency, and the path of the people of knowledge believing in the hadith, and other than that, is sometimes used as evidence of the frequency of the general type. For the extraordinary verses, and this is the least of them, and this is evidenced by the frequency of every kind of them, such as the frequency of eating a lot of food, and the frequency of Frequent purification

And drink, and the frequency of one type of it, such as the frequency of a spring of water from between its fingers, and the frequency of satisfying the great creation with food. A little, and the frequency of each person’s occurrence of it, such as the frequency of a trunk’s longing for it, and the like, and the more a person looks closely at that, He considered this with examples like it, and he considered it and gave him his due consideration and reasoning. This increased his knowledge and certainty, and it became clear to him that Knowledge of this is more evident than anything that is required of knowledge of recurrent narrations, for there is no knowledge in this world that is required of narrations. The condition of any of the prophets, kings, and scholars is more evident than that. And the previous sheikhs, his sayings, his actions, and his biography, except that knowledge of the conditions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is more apparent than knowledge. With it, there is no knowledge that is known with the continuity of what exists now like the knowledge of distant lands like the knowledge of the people of the Levant in Iraq and Khorasan. And India, China, and Andalusia, and the knowledge of the people of the Maghreb about the Levant, and Iraq, Khorasan, and India, and the knowledge of the people of Khorasan about the Levant. And Iraq and Egypt, and the knowledge of the people of India about Iraq and the Levant, and similar things such as the knowledge of the people of the country about each other’s condition, except that they know Man is in the condition of Muslims from the east and west of the earth, and the religion they follow, and the verses they transmit from their Prophet. His laws are more evident than his knowledge of all this.

This is what makes it clear that there is nothing in existence that is known through recurrent narrations, except that the verses of the Messenger and his laws are known through recurrent narrations. Greater than what is known. This matter is in fulfillment of the Almighty’s saying: {It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religions. And Allah is sufficient as a witness.} [Al-Fath: 28]

Its emergence over the entire religion through knowledge, argument, and explanation is only through what it reveals of its signs and proofs, and that is only accomplished. With knowledge of what is transmitted from Muhammad of his verses, which are the evidence, and his laws, which are the meaning intended by the evidence, this may God made him appear in knowledge, proof, and clarification over every religion, just as He made him appear in strength, victory, and support over every religion, and praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.
Just as there is no evidence that can be used to indicate a meaning except that the evidence for the signs of the Lord is greater and more numerous.
Sixth way:

The scholars have compiled many works mentioning its verses and proofs transmitted in the reports, and for this they have prepared books such as the book Evidence of prophecy by the jurist and memorizer Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi, and before that evidence of prophecy by Sheikh Abu Nu’aym al-Asbahani, and before that evidence Prophethood by Abu Sheikh Al-Asbahani, and by Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani, and before them, Evidence of Prophethood by Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Zar’ah Al-Razi, And the sheikh and author, Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Abi Al-Dunya, and the author and memorizer, Imam Abu Ishaq Ibrahim Al-Harbi, and Abu Bakr Jaafar Al-Faryabi, and what the scholarly sheikh Abu Al-Faraj Ibn Al-Jawzi classified in his book called Al-Wafa fi the virtues of the Chosen One, and what he classified. Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah Al-Maqdisi is one of the evidences of prophecy, and these and others mention what they mention of well-known chains of transmission and methods. Multiple, frequent, frequent.

These are among them who distinguish the hadiths they mention between what is in Sahih Al-Bukhari and Muslim, and what is in other than them, even if it is also authentic. Such as Al-Bayhaqi, Ibn Al-Jawzi, and Al-Maqdisi, and among them are those who mention all of this with its chains of transmission, and he may speak about the chains of transmission and methods. He mentions its multiple occurrences without needing to mention what was narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim, such as Abu Zar’ah, Sheikh Muslim, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Abu Naim, and others, and others mention it attributed to the one who narrated it, even if they do not mention its chain of transmission, as Judge Iyad al-Sabti does in His book, called Al-Shifa, defines the rights of the Chosen One, and some of them confirm that through the fame of it and other methods of its authenticity, just as he does it. Many of the theorists, such as Judge Abdul-Jabbar

Al-Jahiz, Al-Mawardi Al-Qadi, Sulaym Al-Razi Al-Faqih, and others, and these books contain hadiths containing the signs of his prophecy. The proofs of his message are many times greater than the hadiths that are transmitted from him, such as the Farewell Pilgrimage, the Umrah of Al-Hudaybiyyah, and the Sad His polytheists, and his reconciliation with them, and his resolution with his companions to Hudaybiyyah, and their return that year, and the conquest of Khaybar, and Umrah The case, and Umrah Al-Jiranah.

Such as his siege of the people of Taif, and his conquest of Mecca before that, and such as his invasion of the Christians in the year of Tabuk, and his sending an army to invade them. In Mu'tah on the outskirts of the Levant, close to the fort called Karak, and similar to his invasion of the Jews at Khaybar, and his invasion of the Jews before that For those who were near Medina, such as the Banu Qaynuqa’, al-Nadir, and Qurayzah, and for example, he sent Abu Bakr as the commander of the Hajj in the year nine, And his abandonment of covenants, and his call that “no polytheist shall perform Hajj after the year, nor circumambulate the Kaaba naked,” and such as his migration with Abu Bakr. Amer bin Fuhayra and a third man who was their guide.

And just as it was reported that he used to lead the Muslims in prayer on the two Eids in the prayer hall outside the city, he would not pray the Eid in his mosque except Once it was reported that he prayed in the mosque because of the rain, and during his reign no one in the city would lead the Eid prayer except for his successor, who would not pray. My prayer is an Eid during his reign and the reign of Abu Bakr, Omar, and Uthman, and the first to do that was Ali bin Abi Talib, when the people were numerous and the peoples were weak. When he went out into the desert, he left behind those who would lead them in prayer in the mosque.

It was also narrated that he used to pray Friday prayers with the call to prayer and the iqamah, which were not called for unless he sat on the pulpit, and this was the case. During the reign of Abu Bakr and Omar, when there were many people during the Caliphate of Uthman, he ordered the third call to be made in a house close to the mosque on the other side. The East is called Al-Zawra, and it is also reported that his mosque was made of mud, its roof was made of palm trunks, and it was the stone of his wives. Before and to the east of the mosque, when the people increased, Omar increased it, then Othman increased it, and built it with plaster and stones, then in the Walid emirate He ordered his deputy, Omar bin Abdul Aziz, to buy the stone and add it to the mosque, so she entered Aisha’s room, in which he was buried. Abu Bakr and Omar were in the mosque from that time, but during his lifetime she was away from the mosque until the year ninety-one, and he said in His death illness:

“May God curse the Jews and Christians who used the graves of their prophets as places of worship. He warns against what they did. Aisha said: Had it not been for that, his grave would have been exposed, but he disliked it being used as a mosque.

It was also reported that he forbade prayer at the time of sunrise and at sunset, and it was reported that he used to sacrifice on Eid al-Adha. Rather, it has been reported on the authority of people of knowledge regarding his famous circumstances, just as his famous deeds have been reported on the authority of the people of knowledge, so it has been reported that he did not He would not give the call to prayer for the two Eids, the eclipse, or rain rain, and he prayed the eclipse with two bows in each rakah, a long prayer, and it was frequently reported that he He circumambulated the House seven times, and prayed two rak'ahs after the circumambulation. He did not pray two rak'ahs after the Sa'i at Safa and Marwah, and it was reported that he He continues, and his companions forbade the connection, and he says:

“I am not like you. I spend the night with my Lord, and He feeds me and gives me drink.” And he did not impose any fasting except the fasting of the month of Ramadan, and he did not He made Hajj obligatory on those who are able except once, and he made the five daily prayers obligatory on every sane adult except menstruating women and postpartum women, and he forbade menstruating women from performing Hajj. The postpartum period is a result of fasting and prayer, and menstruating women were ordered to make up for the fast, but they were not ordered to make up for the prayer.

And he commanded performing ablution in the case of ritual impurity for prayer, and he commanded ablution at the time of prayer for anyone who has urinated, defecated, or has had a wind or odor. Madhi, and that he permitted cleaning oneself with three stones, forbade cleansing oneself with an oath, and forbade cleaning oneself with a bone. And the camel, and he said:

“Indeed, it is an addition to your brothers from the jinn” “And that he did not bring the Muslims together to hear the palm of the hand, nor the drum, nor dancing, nor squealing, neither he nor His companions when they heard the Qur’an. Rather, their hearts ached, their skins shivered, and their eyes shed tears, and because he was not in his covenant. During the reign of his successors, a divorced woman would be returned to her husband in a marriage that was intended to be permissible. Rather, he cursed the one who was promiscuous and the one for whom the person is permissible because this might It was done secretly.

And that he was ordered to visit the sick, and to hold the funeral, and to extend the greeting, and to respond to the supplication, and that he used to pray over the dead and say “Allahu Akbar.” He said four takbeers, and sometimes he used to say takbeers five or seven, and he ordered the dead to be washed and shrouded, and to pray over him and bury him, and that He forbade every intoxicant, and forbade selling a dirham for two dirhams, a dinar for two dinars, and a saa’ for two saa’s of wheat, barley, dates, and raisins. And he commanded the payment of zakat al-fitr as a saa’ of dates or a saa’ of barley when the people of Medina ate dates and barley, and he permitted medicine. And he said:
“Seek treatment, servants of God, for no disease has descended without a cure being sent down for it, except for the poison.” “And the poison.”

Death, and that he was treated with cupping and other things, as well as the hadiths that were transmitted about him, other than what is in the Qur’an regarding the description of Paradise. And the fire, and the mention of the throne and the angels and the jinn, and his sending to the two heavy creatures, and what he mentioned of the names of God, and His attributes, and what he informed of. From the temptation of a person in his grave, from the torment and bliss of the grave, and from the entry and exit of those of his nation who enter Hellfire From the Fire due to his intercession, and the intercession of others, and from the mention of his basin, and what he was informed of of seeing God on the Day of Resurrection, and being held accountable to God. For the servants, and other than that.

What has been reported from him is that he used to send messengers to the kings calling on them to believe in God and in what He brought, just as he was sent to the kings of Yemen, and to the kings of the Levant, Egypt, and Iraq, and to the kings of the polytheists, the Jews, the Christians, and the Magians, after he once fought the Jews. After one time, and what has been reported repeatedly is that he used to ride horses, camels, mules and donkeys, and that he stoned the married adulterer once after Once, he cut off the hand of a thief, flogged a drinker, and that he used to pray four rak'ahs during travel, two rak'ahs, and that he combined the two prayers. He performed the noon and afternoon prayers at Arafat, and in Muzdalifah he combined the sunset and the evening prayers, and he used to pray two rak’ahs in Mina, and he ordered

During the Farewell Pilgrimage, Muslims must exit their ihram and make it an Umrah, except for the one who brings the sacrificial animal, for he has commanded him to remain in the state of Umrah. His ihram, and that he did not exit ihram from his ihram, nor did he perform Umrah after Hajj. Neither he nor anyone of those who performed Hajj with him except Aisha, because she was She was menstruating, and the month of Ramadan was imposed in the second year of the Hijra, so he fasted nine Ramadans.

And that he had four daughters and three sons, and his eldest son’s nickname was Al-Qasim, so he was called Abu Al-Qasim, and that he married my two daughters. Abu Bakr and Omar, and Uthman gave his two daughters in marriage, and he married Ali a daughter, and that his uncles Hamza and Abbas believed in him, and Abu did not believe in him. Lahab, nor Abu Talib, even though Abu Talib used to protect him and protect him, and he appointed Abu Bakr as his successor to lead the people in prayer when he became ill. And he was unable to pray. No one prayed with his permission in his presence except Abu Bakr during his illness, and when he went to reconcile the Banu Amr bin Awf. And that among the elite of his ten companions were Abu Bakr, Omar, Uthman, Ali, Talha, Al-Zubayr, and Saad bin

Abu Waqqas, Saeed bin Zaid, Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah, Abdul Rahman bin Awf, and others like Abdullah bin Masoud, And Ubayy bin Kaab, and Muadh bin Jabal, and Saad bin Muadh, and Saad bin Ubadah, and Abu Talha, and Abu Ayyub, and Usayd bin Hudayr, And many times more than these, and that one thousand and four hundred pledged their allegiance to him under the tree, and they are the ones about whom God revealed: {Indeed, God is pleased with The believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree} [Al-Fath: 18]

And when he came to Medina, he built his mosque, and there was a row to the north of it where single women could stay, and that all the Muhajireen and Ansar They converted to Islam voluntarily, without desire or fear, and the immigrants were greatly harmed by the infidels until a group of them migrated to Abyssinia when Al-Najashi, and that Al-Najashi believed in him, and that when he died, he informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of his death on the day he died, and that he prayed over him. with his companions in the prayer place just as he prays for the dead who are present, and that he used to deliver the sermon on Friday before the prayer, and he would deliver the sermon on the Eid after the prayer. He used to give the call to prayer and the five daily prayers, but he did not give the call to prayer for the two Eids, or anything other than the five daily prayers. Bilal used to give the call to prayer for him in Medina. He and Ibn Umm Maktoum were blind, and Sa`d al-Qarth used to give the call to prayer to the people of Quba, and Abu Mahdhurah used to give the call to prayer to the people of Mecca, and as has been reported on the authority of On his authority and on the authority of his successors

They were not in Mina praying the Eid prayer, but rather they stoned Jamarat al-Aqaba and sacrificed, as he commanded the people of the cities to pray and then sacrifice, to parables. These matters are among the things that are frequent among everyone who knows their circumstances, and some of them are common among the entire nation.

Among them are those that are widely accepted by the majority of them, and there is none of them except that their verses and proofs, may God bless him and grant him peace, have been repeated in them, which have not been More than these matters are mentioned in the Qur’an more than once, and the books that contain its verses and proofs that are outside the Qur’an include The hadiths are many times as many as there are hadiths on such matters. Rather, in every type of its verses there are many times as many hadiths. Examples of this include the frequency of telling him about future unseen, the frequency of his eating and drinking a lot of food and drink many times, and his Purification is either by a spring of water between his fingers, or by the overflow of the spring in which he places some of his traces, or
By the overflow of water from the vessel in which it was poured, while the water remains as it was and has not diminished.

The repeated hadiths in these types are more than the repeated hadiths in such matters that are frequent. For this reason, the fame of these matters among the nation and among the people of knowledge about his conditions is greater than the fame of many of those matters. What is meant here is that the frequency of his extensive verses in hadiths is greater than the frequency of many matters that are frequent among the nation or among Its scholars and the scholars of Ahl al-Hadith, and this is other than the verses and proofs learned from the Qur’an, for these have been stripped of groups of The Muslims mentioned its types and characteristics that are not explained in other than this place, until they explained that the verses in the Qur’an increase On tens of thousands of verses, and this is not what is reported in the books of the People of the Book.

These three types are other than what is in his law with which he was sent, and other than the characteristics of his nation, and other than what is indicated by knowledge of his biography. And His morals, attributes, and conditions, and all of this is other than God’s victory and honor for those who believe in Him, and His punishment and vengeance on those who disbelieve in Him. As he did to the prophets of old, the enumeration of the specific evidence of prophecy is something that it is not possible for a human being to comprehend, since belief in it is obligatory. On every Sunday.

So God makes clear to every people, indeed to every person, signs and proofs that He does not make clear to other people, just as the signs and signs of divinity Greater and greater than any evidence for every signified, for every people, and even for every human being, than the specific signs that God shows him in himself and in Horizons are what other people do not know about. God Almighty said: {We will show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth} [Fussilat: 53]

The pronoun in that refers back to the Qur’an according to the commentators, the predecessors, and the general scholars, as the Qur’an indicates that by saying: {Say, “Have you considered that It was from God, then you disbelieved therein. Who is more astray than he who is in discord far away?} [Fussilat: 52] (52) {We will show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves until It becomes clear to them that it is the truth} [Fussilat: 53]. . .
It has been said: The conscience returns to God, and the first correct view is as He said: {Say: Have you considered if it was from God and then you disbelieved in it?} [Fussilat: 52]
This is the Qur’an. Then he said after that: {We will show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth} [Fussilat: 53]
Then he said: {Is it not sufficient that your Lord is a witness over all things?} [Fussilat: 53]

So he informed that he would show the people within themselves and on the horizons some concrete, well-known and intelligible verses that would show that the Qur’anic verses What is recited is true, so the mind and hearing coincide, the eyes and the Qur’an agree, and the sight confirms the information.

If the Qur’an is true, it is necessary that the Messenger who brought it be truthful, and that God Almighty sent it down, and that what he informed must be believed. with it, and obedience to what He has made obligatory and commanded, and this includes proving the Creator, his monotheism, his names and attributes, and confirming the prophecies, And the confirmation of the Day of Resurrection, and these are the foundations of knowledge and faith on which happiness and salvation are linked.

chapters.title: Detailing Qur’anic evidence for the coming of the messengers with signs
paragraphs: [Chapter: Qur’anic evidence for the coming of the messengers with signs]

The signs and proofs of prophecy occur during the lifetime of the Messenger and before his birth, and after his death they are not specific to his lifetime. It is specific to the situation of the claim to prophecy or the situation of challenge, as some theologians thought. Rather, there must be signs in his life that indicate his sincerity. It is the proof, and the proof is evident from it, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in the authentic hadith: “There is no prophet among the prophets except that he has been given Of the signs, no human being has believed the like of it. Rather, what I was given was a revelation that God revealed to me. I hope that I will be most of them in following on the Day of Resurrection.” And God Almighty said in Surah Ibrahim:
{This is a Book which We have sent down to you so that you may bring people out of darkness into light, by the permission of their Lord, to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy} [Ibrahim: 1]

To his saying: {And We sent Moses with Our signs to bring your people out of darkness into light and remind them of the days of God. Indeed, in that “Signs for every patient and grateful person.” [Ibrahim: 5]

To his saying: {Has there not come to you the news of those before you, the people of Noah and Ad and Thamud, and of those after them no one knows except God? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they put their hands in their mouths and said, “Indeed, we disbelieve in what you were sent with, and we are in doubt as to what you call us to.” one who returns to Him} [Ibrahim: 9] (9) {Their messengers said, “Is there any doubt in God that the Creator of the heavens and the earth invites you to forgive you of your sins and give you respite? For an appointed time} [Ibrahim: 10]

The verses, so Glory be to Him informed that the people of Noah, Ad, Thamud, and those after them - no one knows except God - their messengers had given them clear proofs. So he knew that they had brought clear proofs, and he said: {Then if they deny you, then have been denied messengers before you. They brought clear proofs and the Psalms and the Book that enlightens} [Al-Bukhari and Muslim] Imran: 184]

And God Almighty said: {And the people of Noah, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them and made them a sign for mankind, and We prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment} [Al-Furqan: 37] (37) {And Aad, and Thamud, and the Companions of the Rass, and many centuries between that} [Al-Furqan: 38] (38) {And for each of them We have given parables, and for each of them We have purified Himself with purity} [Al-Furqan: 39]

Then He informed that God, Glory be to Him, set examples for all those to whom He was sent and destroyed them, and did not punish them until after He The proof is upon them, and God Almighty said: {And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed; so ask the people of the Remembrance if you do not know} [An-Nahl: 43] (43) {With Clear Signs and Psalms, and We have sent down to you the Reminder that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them, and that they might reflect.} [An-Nahl: 44]

So He informed that He had not sent except men to whom He had revealed; He had not sent to them angels or women, and that He had sent them with clear proofs and the Psalms. Al-Zubur is the plural of Zabur, which are the Books, for among them was one to whom a Book was revealed, and among them was one who was sent to renew the Book that was before it, and he said God Almighty: {Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, and there is not a nation except that a warner has passed through it.} [Fatir: 24] (24) {And if they deny you, those of Before them, their messengers came to them with clear proofs, and with the Psalms, and with the Book of Enlightenment.} [Fatir: 25] (25) {Then I took those who disbelieved, so how reprehensible could He be?} [Fatir: 26]

He informed that there is not a nation among the nations except that a warner has passed through it, as He said: {And We have certainly sent into every nation a messenger, saying, “Worship God and avoid the tyrant.” And among them are those whom Allah has guided, and among them are those upon whom misguidance has certainty. So travel through the land and see what was the end of the deniers.} [An-Nahl: 36]

Then he informed that to those before them came their messengers with clear proofs and with the Psalms and the enlightening Book, and this is from the special sympathy for The general word is due to its specification as a specific description of it, such as His saying: {And His angels and His messengers and Gabriel and Michael} [Al-Baqarah: 98]. . . For the Psalms are among the clear proofs, and the enlightening Book is from the Psalms, and it is like His saying: {And among the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge, nor guidance, nor the Book. Enlightening} [Al-Hajj: 8]
For guidance is from knowledge, and the Book that enlightens is from guidance.

He made it clear that He seized those who disbelieved in them, and this He sent down to make clear the outcome of the disbelievers, and for this reason He built the verb to the subject, so He said: {He has He denied those before them.} [Fatir: 25]

This surah is Meccan. Then it was revealed about the family of Imran, which is Medinan, in the context of the verses that comfort the Messenger and those who believe in him, strengthen them, and console them for what He struck them as deniers on the day of Uhud and other days, and said: {Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the plague had befallen them - for those who did good. of them and fear a great reward} [Al Imran: 172] (172) {Those to whom the people said, “Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them.” It increased their faith, and they said, Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs} [Al Imran:

173] (173) {So they returned with a blessing from God and bounty. No harm touched them, and they followed the pleasure of God, and God is the Possessor of great bounty.} [Al Imran: 174] (174) {Indeed, it is Satan who intimidates his friends, so do not fear them, but fear if you are believers} [Al Imran: 175]
That is, his friends will frighten you, as said by the majority of scholars. Then he said: {And do not grieve you those who hasten in disbelief, for they will not harm God. Something} [Al Imran: 176]

The context of the speech is to explain that the unbelievers do not harm God or His faithful servants, but rather their harm is on themselves, and that what happened to them A blessing, but it was an induction and a dictation until he said: {God has certainly heard the words of those who said, “Indeed, God is poor, and we are rich. We will write down what They said, “And the prophets killed them unjustly. And We say, ‘Taste the torment of burning.’” [Al Imran: 181] (181) {That is for what your hands have put forward, and that God is not unjust. For slaves} [Al Imran:

182] (182) {Those who say, “Indeed, God has covenanted with us that we will not believe in a messenger until he brings us an offering that fire will consume.” Say, “Messengers have come to you before me.” With clear proofs and with what you said, so why did you kill them, if you were truthful?} [Al Imran: 183]

Glory be to Him has made it clear that this saying of theirs is a lie, so they did not say it except to push the truth, not to believe in those who brought that to them, since Messengers had come to them before him with clear signs and offerings that fire consumes, and yet they killed them, and speech like this The race that supports one another, and follows one another, like the Jews who follow the religion of their predecessors who did that, and for this reason He disparages them in the form of speech, such as His saying: {And when We parted the sea for you, so We saved you and drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were looking on} [Al-Baqarah: 50]
To his saying: {And when you said, “O Moses, we will never believe in you until we see God clearly” [Al-Baqarah: 55]

So the address is to the people of Israel, even if those who witnessed that died and then said: {Then if they deny you, then messengers before you have been denied, and they came With Clear Signs and Psalms and the Book of Enlightenment} [Al Imran: 184]

Here, he deleted the subject, and built the verb into the object, since the intention here is to entertain and console the Messenger, not to mention the punishment of the liars. Therefore, This one was more specific than that one.

chapters.title: A chapter from the signs of the prophets: God’s destruction of their deniers and His victory of those who believe in them
paragraphs: [Chapter: Among the signs of the prophets is God’s destruction of their deniers and His victory of those who believe in them]

Among the signs of the prophets is that God destroys their deniers and gives victory to those who believe in them. This is one of the signs of their prophecy and evidence of their truthfulness. Like God drowning the people of Noah when they denied him, and like God destroying the people of Aad with a roaring wind, and destroying the people of Salih with a cry, and destroying The people of Shuaib with shadows, and the destruction of the people of Lot by overthrowing their cities and stoning them with stones, and the destruction of the people of Pharaoh. By drowning, and God has mentioned the stories in the Qur’an in more than one place, and made clear that they are among the signs of the prophets indicating their truthfulness, as He mentions in Surat Ash-Shu'ara' when he mentioned the story of Moses, he said:
{Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers} [Al-Shu’ara’: 8]
Then he mentioned the story of Abraham, and said at the end of it: {Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers} [Al-Shu’ara’: 103]

Likewise, something like that was mentioned in the story of Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, and Shuaib, and that is what made it a common curse for those who He lied to them, and from the tongue of truthfulness, praise and supplication for them and for those who believed in them, as God Almighty said in the story of Noah: {And We left it upon him among the others} [Al-Saffat: 78] (78) {Peace be upon Noah in the worlds} [Al-Saffat: 79]
And likewise in the story of Abraham: {And We left him in charge of others} [Al-Saffat: 108] (108) {Peace be upon Abraham} [Al-Saffat: 109]
That is, we left this saying that the later ones said, and also in the story of Moses and Aaron: {And We left it among the others - peace be upon Moses And Aaron} [As-Saffat: 108-120]
And {Peace be upon the family of Yasin} [Al-Saffat: 130]

And likewise in the story of Abraham, God Almighty said: {Then when he separated from them and from what they worship besides God, We granted him Isaac and Jacob, and each of them We made A Prophet} [Maryam: 49] (49) {And We bestowed upon them of Our mercy and gave them a language of exalted truth} [Maryam: 50]

And he said in the story of Pharaoh: “And he and his soldiers were arrogant in the land unjustly, and they thought that they would not be returned to Us” [Al-Qasas: 39] (39) {So We seized him and his soldiers and dispersed them into the sea; then see what was the end of the wrongdoers.} [Al-Qasas: 40] (40) {And We made them leaders calling to the Fire. And on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped.} [Al-Qasas: 41] (41) {And We have followed them into this world with a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the abhorrent} [Al-Qasas: 42]
For this reason, God Almighty said: “Indeed, in their stories there is a lesson for those of understanding” [Yusuf: 111].
And he said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: {So be patient. Indeed, the outcome is for the righteous} [Hud: 49]

So he informed that the outcome is for the righteous, then that what happened to these and these is known through hearing and transmission at times, and it is known through reason. And taking into account their effects sometimes, as He said about the people of Hell: {If we had heard or reasoned, we would not have been among the companions of the Blazing Fire} [Al-Mulk: 10] as he mentioned. God has two ways in His saying: {And God will surely help whoever helps Him. Indeed, God is Powerful, Mighty} [Al-Hajj: 40] (40) {Those who, if We establish them in the land, will establish prayer, and pay zakat, and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and to Allah is the end of all matters.} [Al-Hajj: 41] (41)

Then he said: {And if they deny you, before them you denied the people of Noah, Ad, and Thamud} [Al-Hajj: 42] (42) {And the people of Abraham and the people of Lot} [Al-Hajj: 43] (43) {And the companions of Madyan, and Moses denied, so I granted hope to the disbelievers, then I seized them. So how was he ungrateful?} [Al-Hajj: 44] (44) {So like a town which We destroyed. And it is unjust, for it is void of its thrones, a well broken down, and a palace erected.} [Al-Hajj: 45] (45)

Then he said: {Have they not traveled through the earth and had hearts with which they reason, or ears with which they hear? For the eyes are not blinded, but The hearts in the breasts are blinded} [Al-Hajj: 46]

And the Almighty said: {And how many generations We destroyed before them. They were more forceful than them. And they searched in the land. Is there any one who will rescue them?} [Q: 36] (36) {Indeed, there is This is in remembrance of him who has a heart or listens while he is a witness.} [Q: 37]

And God Almighty said: {Have they not traveled through the earth and seen what was the end of those before them? They were stronger than them in strength and had divided the earth. And they inhabited it longer than they inhabited it, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs. It was not Allah who wronged them, but it was they who wronged themselves. 9] (9) {Then the end of those who did evil was misfortune, that they denied the signs of God and mocked them.} [Al-Rum: 10]

And God Almighty said: {Have they not traveled through the earth and seen what was the end of those who were before them? They were stronger than them in strength and influence in land, so God seized them for their sins, and there was not for them from God any protector.} [Ghafir: 21] (21) {That is because their messengers used to come to them. With clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so God seized them. Indeed, He is Powerful, severe in punishment.} [Ghafir: 22]

And God Almighty said: {Have they not traveled through the earth and seen what was the end of those before them who were greater than them and stronger in power and influence in earth, but what they used to earn availed them nothing. [Ghafir: 82] (82) {And when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced because of what they had. knowledge, and that which they used to mock has overtaken them.} [Ghafir: 83] (83) {And when they saw our misfortune, they said, “We believe in God alone, but we disbelieved in what we had done.” [Associating with Him} [Ghafir: 84] (84) {And their faith did not benefit them when they saw, through Our punishment, the laws of God which had passed among His servants, and there they lost. The disbelievers} [Ghafir: 85]

And he said, when he narrated the stories of Noah, Hud, Salih, Abraham, Lot, Shuaib, and Moses in Surat Hud: {This is from the news of the towns. We narrate it. Upon you from it is one who rises and reaps.} [Hud: 100] (100) {And We have not wronged them, but they have wronged themselves, so their gods whom they call upon besides God have not availed them. of anything when the command of your Lord had come, and they did not increase them without repentance.} [Hud: 101] (101) {And thus did your Lord seize when He took the towns while they were unjust. A severe and painful seizure of him.} [Hud: 102]
And when he mentioned the story of Lot in Surah As-Saffat, he said: {And indeed, you pass by them in the morning} [As-Saffat: 137] (137) {And by night, will you not understand?} [As-Saffat: 137] 138]

And in Surah Al-Hijr: {Indeed, in that are signs for those who strive.} [Al-Hijr: 75] (75) {And indeed, it is on a straight path} [Al-Hijr: 76] (76) {Indeed, in that is a sign. For the believers. (79)
The clear Imam is the clear and clear path.

Glory be to Him has made it clear that this and that are both in a way for the people to see them with their eyes and thus know what God has done to those who lie. His messengers and their disobedience, and the significance of God’s victory for the believers, and His vengeance on the unbelievers, on the truthfulness of the prophets, of the same type as the significance of the verses. And the miracles are true despite their truthfulness. The fact that this was done for this reason, and the fact that that was the reason for this is what is known about harm when... Imagining the matter as it is, such as the staff turning over into a serpent after asking Pharaoh for a sign, and the moon splitting when asking the polytheists of Mecca. A verse, and the like.

The famous question that is raised in this place is about who denies the justification for God’s actions and makes every action permissible for God, where it was said: To them: according to your origin: God does not do anything for the sake of something, and at that time He did not bring the extraordinary signs in order to confirm the Messenger’s belief. Nor did he punish these people for their disbelief in him, nor did he save these people and help them because of their belief in him, if he did not do anything for you. And they also said to them: If you make every act permissible for the Lord, it is permissible for supernatural things to appear at the hands of a liar. And it will be said to them also:

You do not know what the Lord does except by custom or the report of the prophets. Before knowing the truthfulness of the prophet, nothing is known by his report. The custom only occurs in what is repeated, such as the rising of the sun, the falling of rain, and the like, and bringing something supernatural to confirm it is not customary.

It is said: This question, if it is directed, only discredits the statement of those who say: He does something for the sake of something, and they allow it. He does everything possible, they do not prevent him from doing bad deeds, and there is nothing wrong with them that is bad or unjust except what is abstained from, such as making... The thing exists and is non-existent, and the body is placed in two places, and for this reason their opponents mentioned that as an argument in invalidating their doctrine, and they said: Their statement discredits the necessary sciences, and closes the door to knowledge due to the truthfulness of the messengers. They said:

If you make it possible for him to do everything, then make it possible for the mountains to turn into ruby, and the vapors to be milk, and other such things that are known. Of necessity, it is invalid, and they made it permissible for him to create miracles at the hands of liars. The intent here is not to answer these people, nor to explain Their statement was invalid, but what is meant is that if this question was addressed, it would only discredit what these people said, not discredit what he knew. By necessity from the meanings of the aforementioned verses regarding the condition of these and those, and that God Almighty saved Moses and helped him because of his truthfulness. And his prophecy and his faith, and he destroyed Pharaoh for his denial, and likewise he supported Muhammad and those who followed him over those of his people who denied him, and he supported Noah. Against those who disbelieved in him, and he supported Christ over those who denied him, and he supported all the messengers and their believing followers, as God Almighty said:
{Indeed, We will certainly help Our Messengers and those who believe in the life of this world and on the Day when witnesses will be raised} [Ghafir: 51] (51)

And He said: {Our word to Our messenged servants preceded} [Al-Saffat: 171] (171) {Indeed, they will be helped.} [Al-Saffat: 172] (172) {And indeed, We must fight for them. Those who are victorious} [Al-Saffat: 173]

Nor does it invalidate what is taught by necessity, that God sends down rain at appointed times to irrigate farms, and that He directs the Nile to irrigate the land of Egypt. And He made the parts of man for the benefits they contain, such as striking with the hands, walking with the feet, seeing with the eyes, and hearing. With the ears, and speaking with the tongue, and he made the water of the eye salt because it is a sludge, and the salinity prevents it from dissolving, and the water from the ear is bitter. To prevent flies from entering the brain, to make the water in the mouth fresh to flavor food and drink, and to make sea water salty to sustain sleep, for if It was sweet, and a great animal dies in it, and the wind corrupts it, and humans and animals die by this wind, and countless wisdoms. God is witnessed in His creation.

And for lack of explanation, they say: We know that this is comparable to the customary ruling that God has established, even if He did not create anything for another thing. Likewise, those who deny the causes while also denying the explanation say: We know that He created this with this, not with it. What is miraculous is the belief in this regard according to them, but it remains for them that this is only known by habit, and not by habit.

There is no crime, they returned to his nature, that this is a known matter of necessity, even if it contradicts their corrupt origin, and they gave an example of this. By the king who demonstrated something contrary to his habit of believing his messenger.

But it is said to them: The king performs an act for a purpose. So it can be said: He rose to confirm His Messenger, while you hold that God does not He does one thing for another, so the proverb did not remain consistent, and that is why they became disturbed in this situation, sometimes saying:

Miracles are evidence of truthfulness so as not to lead to the incapacitation of the Lord, for there is no evidence of truthfulness except the creation of impotence. If it is not evidence, it must be. The Lord is not able to believe the truthful Messenger, and this is the method of Al-Ash’ari in most of his books, and one of his two sayings, and the judge Abu Bakr followed it. And Abu Ishaq Al-Isfaraini, Abu Bakr bin Furak, Abu Muhammad bin Al-Labban, Abu Ali bin Shazan, and Judge Abu Ya’la, And others

And the second, they said: We know by necessity that he did this for the sake of the truth, as the proverb used, and this is the other saying, and it is The method of Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ash’ari in his Amaliyah, which is the method of Abu Al-Ma’ali, and his followers such as Al-Razi and others, and they disputed: Is it possible to create this? At the hands of a liar? It was said: It is not possible because if it were possible, it would be permissible for it to happen. And it was said: Rather, it is possible, but we know that He will not do it just as we know that He will not do it. He performs many powerful miracles, such as turning a mountain into ruby and turning the sea into oil.

They said: We know of necessity that he does not do it, so it does not follow from the fact that it is possible and possible that it is not known that it will not happen, rather It may be known that it did not happen by necessity, even though we say that it is possible and destined, and the appearance of miracles at the hands of a liar in a claim We have prophecy in this regard.

And they said: The miracle is evidence of the truthfulness of the prophets, so it is impossible for the evidence to not be necessary for what is indicated, and this saying is true, but Those who dispute them say: It entails the opposite of what they denied about the fact that God creates something for something, and creates one thing for another thing, and what they said about His being It is permissible for him to do everything, and what they mentioned of the truth is evidence that the creation knows what they know of the wisdom of the Lord and what He wills for it. He created him for another reason, and that He, Glory be to Him, is far above doing things. It is not permissible for Him to do everything, and they say here:
Something may be possible and permissible even though it is known that it is not a reality, like mountains turning into rubies.
The sea is mercury, the death of all the people of the country in one moment, and the fate of children as wise scholars in one moment.

They rely a lot on this answer, as mentioned by Judge Abu Bakr, Judge Abu Ya’la, Abu Al-Ma’ali, Al-Razi, and others. Then they say about reason that it is necessary knowledge, such as knowledge of the obligation of obligatory things, the abstention of impermissible things, and the permissibility of rewards. The things that are prohibited are like the bloody overthrow of the Tigris, and similar things in ordinary matters. They make customs obligatory at times, and abstainable at other times, with There is no reason to necessitate either this or that.

And they say: We know that this is permissible and possible and does not depend on any reason, nor does it have an obstacle like the other. Then we know that this is a reality, and this It does not happen simply because of custom, even though breaking custom has no control among them. Rather, everything that happens from customs are miracles for the prophets. According to them, it is permissible for it to be for a guardian or a magician, and the difference between them is the challenge or lack of opposition, and the same applies to the philosophers. Atheists who say:

The reasons for the verses are astronomical forces, psychological and natural forces, and all of these are common to them among the prophets and magicians. But the prophet means good and justice, and the magician means evil and injustice.
