For this reason, whoever proves something or denies it, and is asked for proof and does not provide it, is interrupted in the debate, and if he objects The one objected to with objection or opposition and responded to it, the objected to it ceased, and the first statement was confirmed, even if he did not answer The opposition has ceased to have evidence, as the evidence that must be followed is sound evidence for the opposing opponent, even if he establishes conclusive evidence. Then he was confronted with something that did not help in cutting, so he could have said:

What I have mentioned is beneficial to science, and knowledge is not contradicted by suspicion, and evidence is not contradicted by suspicions that are of the type of Sophistical talk. He, Glory be to Him, forbade speaking without knowledge.

Absolutely, and he specifically spoke about God in the Almighty’s saying: {Say, “My Lord has only forbidden immoralities - those of them that are apparent and those that are latent, and sin and transgression.” without the truth, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has not sent down authority, and that you say about Allah that which you do not know.” [Al-A’raf: 33]

He forbade following in the footsteps of Satan, and told that he commands to speak about God without knowledge, so He said: {O people, eat of what is on the earth. lawful and good, and do not follow in the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is your clear enemy.} [Al-Baqarah: 168] (168) {He only commands you to do evil and immorality, and to speak against God is what you do not know.} [Al-Baqarah: 169] (169) {And when it is said to them, “Follow what God has revealed,” they say, “Rather, we follow what we found our fathers upon, even if it were.” Their fathers understood nothing, nor were they guided.” [Al-Baqarah: 170]

Likewise, he condemns those who argue and argue without knowledge, according to the Almighty’s saying: {And among the people is he who disputes about God without knowledge, nor guidance, nor an enlightening Book} [Al-Hajj: 8]

And he said: {And among the people is he who disputes about God without knowledge and follows every rebellious Satan} [Al-Hajj: 3] (3) {It is decreed for him that whoever befriends Him - surely he will lead him astray. And He will guide him to the torment of the burning fire.} [Al-Hajj: 4] And the Almighty said: {Behold, these are you who have disputed concerning that of which you have knowledge, so why do you dispute concerning that of which you have no knowledge? Knowledge, and God knows, while you do not know” [Al Imran: 66]
And God Almighty says: {If a sinner comes to you with news, then investigate.} [Al-Hujurat: 6]

It deals with the information of every sinner, and if he is an unbeliever, it is not permissible to deny him except with evidence, just as it is not permissible to believe him except with evidence, and in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Abu Hurairah said: The People of the Book used to read the Torah in Hebrew, and interpret it in Arabic, so the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: He, peace be upon him, said: “When the People of the Book narrate to you, do not believe them and do not disbelieve them. Either they narrate to you a truth and you disbelieve it, or They tell you falsehood and you believe it, and say: {We believe in that which was revealed to us and was revealed to you, and our God and your God are one, and to Him we submit} [Al-Ankabut: 46] »

This is what the Qur’an and Sunnah indicate, regarding a person abstaining from that which he does not know to be absent or confirmed. It has been reported from others. The prophets, as it came from Christ, peace be upon him, that he said: There are three matters: a matter whose right path has become clear, so follow it, and a matter whose wrongdoing has become clear. So avoid it, and if something is suspected of you, refer it to the one who knows it.

Most of the rational people of the children of Adam are on this, and for this reason it is not permissible to believe in a report transmitted from the Messenger or anyone else except with evidence indicating its truthfulness. It is not permissible for him to be a liar except with evidence indicating that he is lying, and based on this knowledge and religion, the scholars have spoken and written many books on Criticism and fairness in men and hadiths. Among the people are those who are known for their truthfulness and accuracy. This is justice whose information is accepted, and among them are those who He may be truthful, but he may not memorize or be precise, so they say about something like this:

It is truthful and spoken by someone who has memorized it, and among them are those who are known to lie, and if the hadith is narrated by someone who has a bad memory or someone who has He is lying. They did not rule by that hadith, nor did they confirm it.

Then sometimes the evidence is based on his lying, and sometimes they stop at it, not knowing whether it is true or a lie, and such things are neither believed nor proven. It cannot be taken as evidence, such as a witness who testified for the plaintiff, and he does not have satisfactory justice, or he is an adversary or a suspicious accused. This is if his testimony is rejected. It was not accepted. The meaning of that ruling was not that he was a lie or a mistake. Rather, the meaning of that was that there is no evidence based on it, and it is not ruled based on the lack of Knowledge is true, not knowledge is false.

If the defendant has a right or is innocent, then it is an argument that favors his side, and he added the right street to it, as in Sahih. Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If people were to be given according to their claim, men would claim the blood of a people.” And their property, but the oath is on the defendant. If the plaintiff has nothing but his claim, then the evildoer’s side is stronger than his side. Because with him:

The basic principle in the hands is that they are right, and the basic principle is that they are clear of liability, but the plaintiff may be honest and have no proof, and this is often the case. Very well, it is not defended merely by the original. Rather, the one who denies swears an oath, and his oath is made up of the original with proof, so denying this is in response to a claim. This is both news, the truth of which is not known, so they conflicted, and the denier preferred the original, so it remains as it was and is not accepted by any argument of the plaintiff. He claimed it merely because of his claim, and his claim against the defendant does not cease because he did not come up with an argument to defend him. If the denier swears, his oath is An argument that settled the dispute and ended the lawsuit.

If the denier does not take the oath, but rather abandons it, and the accuser does not provide a proof, then the matter remains in place according to most scholars, and according to some of them: He punishes the evildoer with rebuke, and makes his rebuttal either a substitute for what he asked for, or an acknowledgment of it, and most say: Rather, the oath is returned to The claimant is the student who says that he knows that he is sincere in what he claimed, and that he is aware of what he claimed, so it is said to him: Swear and take it. If he swears He took, otherwise they would pay. Then among the scholars are those who reject oaths in most cases, and among them are those who rule by contradiction, even if the denier says:
I do not know what he claimed, and both sects mention narrations about the Companions.

What is narrated on the authority of the Companions indicates detail, and it is the clearest of the sayings, which is that: If the denier is the one who knows, not the one who is claiming, as If a defect appears in the item sold, and it was sold on a cleared note, and the buyer says: I did not know about it, then here it is said to him, as Uthman ibn Affan to Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with them both: Swear that you sold him and that there is no disease in him that you know of. If he swears an oath, otherwise he will be judged for redemption, just as Uthman judged Ibn Omar for redemption, and if the plaintiff says that he knows what he claimed, then he He claimed a debt or property from another and said:
I do not know what you claimed. Swear and take. If he does not swear, he will not be given anything.

Evidence in claims, according to most scholars, is what clarifies the truth, makes it clear, and clarifies it, such as evidence, sign, and sign. An oath is taken by either of them, such as when the plaintiff appoints a witness, so he swears an oath with his witness, and he judges it with a witness and an oath, as was the case in the Sunnah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is the opinion of most scholars, and some of them say:

The oath is always on the side of the defendant, and the same applies if there is taint, smear, or suspicion in the murder case, which are signs that favor the side of the defendant. The plaintiff, the guardians of the murdered person swear fifty oaths, and this is decided upon for them according to most scholars, as was the case in that year.

Likewise with regard to cursing, if the husband swears and bears four testimonies to God that he is of the truthful, and confirms it with the fifth, then he has established proof of the truth. His claim, because the woman was stubborn and testified four times, confirming the fifth, that he is a liar. The two pieces of evidence and testimonies contradicted each other. He was not judged to be a slanderer, nor was he judged to be an adulterer. If she ate and did not swear, then more. الْعُلَمَاءِ يَقُولُونَ:

She will be judged to be an adulteress, and she will be tortured for that as indicated by the Qur’an, because it combines the testimony of the husband and her refusal to object, as The sign and the oath are combined in the division, just as the witness and the oath are combined, and just as in the case of a denier the original and the oath are combined.
This and other similar things that the Sharia brought, and its extension has another place.

What is meant here is that the news, if there is evidence of its truth or falsehood, otherwise it remains something that he did not believe in or disbelieve in, and the people of Knowledge of the hadith if they say: This hadith was narrated by so-and-so, and he was wounded, or weak, or of poor memory, or from one whose hadith was not accepted. His narration, and the like, is like the saying of someone who said: This witness is injured, or has poor memory, or is one whose testimony is not accepted, and this is useful. It is not judged based on it. The ruling does not indicate that he is a liar. Rather, it may be possible that he is true, so it cannot be said that he is a liar except with evidence.

And if they say about the hadith: It is weak, then this is what they mean, meaning that it has not been proven, cannot be used as evidence, and it is not permissible to judge its truthfulness. It is not What they mean is that by doing so, he rules that the transmitter is a lie, denies what he reported, and says:

This was not without our knowledge of this denial. Rather, if there was evidence that what was reported was not present, we would rule accordingly. Otherwise, we would remain silent. We did not deny it, nor did we confirm it. This is a principle that must be known, as many people do not distinguish between what he denies because there is evidence to deny it. And what he did not prove due to the lack of evidence to prove it. Rather, you see them as what they did not know to prove, so they have confirmed what they have no knowledge of. And they said with their mouths what they had no knowledge of, and this is many of the people of reasoning and theorizing and the people of chain of transmission and information. The first two are sects who seek evidence to prove something. If they do not find it, they deny it. It is known that lack of knowledge is not knowledge of nothingness. Conscience does not necessitate non-existence unless the seeker is among those who are able to do so, either with knowledge or overwhelming suspicion. Among these are those who He says about the attributes of God unless there is definitive evidence to prove it, otherwise it is necessary to definitively deny it, because the attributes of God are not proven unless Absolutely, and the majority of people disagreed with them on that, and they said:

Just as it is not permissible to refute a statement of proof except with conclusive evidence, it is not permissible to refute a negation except with conclusive evidence of negation. So, since it is not permissible to We are affirmed only with knowledge, and we are not denied except with knowledge.

The one who denies has evidence, just as there is evidence for the one who affirms. These people said: These issues are based on definiteness, so it is not permissible for us to speak about them based on surmise. If the definite person does not do so, we will deviate. In the negative. So it was said to them:

This is an argument against you, for if you deny what you do not know to deny, you speak with suspicion, and if you deny it without being definitive, you have You spoke about definitive matters without any definiteness, whether denying or confirming the statement, and it is not known from the legal or rational evidence that everything that did not If there is auditory or mental evidence to prove it, then you must deny it, and categorically deny it. Rather, speaking of this is speaking without Science.

Hence, many theorists made a mistake in denying many of the Lord’s attributes, His rulings, and His actions, as they did not know of conclusive evidence. He confirmed it, but they denied it, and it was proven in the same matter, and others may have conclusive evidence that proves it, even if it is assumed that people do not know. All of them have it, for God has knowledge that His servants do not know, and God has names that He has kept in His possession in His knowledge of the unseen that people do not know about them, and not if He does not To know the validity of a characteristic, its absence must be known. Rather, it may be suspected that it is proven or absent, and it may be doubted about it, so it is neither known nor suspected. One of them, and it is obligatory for a person to say what he knows:

I know it, and when he thinks it: I think it, and when he doubts it: I doubt it, and God Almighty has not made it obligatory for a person to sever something because of the absence of something. If it is not known that it is negligible, then whoever says: We must sever it with negation has made a mistake.

This is in contrast to what contradicts the proven attributes, for this must be denied about God, as it is known through conclusive evidence that God is described. With the attributes of perfection that contradict imperfection, such as: He is Ever-Living, Ever-Subsisting, All-Knowing, and has Power over all things, and that He is the Creator of all things and its Lord, And His King, and that He is independent of everything else in every way, so everyone who says something that contradicts this knows that it is false, like those who said: Indeed, He has A partner or a child, or that he intercedes with him without his permission, and the like that contradicts his known perfection.

The absence of the necessary indicates the absence of the binding, such as the matters that if It exists because it must be transmitted frequently and commonly, for the absence of the necessary indicates the absence of the obligatory, as if someone said:

A city greater than Baghdad, Mosul, Isfahan, and Egypt was built between Iraq and the Levant, or between the Hijaz and the Levant, with three floors. days, and so on. He knows that it is a lie, for this is something people would be keen on conveying if it were present. If not This becomes more widespread and the knowledge spreads that the one who reported it is a liar.

Likewise, if a plaintiff claims that on Friday or Eid the preacher was killed, and the people did not pray on Friday, and this does not apply. And it spread, or he claimed that he killed some kings of people, and this did not spread, and it did not spread, or he claimed that a prophet was sent among the Messiah. And Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, or after Muhammad, brought a book such as the Qur’an or the Gospel, and many people followed it, and many people denied it. He knows that this is a lie, as something like this is bound to increase and spread.

Likewise, if he claimed that the Quraysh or others opposed the Qur’an and brought a book similar to the Qur’an, and they demonstrated that and invalidated it. With it is the proof of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so this is what is confirmed by his lying, because if something like that had happened, it would have been a source of determination. The reasons for transferring it, and likewise if he claimed that Muhammad ordered the pilgrimage to a house other than the ancient House or required fasting in a month other than the month of Ramadan. Or he made it obligatory for a sixth prayer at the time of Duha, or he ordered the call to prayer and the iqamah for other than the five prayers, or he said publicly among the people to Ubay Bakr, Abbas, Ali, or others:

This is the caliph after me, so listen to him and obey him, or that Ali called for himself in the caliphate of the three, and such matters. Which, if it had occurred, would have had concomitants. The absence of the concomitant indicates the absence of the obligatory. Then, some of these concomitants are clear and some are hidden. He is known to the elite.

For this reason, the people of knowledge about the circumstances of the Messenger used to assert that hadiths were false, and no one else would assert that they were false, because of their knowledge of the implications of that. Hadiths and the absence of what is necessary for them, just as those who know the raids of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, assert that he did not fight in the Battle of Tabuk, and that The fighting raids were only nine, and he did not raid himself into Yemen, nor Iraq, nor went beyond Tabuk after the prophethood. He did not perform Hajj after the Hijrah except the Farewell Hajj, and he did not fast except nine Ramadans.

And thus they know that so-and-so made a mistake in this hadith against so-and-so, because they knew from proven sources that that hadith was He narrated it in a specific form, so if someone who is not trustworthy narrates something that contradicts that, they know that it is false, and that he made a mistake or deliberately lied, for example They do not know that the one who adds to the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is lying: “There is no precedence except in a shoe, a hoof, or a blade.” So some people added to it: “Or Jinnah” when he saw that some of the princes had pigeons with him, and they knew that he had lied to get closer to that prince.

And as they know, those who narrated that Musaylimah and his people were believers in God and His Messenger lied, but the truthful fought them because they did not give Zakat, for they have learned through the chain of transmission that Musaylimah claimed to be a prophet, and his people followed him in that, and that he wrote to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. During his life, he said: From the greeting of the Messenger of God to Muhammad, the Messenger of God. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to him:

“From Muhammad, the Messenger of God, to Musaylimah the liar.” And they know that he had tricks, and that his lies appeared in many ways. And that Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq and the Companions fought him for lying in the claim of prophethood, and they fought his people for their apostasy from Islam. And they followed a false prophet and did not fight them because they did not pay zakat to Abu Bakr.

Likewise, Al-Aswad Al-'Ansi, who claimed prophethood during the life of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and was killed during his lifetime. Each of them was known to be a lie. By denying the truthful and trustworthy Prophet, and from what appeared from the evidence of their lies, such as false news that contradicts prophecy, and such as Coming up with a fabricated Qur’an so whoever hears it will know that God did not speak it, but rather it is a classification of human beings, as Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq said. To them when they repented of apostasy and returned to Islam: “Make me hear the Qur’an of Musaylimah.” When they heard it from him, he said:

And judge by where it goes with your minds, for this is speech that did not come from “El.” That is, it did not come from a Lord. Immorality and lying, such as when the most trusted person found out that he was lying, and he sought help from someone who fabricated lies for him, such as He was promising them that Gabriel had told him that he would be victorious, so when the facts were established, he said to them: You have no Gabriel, so fight on behalf of I think you are like these things that indicate that the liar is lying.

Honesty has necessary evidence that indicates truthfulness, and lying has necessary evidence that indicates lying, and it is not permissible to judge truthfully. An informer, nor an informant of a lie unless there is evidence, and as long as it is not known whether he is truthful or a lie, nor is it proven or disproven, then it is obligatory to abstain. About him, and the one who says: I do not know this, and it has not been proven to me, and I do not assert it, nor judge by it, nor do I use it as evidence, nor do I use it as evidence. I do not base my doctrine, belief, work, or the like on it. He does not say:

I categorize this as a lie and its absence, even if I categorically confirm that whoever confirmed it spoke without knowledge, then I categorically categorize it as ignorance of the one who affirmed it. The believer has nothing but certainty of its absence, so whoever denies it without evidence requires severing it. We rupture it with his ignorance, misguidance, and error, even if he does not It is severed by the absence of what he has proven in the same matter, as if he who ruled on the testimony of an injured and sinful person, God commanded that his report be confirmed, so whoever judges And his report was interrupted without evidence to indicate its truthfulness. We ruled that this was a wise speaker without knowledge, even if the informing witness was not ruled to be a lie. But it is not permissible for a person to deny the knowledge of another, or to deny it, without his knowledge of the reasons by which he knows and informs, for he A person often has many pieces of evidence that indicate the truthfulness of a particular person, or the proof of a particular matter, even if no one else knows any of that. Evidence.
This is also one of the mistakes that many people make when they look at themselves.

And the extent of their knowledge, then if they did not find with them what required knowledge of that matter, they made others do so without their knowledge. By the absence of reasons for knowledge for that other person, and they may establish weak arguments that someone else does not know that, just as he does. Many people rely on theory, inference, and consideration, and whoever does not equal them in their theory, evidence, and strength of mind does not know what They taught him, and many people knew many things through news, transmission, and inference from that, and those who did not share with them what they heard, and in what They knew him from the circumstances of the informants and the informant, and the completeness of their knowledge of that is not known as what they knew.

For this reason, the people of rational theorizing have methods that are not known to the people of information, and the people of auditory information have methods that are not known merely Minds, and for this reason these people had ways to indicate the truthfulness of the Messenger and his prophethood, and to provide evidence for that, many things that he did not know. The people of hadith and narrations, and among these people there are hadiths that are frequently transmitted with them, and extensive verses with them that they know of. The Messenger spoke the truth, even if those people did not know it. Rather, there are ways to know the Maker and believe His Messenger. Every people may have a way or Ways that others do not know, and they share in acknowledging God and His Messenger, and every people has ways and evidence other than the ways of others. And their evidence, rather, what has been reported to them about the circumstances of the Messenger. They may be the informants.

For those to whom it has been reported repeatedly about His verses and laws, without informing them to those, just as the Companions were the informers. to the people of the Levant with the verses of the Messenger, the Qur’an, and the laws of Islam other than the companions who informed the people of Iraq, but the news of these people is true. He informed these people, and even if each of the two sects does not know the notables of those who informed those, and so on with all other sciences, it may be the one who He taught these people jurisprudence, theorizing, grammar, or medicine other than the one he taught these people, even if all of them shared the kind of jurisprudence, theorizing, and grammar, And medicine, and he taught what these people knew of objects and types, even though the path of these people is not the path of those people, even if they share the type.

In general, what people know through sense is from this perspective, as a person senses the conditions of his soul, such as his hunger, thirst, and fullness. And his feeling, his love, his hatred, his desire, his repulsion, his pain, and his pleasure. Rather, he feels his organs, such as his stomach and genitals, but he does not feel Like others, but they share in the general sex, so they share in the sex of feeling their hunger and fullness, and they may participate in other things. What they sense, such as their participation in seeing the sun, the moon, the crescent, and the planets.

A group of theologians in Greek logic made a mistake in this matter. They claimed that the experimental, periodic, and intuitive sciences, If they make it a category other than empiricism, then there are those among them who make intuitionism a type of empiricism, and among them are those who make it another type. These people claimed that these sciences are specific and cannot be used as an argument against those who do not know them, apart from the sensory sciences and existential matters. And mentalities, but not so, but just as these are sometimes common, and other times specific, so are the sensual things, for all the people of the time And a place in which they know by intuition the conditions of that place and time and the conditions of its people in which no one else shares with them, and likewise Oddities, for whoever is afflicted with oddities in political and physical matters learns of them that no one else shares with him.

The same applies to mentalities, for some people have a root with which to measure branches and know the common value, which is the middle limit. He knows about the connection of the ruling to him what no one else knows.

The types of sciences and their methods, some of them are specific, some of them are common, and some of them are common, and some of them are shared by the human race. Some of them are common to each type and sect. This is a comprehensive principle that should be known to whoever speaks about this topic.

chapters.title: Separating the circumstances and evidence of the informant’s truthfulness and lies
paragraphs: [Chapter: Circumstances and evidence of the truthfulness and falsity of the informant]

And if the gender of the one who informs him may be a liar or he may be telling the truth, then it is known that not every person who tells a piece of news is absolutely believed, nor He lies absolutely, for none of the wise people has ever said that every single piece of news or every single piece of news is truthful or useful to knowledge, nor that it is A lie. Rather, people know that a single piece of news may provide evidence of its truthfulness, so it is known that it is true, even if it is a single piece of news, and the evidence may provide If he tells a lie, then it is known that it is a lie, even if thousands of people are told about it, if their news was without knowledge of what they were told about, or about Complicity on their part in lying, such as telling people of false beliefs about the falsehood that they believe, but if they were informed about Some of them are aware of what they were informed of, so these people are truthful in the same matter, and their truthfulness is sometimes known by their narrations being consistent, without collusion. And if they were two, then when the two told a long story, they attributed it to knowledge, and it is known that they did not conspire against him, nor It is from what is usually agreed upon that they are similar in lying or error, it is known to be true.

The truthfulness of a single piece of news may be known through various types of evidence that indicate its truthfulness, and the truthfulness of a single piece of news may be known through evidence that correlates with its news. His truthfulness is known by it, and these signs and clues may be characteristics of the informant, such as his knowledge, religion, and investigation of truthfulness, such that he is known for certain. He does not intentionally lie, as the scholars of Ahl al-Hadith definitely know that Ibn Omar, Aisha, Abu Saeed, and Jabir bin Abdullah, And people like them did not deliberately lie to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, let alone Abu Bakr, Omar, Othman, and Ali. And Ibn Masoud, Ubayy bin Ka’b, Muadh bin Jabal, and their likes. Indeed, they know with certainty that Al-Thawri, Malik, and Shu’bah, Yahya bin Saeed, Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi, Ahmad bin Hanbal, al-Bukhari, Abu Zur’ah, Abu Dawud, and others like them, They do not intentionally lie in conversation.

The evidence may be characteristics of the informant that are specific to that news or its type by which it is known that that informant is not lying, for example That news is like the prince’s chamberlain when he said in his presence to his soldiers: The prince has given you permission to leave, or ordered you to ride. Tomorrow, or so-and-so commands over you, and the like, they know that he does not intentionally lie about something like this, even if it is not in his presence. So how if it was in his presence, even if they might deny him anything other than that?

The evidence may be that someone who shared his knowledge of that news heard it, and it was confirmed by him, as custom may prevent collusion in lying. It may prevent collusion in concealment, admitting to lying, remaining silent, and denying it, as long as there are determinations and reasons to mention it. The news of it prevents the people of tuatir from colluding to conceal it, just as it is usually impossible for a great event to occur that is known Concerns and reasons for conveying them during Hajj, the mosque, or the military, and where custom requires those present to convey what they saw and then not convey That is one.

Admitting a lie and remaining silent in response to it is usually greater abstinence than concealment, for a person may be habitually prompted by his soul to He remains silent about what he saw and heard and does not tell about it, and his soul does not invite him to lie to him, and tell about him what he knows to be a lie. So he should confirm it and not deny it, since people’s habit of denying such things is more eloquent than their habit of informing about it. Likewise, if He lied about a story, and those who witnessed it reported that, so their will to deny this is greater than their will to tell them what happened. First of all, if it is one of the issues that silence prevents from revealing, then remaining silent about the liar’s denial about it is even more abstinent, and it may The signs are characteristics in him that are associated with his experience, for a person may see the redness of his face and distinguish between the redness of his embarrassment and modesty and the redness of his face. His redness is from fever and increased blood, and his redness is from a bath, and his redness is from anger, and he also distinguishes between his yellowness from panic, And fear, and between his yellow appearance of sadness and fear, and his yellow appearance of illness, just as his complexion and his face are known for his conditions. His natural body from his various diseases, to the point that skilled doctors know the patient’s condition from his condition, so they do not need to A pulse and a bottle, and you also know his psychological state. Is he happy, happy, or sad and distressed?
And he knows whether he is a lover, a friend, and someone who wants to do good.

Or is he an enemy who hates and desires evil? As it was said: The eyes speak to me, but the heart is silent... and the eye knows from the eyes of its interlocutor whether he is from its party or from its enemies, and as it was said: There is no good in being haughty and looking sad. Then when he speaks, despite that, his speech indicates something more eloquent than what his facial features indicate, as God Almighty said about The hypocrites: {And if We had willed, We could have shown them to you, and you would have recognized them by their marks, and you would have recognized them by the tone of speech} [Muhammad: 30]

So he told that it is necessary to know the hypocrites by the tone of what they say, and that their knowledge of the specifics depends on the will, and the lying hypocrite He says with his tongue what is not in his heart, so he made it clear that in the tone of his words he knows that he is a liar, and he said regarding the believers: {He will mark them on their faces. From the effects of prostration} [Al-Fath: 29]
And He said regarding the disbeliever: “He will be held back by a burden after that.” [Al-Qalam: 13]
That is, he has a trace of evil, that is, a sign by which he is known.

It was narrated on the authority of Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, “No one concealed a secret except that God revealed it on the pages of his face and the slips of his tongue.” We have expanded the discussion on this in the issue of faith, and we have explained that what is established in the heart of belief, love of God and His Messenger, and veneration, It must appear on the limbs, and vice versa, and for this reason the absence of the apparent obligatory is inferred from the absence of the hidden obligatory, as In the authentic hadith on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said:

“Indeed, there is an embryo in the body that, if it is good, the rest of the body will be good for it, and if it is spoiled, the rest of the body will be spoiled for it, namely the heart.” And as Omar ibn Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said to someone who saw him tampering with prayer: “If this man’s heart were humble, his limbs would be humble.” In this regard, the Almighty says:
{You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day being friendly with those who oppose God and His Messenger} [Al-Mujadila: 22]
And His saying: {And if they had believed in God and the Prophet and in what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as guardians} [Al-Ma’idah: 81]
And he said: “And if they had wanted to go out, they would have prepared for it a number of things” [Al-Tawbah: 46]

The will that is in the heart, along with the ability, necessitates doing what one wants, and traveling on a distant expedition is not possible except with a period of preparation, and from this point Othman said to Omar when he consulted with him about the woman who confessed to adultery: “I see her making it the same way as someone who does not know that it is forbidden.” When he saw her openly talking about what she had done, and telling it without caring, it became clear to him that she did not believe it was forbidden, and that it was reprehensible. He was punished for it, and Omar, Ali and others agreed with him on that.

And the truthful and righteous man is revealed on his face by the light of his sincerity, and the brightness of his face is a feature by which he is known, and so is the immoral liar, and whenever As long as a person lives, this effect appears in him, to the point that a man will have a beautiful face when he is young. If he is one of the immoral people, he insists on This appears on him at the end of his life due to the ugliness of his face that his inner self affected, and vice versa.

It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: A good deed brings light to the heart, radiance to the face, strength to the body, abundance of sustenance, and love. In the hearts of creation, and evil has darkness in the heart, darkness in the face, weakness in the body, and hatred in the hearts of creation.

The man may be one of those who does not intentionally lie, but rather holds false beliefs about God, His Messengers, His religion, or His servants. The righteous, and he will have asceticism, worship, and diligence in that. This will affect the lie that he thought was the truth and its consequences inside him. This will appear on his face, and he will add dirt and blackness to it that suits his condition, as some of the Salaf said: If the one who is an heresy anointed all A day with daubing. Indeed, the blackness of innovation is on his face.” And these matters will appear completely on the Day of Resurrection. God Almighty said:

And on the Day of Resurrection you will see {those who lied about God, their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell a resting place for the arrogant?} [Az-Zumar: 60] (60) {And God will save. Those who fear Allah will not be affected by evil, nor will they grieve.} [Az-Zumar: 61]

And God Almighty said: {On the Day when faces will be whitened and faces will turn black. Then as for those whose faces have turned black - you have disbelieved after your belief - then taste the torment for what You were disbelieving} [Al Imran: 106] (106) {And as for those whose faces have been whitened, they are in the mercy of God; they will abide therein forever} [Al Imran: 107].
Ibn Abbas and others said: The faces of the Sunnis and the community become white, and the faces of the people of heresy and division become dark.

What is meant is that what is in the hearts of the intention of honesty, love, righteousness, and the like may appear on the face until it is known. Necessary of the most necessary knowledge, as well as what is in it of the intention of lying, hatred, immorality, and other things, and a person accompanies in The journey of someone who has never seen him except for that moment. If he sees him and hears his words, he should not wait a while to find out whether he is safe and can be reassured. Or is it not so? He may be suspected at first, and he may have made a mistake, but the prevailing custom is that it later becomes clear to the general public.

Likewise, the neighbor knows his neighbor, and the dealer knows his dealer, and for this reason, when a man testified with Omar Ibn Al-Khattab and another person gave him the sanction, he said: Did Are you his nearest neighbor and know his evening and morning? He said: No. He said: Did you deal with him regarding dirhams and dinars, by which people’s trusts are tested? He said: No. He said: Did you accompany him on the journey in which people's morals were revealed? He said: No. He said: You do not know him, and it was narrated that he said: Perhaps you saw him performing several rak’ahs in the mosque. This is because the hypocrite may reveal the prayer, but whoever does not tell him does not know the innermost matter of his matter, as it was said:
A wolf you see praying... so when you pass by it, it kneels.

He supplicates, and the greatest of his supplications is that the prey does not fall... and when the prey appears imaginary, then asceticism and piety are gone. If this is so, then who foretold it? And God chose him for the message, his heart was among the best of hearts, truthful and righteous, and whoever invents a lie against God, his heart is among the worst of hearts, lying. And immorality, as Abdullah bin Masoud said:

God looked into the hearts of the servants and found the heart of Muhammad the best of the hearts of the servants, so he chose him for his message, then he looked into the hearts of the servants after the heart of the servants. Muhammad found the hearts of his companions to be the best of the hearts of servants, so he took them to accompany his Prophet and establish his religion, but the believers did not see it as good. In the sight of God is good, and what the believers see as bad is bad in the sight of God, and Abdullah bin Masoud said: Whoever among you is patient, let him be patient. As for someone who has died, the living person is not safe from temptation.

These are the companions of Muhammad, the most righteous of this nation in heart, the deepest in knowledge, and the least intrusive. They are a people whom God chose for the company of His Prophet. And establish his religion, so know their rights, and hold fast to their guidance, for they were on the straight path.

If he is one of the greatest, or even the greatest, people of his time, he is honest and righteous, then it must appear on the slips of his tongue and the pages of his face. It is appropriate for that, just as the liar and disbeliever must appear on his face and the slips of his tongue that are appropriate for that, and this sometimes happens when Telling him what he was told, and sometimes he was in a situation other than that, for if a man came and said:

The sultan, or the prince, or the ruler, or the sheikh, or so-and-so sent me to you with such-and-such, it may be associated with the same information from him. His quality and condition are what makes it known that he is telling the truth or lying, even if it was known before that.

By telling the truth or lying, that is another indication, and he may be one of those who lie, but he is known to be truthful in that news. Let those continue. On the same experience for twenty-odd years with all types of people and their different circumstances.

It should be known that people differ in their circumstances in knowledge, experience, consideration, and reasoning in all knowledge. A person may be aware of a meaning that no one else is aware of, and what is hidden to others may become clear to him. Even the prophets differ, as he said. God Almighty: {And David and Solomon, when they were judging the field, when the people’s sheep scattered therein, and We were witnesses to their judgment - So Solomon made it understandable, and they both We have given judgment and knowledge} [The Prophets:

78 - 79] What is meant is that knowledge of the truthfulness of the truthful person and the falsehood of the liar, like any other piece of information, may be necessary, or it may be theoretical. It is not one of the primary, universal necessities, such as the knowledge that one is half of two, but rather it is one of the knowledge of specific matters, such as the knowledge With the redness of shame, the paleness of shame, the justice of the just, the injustice of the oppressor, and other such things of which the expert has necessary knowledge, If it is deductive, then knowledge of science does not occur simply by having

The evidence is in itself, rather the heart must know it, and people differ in that, and the evidence is never what is necessitated by the signified, for every Whatever is necessary for a thing is evidence of it, but it is necessary to know it, and to know that it is necessary, then when knowledge is achieved, it becomes Necessary, and it may be necessary without the intermediary of specific evidence, and knowledge of specific things is not the same as knowledge of the truth of this and the falsity of this, which is necessary. There is a need for a comprehensive analogy, as this only serves to mediate a general issue, and the specifics may not require that, even if it is not There must be some experience with that particular condition.

If the one who says: I am the Messenger of God, he is either one of the people’s choice, the most truthful, the most righteous, and the best of them, or he is one of the The most evil of people, the most lying, and the most ungodly, and the difference between these two is in many aspects that are almost indistinguishable, each of which is known for its honesty. This and this man lied, and knowledge of this might have occurred upon hearing the news of this and the news of that, seeing his face, and hearing His words, and the joy and light of honesty, and the darkness, blackness, and ugliness of lying.
It becomes clear from this that many people gain the necessary knowledge that this prophet is truthful, and this prophet is a liar in the same way. Before they saw something extraordinary.

Some theologians say: Unless it is unusual, the Prophet has no jurisdiction over it, so it does not indicate anything. It is said to him: The term “breaking the custom” is a general term, and specifying the claim of prophecy as truth or false is not a customary matter, and this did not happen. Except in the case of individuals from the world, and it is much less than informing about the unseen, for this is more present than the claim of prophecy, as Every prophet tells of unseen things, but not everyone who tells of them is a prophet, and of those who say this, most of them or many say so. Among them:

The claim of prophecy, challenge, and miracle is all related to the Prophet. Otherwise, they say: Whatever was a miracle of a Prophet is permissible. To appear at the hands of a guardian or a magician, but the only thing that separates them is challenge and lack of opposition. Among them are those who deny the violation of the custom that it appears at the hands of other than a prophet, and among them are those who do not differentiate between a saint and a magician except by the righteousness of this and the immorality of this. This, and among them are those who dismiss this in the Prophet, especially the Greek philosophers, for they are among the ignorant.

people about the matter of prophecy, since they did not take it from knowledge of the truthfulness of the prophets, and of the signs, proofs, and knowledge they brought. By their attributes, but they took it from the analogy of dreams, so they interpreted it as what is permissible for a sleeper of dreams and imagination, and what befalls The people of the Black Marra are similar to that.

This is what is found in most of Aristotle’s followers, but their later followers, such as Ibn Sina, added to that his behavior in the world when he reached Of their actual miracles, which those people did not know, as Aristotle’s knowledge was what his people from Greece knew, and they A nation of the children of Japheth. There were none among them, such as the children of Shem, such as Jews, Saleh, and others, then the children of Abraham, the friend whom God had promised him. To instill in his descendants prophecy and the Book so that the knowledge of prophecy will be famous among them. God Almighty made from the time of Hebron in His descendants are prophecy and the Book, as he told about that in the Qur’an, and they were not of his descendants, nor were they knowledgeable about the circumstances of His descendants, and a group of them, such as Muhammad bin Yusuf Al-Amiri and Sa’id bin Sa’id Al-Andalusi, mentioned that their masters were five.

Then four Epenodocelus, then Pythagoras, then Socrates, then Plato, came to the Levant, and benefited from the Children of Israel, and for this reason there were no These are the ones who said that the world is ancient, unlike Aristotle. They said:

He did not come to the Levant, and these people, such as Muhammad bin Yusuf Al-Amiri and others, mentioned that the first person to be named with wisdom was Luqman, and that Ibn Diocletus benefited from it, and he was a follower of David, peace be upon him - because he was in the time of David, and if this is what these theorists say, And the people of theology and philosophy. For them, the mere violation of custom does not alone necessitate prophecy, such that it alone is evidence. Rather, it is necessary To join that challenge and not oppose.

For this reason, when a group of them, such as Abu Al-Hasan and his followers, disagreed: Is it permissible for the supernatural to appear at the hands of a liar? It was said: It is not permissible because it is the science of prophecy, so its meaning cannot differ from it, like all other evidence. And it was said: It is permissible, but God does not He does it. Then it was said: Because it entails his inability to believe the Messenger, since there is no way to him except the miraculous according to them, and it was said: Rather, it is possible. It is possible, but we necessarily know that He does not do it, as much of what is normally possible, and we know that God does not do it, and all Who combined the two sayings and said:

The totality of what indicates prophecy, and it is the supernatural one who is free from opposition and prevents it from being for anyone other than a prophet other than the supernatural type, so it was said to him: This abstention is either normal, or it is due to the inability to believe the Prophet, and this is abstainable, so if it is Abstained due to his inability to believe the Prophet, and that is abstained. Uncontrollable

As a rule, you do not have an objection, so you must give that answer, which is to say that we must know that this did not happen, and then if You knew that this is necessary knowledge, and that knowledge of its significance of truthfulness is a necessary matter, like the example you gave about the king sending a messenger. And His Messenger said: If you are truthful, then change your habit of standing and then sitting. He did that after asking the Messenger, for that necessitates knowledge. It is necessary for the truthfulness of the Messenger.

And it was said to you: You know the king’s habits, and it is known that he did that to make you believe, and to you the Lord did not create anything for the sake of it. So you said: Rather, He creates something comparable to something like ordinary things, and this is one of them. So you were told: Habits have been repeated. So you said: We may know that without repetition, and you made that a matter of positive significance, like the expression’s indication of the speaker’s intention, and you said: It may We know what he meant by necessity without prior explanation, and these are the necessary knowledge that you mentioned by which the truthfulness of the Messenger is known, even if it is Indeed, the majority of people say:

You did not acknowledge its implications of the fact that he was doing it for such and such, and they say: the statement that he created the miracle with the intention of making it believable with To say that He does not create anything for the sake of anything is a contradiction. So you said: It is not a condition of necessary knowledge to know that one does such and such for such and such a reason. So it was said
For you: Suppose it is so, but the necessary knowledge is not obtained with knowledge of what contradicts it.

What is meant is that what these theorists and like them, and even the general public, mention, is in what they prove of knowledge and facts. Information is more powerful than they are and more correct in what they deny, for a person is more knowledgeable about what he proves than what he denies, and his testimony is Proof is stronger than his testimony to denial, and even if the denial may be known, people are more likely to err in what they deny and deny. Because of their error in what they prove and believe in, and for this reason God Almighty said: {Rather, they denied that of which they did not comprehend the knowledge and when its interpretation had come to them} [Yunus: 39]

For this reason, you find someone who followed one of the paths, either in establishing knowledge of the Maker, or in knowledge of prophecy, or knowledge of the Resurrection, or something else. That is, someone who says: There is no path except this path, makes more mistakes in denying than in affirming, and among them are these people, for they may They deny knowledge and methods that which others know by necessity, and confirm what they say is known by necessity, and it may be others. He is more correct in what he confirms than they are in what they deny, and even in what they confirm.

For this reason, those who agreed that there is no path other than miracles differed regarding their significance, so these people established a method by which they used it as evidence. They deny the path of others, and vice versa. If they say anything other than that which is contrary to the norm, it is not specific to the Prophet, so it does not indicate his prophecy. They were told:

Evidence is that which is necessary for the signified, and its verification requires the verification of the signified. The word “unusual” has a general meaning, as previously mentioned. At that time, God’s very news to the Prophet, his selection of him for his message, and his ability to receive it from the king are among the supernatural customs, and that One of the miracles that God made His creation incapable of performing, and He is specific to the prophets, and this description is more exalted and greater in value than any other. Of the supernatural, and what is necessary for this supernatural thing can only be supernatural, and it is the proof, as it is necessary for the confirmation of what is necessary to be proven, and from The absence of the necessary is the absence of the necessary, and the usual thing that exists without prophecy is not evidence.

As for what does not exist unless prophecy exists, it is evidence. It has become clear that everything that indicates the truthfulness of the Messenger, and is extraordinary, is a sign. And a prophecy of its truth, and as for what is unusual and does not require prophecy, it is not evidence, and the thing may be usual without Prophecy, and with prophecy there is a violation of custom, such that his presence with prophecy is a violation of custom, unlike his presence devoid of it, because Prophecy is a violation of custom, so only one who breaks the custom can be obligated to it.

So the speaker’s statement: The truth of it is not known except by a miracle, and it is beyond the ordinary, if he meant by it the general meaning, which is what it entails. His sincerity is invalid. He singled that out with the verses that He created separately from it, even if He meant by that a specific type, with everyone participating in it. The significance of his denial has become apparent.

As for what exists without it as well as what exists with it, such as the matters that happen to the truthful person claiming to be prophetic, and the liar claiming to be prophetic, then these are not It indicates, and the types of things that God reveals at the hand of the Prophet by which his truthfulness is known, there is nothing in them that would be for a liar.

Rather, the liar has no evidence except what requires his lying. Everything that indicates the liar’s lie does not indicate the truthfulness of the truthful person. On the contrary, the evidence of a lie requires it, and the evidence of the truth requires it, and they are two opposites that prevent a claimant of prophethood from being a prophet. A truthful person, and a false prophet. The two opposites do not go together, so it is impossible for one thing to indicate two opposites. This rule is useful in Places: including:

When many people see a liar and hear his words, it becomes clear to them that he is lying, sometimes with necessary knowledge, and sometimes with inferential knowledge. Sometimes with a strong suspicion, and likewise the truthful prophet, if they see him and hear his words, his truthfulness becomes clear to them through necessary or theoretical knowledge, and he has It occurs first with a strong suspicion, then the suspicion strengthens until it becomes certain, as in the sciences, with repeated reports and experiments. If the first It indicates a kind of suspicion, then it is strengthened by the second and third news until it becomes certain.

This path was taken by groups of people, and among those who alerted to this was Judge Iyadh. Judge Iyadh said: If the fair-minded person considers what we have presented... Beautiful is his impact, praiseworthy is his conduct, the prowess of his knowledge, the wisdom of his mind, his dream, the sum of his perfection, and all his qualities, and witness His condition, and the correctness of his statement, he did not hesitate in the validity of his prophecy, and the truthfulness of his call. He said: “This was sufficient for more than one person in his Islam and faith.” It was narrated to us on the authority of Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Qani’, and others with their chains of transmission that Abdullah bin Salam said:
When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, I came to him to look at him, and when I saw his face

I knew that his face was not the face of a liar. It was narrated by more than one person, such as Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi, Muhammad ibn Ja`far, Ibn Abi Adi, and Yahya ibn Sa`id on the authority of Awf ibn Abi Jamila The Bedouins, on the authority of Zurara bin Awfa, on the authority of Abdullah bin Salam. On the authority of Abu Rimthah Al-Balawi, he said: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and with me was a son of mine, so I showed him, and when I saw him, I said: This is the Prophet of God.

Muslim narrated in his Sahih, and others, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that a bandage came before Mecca, and it was of the worst kind, and it was a ruqyah from this wind. Then he heard fools from the people of Mecca saying: Muhammad is crazy. He said: If I had seen this man, perhaps God would heal him at my hands. He said: He met him and said: O Muhammad, I am performing ruqyah from this wind, and God heals at the hands of whomever God wills, so do you? Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Indeed, praise be to God, we praise Him, and we seek His help. Whoever God guides, none can mislead him, and whoever He leads astray, none can guide him. And I bear witness that there is no god but God is alone, He has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. Now then. He said: Repeat these words to me. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, repeated them three times. He said: He said: I have heard the priests say, the magicians say, and the poets say, but I have never heard these words like yours, and they have reached the dictionary The sea. Give me your hand and I will pledge allegiance to you on Islam. So he pledged allegiance to him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said:
And upon your people. He said: And upon my people. . . . » Hadith.

Jami` bin Shaddad said: There was a man among us called Tariq, and he reported that he “saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina and said: Are you with you?” Something you sell? We said: This camel. He said: How much? We said: With such-and-such, an wasq of dates. So he took his reins and walked to the city. We said: We sold a man, we do not know who he is, and we have a woman with us. She said: I am a guarantor for the price. The camel, I saw the face of a man like the moon on a full moon night, who did not despise you. In the morning, a man brought dates and said:
I am the Messenger of God, the Messenger of God to you. He commands you to eat of these dates and measure them until you are satisfied, so we did.”

And in the news of Al-Julandi, Malik Ghassan, when the Messenger of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed him of them inviting him to Islam, so Al-Julandi said: By God He pointed out to me this illiterate Prophet that he does not command good unless he is the first to take it, and does not forbid evil unless he is the first to abandon it. And he is victorious and does not become irritated, and he is defeated and does not become weary, and he fulfills his covenant and fulfills what is promised, and I bear witness that he is a prophet.
Naftawayh said in the Almighty’s saying: “Her oil would almost shine even if no fire touched it” [An-Nur: 35].

It is an example that God presented to His Prophet. He says: His appearance almost indicates his prophethood, even if he did not recite the Qur’an, as Ibn Rawaha said: If There were no clear verses in it... His intuition was informing you of the news. I said:

The faith of Khadija, Abu Bakr, and other early predecessors was before the splitting of the moon, before he was informed of the unseen, and before He challenged him with the Qur’an, but it was after they had heard the Qur’an, which itself is a necessary sign for his truthfulness, and the same words he said and told him. That I am the Messenger of God, despite what is known about his conditions, requires his truthfulness, as well as other signs and proofs of truthfulness.
Rather, Khadija said to him: No, by God, God will never disgrace you, for you are upholding ties of kinship, truthful in hadith, tolerant of all, and hospitable to guests.
She helps the needy, and helps in the calamities of the truth, as she was aware of his conditions, which required denying his lies, immorality, and manipulation. Satan with it.

Abu Bakr was one of the wisest people, the last of them, and he was venerated among the Quraysh for his knowledge, benevolence, and mind. When his situation became clear to him, He knew with essential knowledge that he was a true prophet, and he was the most complete of the people on earth in certainty and knowledge, and likewise Heraclius, the king of the Christians, when he was sent To him the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, invited him to Islam. He asked about ten characteristics, as in the two Sahih books on the authority of Ibn Abbas. He said: Abu told me Sufyan bin Harb from Fih to Fi, he said: I set out during the period that was between me and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said:

While we were in the Levant, a letter was brought from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Heraclius. He said: Dihiyah al-Kalbi had brought it and he pushed him away. To the great of Busra, and the great of Busra sent him to Heraclius, and Heraclius said:

Is there anyone here among the people of this man who claims to be a prophet? They said: Yes. He said: So I summoned a group of Quraysh and we entered upon Heraclius, and we sat in front of him. He said: Which of you is closer in lineage to this man who He claims to be a prophet?

Abu Sufyan said: So I said: I am. So they made me sit in front of him, and they made my companions sit behind me. He called for his interpreter and said: Tell them: I am asking this about this man who claims He is a prophet, so if he denies me, then they will deny him.
He said: Abu Sufyan said: By God, had it not been for fear that the lie would influence me, I would have lied to him.
Then he said to his interpreter: Ask him how he ranks among you?
He said: I said: He is worthy of reckoning among us.
He said: Were any of his fathers a king?
I said: No.
He said: Were you accusing him of lying before he said what he said?
I said: No.
He said: And who followed him? The most noble people or the weak ones?
I said: Rather, their weak ones.
He said: Will they increase or decrease?
I said: No, but they increase. He said: Does any of them abandon his religion after he entered it, out of displeasure with him?
He said: I said: No. He said: Did you fight him?
I said: Yes. He said: How was your fight with him?
He said: I said: The war between us and him will be a dispute, and he will suffer from us and we will suffer from him.
He said: Does he betray?
I said: No, and we have been with him for a while and we do not know what he is doing. He said: By God, I am not able to say anything in it other than this. He said: Has anyone said this before him?

He said: I said: No. He said to his translator: Tell him: I asked you about his lineage, and you claimed that there is one of lineage among you, and so are the messengers sent with a lineage. Her people, and I asked you: Were any of his forefathers a king? You claimed not, so I said: If one of his fathers had been a king, I said: A man seeking his father’s kingdom, and I asked you about his followers: Were they weak or Their nobles? So you said: Rather, they are weak, and they are the followers of the Messengers, and I asked you: Were you accusing him of lying before he said what he said? So you claimed no, because I knew that he would not stop lying to people and then go and lie to God, and I asked you:

Will any of them abandon his religion after entering into it out of displeasure with him? So you claimed that no, so is faith when it mixes with the multitude of hearts, and I ask you: Will they increase or decrease? So you claimed that they would increase, and so does faith until it is complete, and I asked you: Did you fight him? So you claimed that you had fought him, so the war would be a dispute between you and him, and he would attack you and you would attack him, and likewise the messengers are tested and then have The outcome, and I asked you: Does he betray? So you claimed that he does not deceive, and likewise the messengers do not deceive, and I asked you: Has anyone said this before him? You claimed no, so I said:
If someone had said this before him, I would have said: A man who followed a statement that was said before him.
Then he said: What does he command you?
I said: He commands us to pray, to pay zakat, to maintain ties, and to be chaste.

He said: If what you say about him is true, he is a prophet, and I knew that he was coming, and I did not think he was one of you, even if I knew that I would be sincere. To him I would love to meet him, and if I were with him I would wash his feet, and let them reach his kingdom what is under my feet. Then he called for the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he read it, and lo, in it was:

“In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, from Muhammad, the Messenger of God, to Heraclius, the Great of Rome, peace be upon whoever follows guidance. As for what follows, I invite you With the call to Islam, submit and you will be safe, and submit and God will reward you twice, and if you turn back, then upon you is the sin of the Arisians, and:

{Say, O People of the Book, come to a common word between us and you: that we shall worship none but Allah, and not associate anything with Him, and not take lords other than Allah. But if they turn away, then say, “Bear witness that we submit.” [Al Imran: 64]

And in a narration: What does he command you to do? He said: He commands us to worship God alone, and not to associate anything with Him, and he forbids us from what our fathers used to worship, and he commands us to pray, Charity, chastity, fulfillment of covenants, and performance of trusts. He said: This is the characteristic of a prophet.

What the Christian king Heraclius used as evidence of knowledge and its characteristics is evidence of his own nature, for people are in degrees of prophecy: some of them are He needs to know the type of prophecy, so he believes in the type of human messengers. He does not disbelieve in the type, as he denied that among the people who lied. Noah, Ad, Thamud, and others, and for this reason God Almighty says: {You have denied the people of Noah the messengers} [Al-Shu’ara’: 105]
{Ad has denied the messengers} [Al-Shu'ara': 123]
{Thamud denied the messengers} [Al-Shu'ara: 141]

Because their denial was not to one person, but rather they were denying the race of messengers, and God addresses these people in the Meccan surahs, as He said: God Almighty: {And they did not estimate God according to His value when they said, “God has not sent down to human beings anything.” Say, “Who sent down the Book which Moses brought as light and guidance?” for the people} [Al-An’am: 91]

So he used the revelation of the Book of Moses as evidence due to the striking verses that had been reported repeatedly in his experience indicating its truthfulness, and the Gospel follows the Torah. Then he said: {And this is a Book which We have sent down, blessed, confirming what is before it} [Al-An’am: 92]

Because of the verses indicating his descent, and for this reason, Glory be to Him, He mentions in the Meccan surahs confirming the command of the messengers and their verses, And their proofs, and their good outcome, and from the misguidance of their opponents, and their ignorance, and their wrongdoing, and their abandonment, and their bad outcome is what is in it. A lesson.

62] (62) {Those are those whom God knows what is in their hearts, so turn away from them and admonish them, and speak to them within themselves an eloquent word} [An-Nisa: 63] God has informed that He has appointed for the prophets those who would be hostile to them from mankind and jinn, and God Almighty said:

114] (114) {And the word of your Lord has been completed in truth and justice. And those who have something that contradicts some of what the messengers were told are three types: the imaginative people, the philosophical atheists. And the Batiniyya are those who say: The messengers reported about the matter of belief in God and the Last Day something that contradicts the truth about the same matter in order to make them imagine. To the public what they benefit from, and they consider this one of the virtues of the messengers, and the response to these people has been explained in more than one place.

And the people of distortion and interpretation: those who interpret their words in a way that contradicts what they intended, and they claim that they intended that meaning even though it is not There is nothing in their words that indicates the desire for that meaning, but rather their words indicate the desire for the opposite.

And the people of ignorance: those who say that speech has no meaning that the Messenger or anyone else knows, but God alone knows, and these two The two opinions say that each of them had sects that glorified the messengers, and their corruption has been made clear elsewhere.

As for those who say: The messengers and others know the meaning that God made clear to them with His words, but God took advantage of knowing another matter that He does not They know it just as it is influenced by the knowledge of the unseen of the Hour. This is the saying of the Salaf and the Imams, and this has been explained in another place.

What is meant here is that the talk about prophecies is sometimes about their type, and sometimes about the person of the specific prophet, and Heraclius, the Roman king, did not need Belief in the type of prophecy, because he was one of the People of the Book, and the People of the Book acknowledge the type of prophecy, as they acknowledge the prophecy of Noah. Hebron, Moses, the prophets of the children of Israel, and the Christians nevertheless acknowledge Christ and the Gospel.
There are two types of people who need to know the specific Prophet:

They knew that a prophet would be sent, and they might know some of his characteristics, so they would need to know his exact essence. And Heraclius and others like him were among the people of The writers were of this type, and they knew that a prophet would be sent, but their need was to know whether he was this prophet. The one mentioned or something else, so what they need of evidence of his truthfulness is easier than what is needed by those who do not believe in messengers or do not know that he is a prophet. He will be sent, and whoever knows the type of messengers, and does not know whether a prophet will be sent or not, needs to know that this particular person is of the type True prophets or false prophets, and this is known by the signs of his truthfulness, and considering what he brought. The prophets before him, for the origins of that are matters about which it is not possible for the prophets to differ, and they are the matters that do not accept abrogation, such as narration. About God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, this is one of the things about which it is not possible for the prophets to differ, since everything that The Prophet tells it, so it is truthful, and true news does not contradict or be abrogated, but some prophets may be more knowledgeable than others. What Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, told us is more complete and more complete than what Moses and the Messiah, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them, told us.

People disagreed about something like this: Is it possible to abrogate it and change the laws based on it? On two opinions: Whoever allows God to command everything and forbid everything refers that to pure will and not to attributes that require The matter is this rather than this, for they allowed the inclusion of abrogations in this, and the diversity of the laws in it, as Jahm bin Safwan says, Al-Ash’ari, and those of Malik, Al-Shafi’i, and Ahmad who agreed with him, even though they say that there was no abrogation of it.

As for the majority of people, from the predecessors and successors, they do not permit the inclusion of abrogations in this, nor the diversity of the laws in it, and for this reason the religion of The prophets are one, as God Almighty said: {O you messengers, eat of the good things and do righteousness. Indeed, I am All-Knowing of what you do} [Al-Mu’minun: 51] (51) {And indeed This is your nation, one nation, and I am your Lord, so fear Me.” [Al-Mu’minun: 52]

And God Almighty said: {He has legislated for you of the religion that which He enjoined upon Noah, and which We have revealed to you, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus, that you should establish the religion and not You will be dispersed therein. Hard for the polytheists is that to which you are calling them.} [Al-Shura: 13]

And God Almighty said: {So set your face upright toward the religion, upright. It is the nature of God which He created mankind. There is no altering of God’s creation. That is the right religion, but Most people do not know.” [Al-Rum: 30]
And in the two Sahih books on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “We, the Prophets, have one religion.”
